item.title: COSMIC Epoch 1.12.0: what actually changed since 1.11.0
item.description: System76 tagged Epoch 1.12.0 on November 24 with an empty release body. The real changes are in the submodule commits: theme bundles, a pointer size setting, Xwayland controls, and a batch of a11y and security fixes.
item.content:encoded:
As of November 25 2026, COSMIC Epoch 1.12.0 is tagged and stable. Jeremy Soller created the annotated tag on November 24, roughly a month after 1.11.0 on October 20. There was no separate feature freeze announcement: an epoch is a coordinated bump of every submodule, and this one moves 28 of them. The GitHub release body contains only the tag message, “Epoch 1.12.0”, so the list below comes from the merged commits in the range rather than from official notes. What is still open is packaging: the tag is upstream, and distro packages will pick it up on their own schedule.

Things worth your attention

Theming: bundles, dark and light wallpapers, fades

This is the biggest user-facing area in 1.12.0. COSMIC Settings can now save a look as a self-contained theme bundle, import one, rename it, and keep several side by side (cosmic-settings, theme-bundle-config). The strings you will see are “Save as…”, “Save theme as”, “Rename theme”, and “Legacy theme file”. A bad import says “select a .zip bundle or .ron theme file”. Bundles write to /usr/share-style config and data roots with an x-cosmic-format metainfo marker, and the import path accepts old ThemeBuilder .ron files, so earlier custom themes are not stranded. Frosted glass is enabled by default in this cycle.

Backgrounds gained per-mode entries, so dark and light mode can use different wallpapers (cosmic-bg, cosmic-bg commit d6dcfa9). Switching between them fades over 500 ms by default through wp-alpha-modifier-v1 and subsurfaces; the config key is transition_duration, in milliseconds (cosmic-bg commit 203159b). The default wallpaper is now system76-cosmic-dark.png (cosmic-bg commit 803047f), also used as the greeter fallback (cosmic-bg commit 2439903). Several modules switched from the old JPEG XL decoder to jxl-rs, including cosmic-bg, cosmic-files, cosmic-greeter, and cosmic-settings.

Who it affects: anyone who customizes COSMIC themes, and theme authors who shipped .ron files. The bundle format is new, so expect a migration edge or two in the first packages.

Pointer size, end to end

COSMIC Settings has a “Pointer size” slider in Accessibility (cosmic-settings, cosmic-settings commit aaf58b4). It steps through 24, 32, 48, 64, and 96 logical pixels. On the compositor side, cursor_size is a new cosmic-comp config key that falls back to $XCURSOR_SIZE (cosmic-comp commit 0681eaf); changing it at runtime reloads every seat and the Xwayland cursor without a restart. cosmic-settings-daemon mirrors the value to GTK via org.gnome.desktop.interface cursor-size, which matters because GTK apps draw their own cursor (cosmic-settings-daemon commit ff28489).

Who it affects: HiDPI users, people with motor impairments, and anyone who found the old fixed cursor too small on a large monitor. This completes a loop that previously only worked through environment variables.

Compositor defaults and Xwayland controls

Mutter-style server-side decorations are now the COSMIC default. The new decoration_preference key sets DecorationPreference::ServerSide, and Settings exposes it as “Use system window headers when possible” with the note “Applications may use their own window headers in some cases” (cosmic-comp cosmic-comp commit 63dacd1, cosmic-settings cosmic-settings commit 5f43cfc). Touchpads default to natural scrolling (cosmic-comp commit 88a3421).

Xwayland can be disabled outright with COSMIC_DISABLE_XWAYLAND=1 (cosmic-comp commit ed9a71c). Font smoothing for Xwayland apps was added: the compositor now writes Xft/Antialias=1, Xft/Hinting=1, Xft/HintStyle=hintslight, and Xft/RGBA=none (cosmic-comp commit 8129317). cosmic-comp also retries opening GPU nodes at startup (cosmic-comp commit 0a67a6c), picks the highest refresh rate when a mode reports none (cosmic-comp commit 8e0b615), and resets GAMMA_LUT during CRTC init (cosmic-comp commit cb86b9e).

Who it affects: multi-monitor and hybrid-GPU setups, users who want a Wayland-only session, and anyone whose X11 apps looked rough on HiDPI. The environment variable is opt-in, not a default change.

Urgent notifications over fullscreen windows

cosmic-notifications gained a FullscreenBehavior setting with three values: None (the default, notifications stay behind fullscreen windows), UrgentOnly, and All (cosmic-notifications commit 2137773). The implementation keeps a second overlay layer surface and decides per notification which one to use. Critical alerts can now break through a fullscreen game or presentation, but only if you ask for it.

Who it affects: users who miss critical notifications during fullscreen work, and kiosk or signage setups where popping up over fullscreen would be unwanted.

App launching and GPU choice

Four modules now launch apps as .service units with XDG cgroup names: cosmic-app-library (cosmic-app-library commit e4c3d73), cosmic-applets (cosmic-applets commit 582281f), cosmic-launcher (cosmic-launcher commit 81647dd), and cosmic-store (cosmic-store commit 63e7650). cosmic-app-library also fixes daemonized apps such as Zed closing when the launcher exits (cosmic-app-library commit 096f348). GPU preference handling was corrected in three places: the default discrete GPU is retained and a preference override is no longer set when the ID already is the default (cosmic-launcher commit eb74145, cosmic-launcher commit 3c52515, cosmic-store commit bb24819).

Who it affects: hybrid-GPU laptop owners and anyone whose terminal-launched apps vanish on exit. Grouping apps into their own cgroups also makes per-app resource limits possible for distro integrators.

Updates pages on Pop!_OS

cosmic-settings gained a Pop!_OS-only OS updates page built on pop-system-updater-zbus (cosmic-settings commit 4d515f2). It offers Daily, Weekly, and Monthly schedules with AM/PM and weekday fields, visible in i18n/en/cosmic_settings.ftl. cosmic-initial-setup gained an automatic updates page using the same bindings (cosmic-initial-setup commit 282c01a), and the old update notification toggle was deliberately removed (cosmic-initial-setup commit 973f17c).

Who it affects: Pop!_OS users going through first-run setup or changing update policy. The removed toggle is intentional, so any workflow that depended on it needs the new schedule controls instead.

Lock screen and greeter hardening

The greeter hides the password prompt while you are typing a username (cosmic-greeter commit b7b59d4). The locker now rate-limits PAM retries to at least 500 ms per attempt (cosmic-greeter commit 84a04d3, PAM_MIN_ATTEMPT_DURATION). Bluetooth agent code answers authorize_service with the paired state (cosmic-applets commit 6f89bfa, cosmic-settings commit 057e2e7).

Who it affects: everyone at login, and more specifically anyone who mistypes a username on the first try or leaves a Bluetooth device paired but untrusted.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • cosmic-comp removed internal mutexes and atomics from CosmicStackInternal, CosmicWindowInternal, and ContextMenu (cosmic-comp commit e10d1f9, cosmic-comp commit 73217f3, cosmic-comp commit 2f577fa); the Wayland connection buffer was enlarged (cosmic-comp commit 9b4296b).
  • cosmic-comp-ipc is a new crate for passing session environment variables over a Unix socket using JSON messages (cosmic-comp commit f2beba6); cosmic-session now uses it (cosmic-session commit efc36fc).
  • cosmic-files syncs copies in batches so large transfers do not exhaust open file descriptors (cosmic-files commit a7164ac, cosmic-files commit 84a32e1), reuses descriptors for batch sync (cosmic-files commit e03001c), and syncs copies before deleting sources (cosmic-files commit 3868a8e).
  • cosmic-files falls back to gio copy when reads from gvfs FUSE paths fail (cosmic-files commit 3204c6a) and keeps serving FileManager1 after the zbus 6 upgrade (cosmic-files commit 70f33d9).
  • cosmic-panel restarts applets killed by a signal and cleans up the client of one that exited (cosmic-panel commit 160a951, cosmic-panel commit 45340f5).
  • cosmic-store refreshes AppStream data for system Flatpak remotes (cosmic-store commit 8846658); cosmic-term displays every monospace font on the system (cosmic-term commit b209f70).
  • The whole stack moved to zbus 6 (cosmic-comp cosmic-comp commit 46b26e6, cosmic-session cosmic-session commit 3fe5d42, cosmic-settings-daemon cosmic-settings-daemon commit e3040f1, and others). cosmic-comp raised its MSRV to 1.95 (cosmic-comp commit 4d79aa0).

Visual polish

  • Panel border radius and padding now derive from the theme instead of fixed overrides (cosmic-panel commit 71c49f4). An unset override shows as “None” in the default schemas. The default dock size changed too (cosmic-panel commit add4154).
  • cosmic-files shows mounted drives in the move/copy-to dialog (cosmic-files commit 9e4d406) and image and video thumbnails in Trash (cosmic-files commit 8475dfd).
  • The audio applet no longer stretches album art and truncates long track titles at 32 characters with ContentFit::Contain (cosmic-applets commit dc252e3).
  • cosmic-edit uses the selected text as the new find value (cosmic-edit commit a741508) and fixes the highlight rectangle drawn at X position 0 while horizontally scrolled (cosmic-edit commit 9d19fd9).
  • cosmic-comp fixes title truncation to respect character boundaries (cosmic-comp commit 683ae8b) and replaces paragraph separators in window titles (cosmic-comp commit 59d98e5).
  • cosmic-settings tracks natural scrolling in the touchpad panel (cosmic-settings commit af9416c) and adds font and icon selection improvements in Appearance (cosmic-settings commit 74185d1).

Developer tools

  • cosmic-settings has a CLI path straight to the keyboard settings: keyboard shortcuts and keyboard shortcuts custom subcommands (cosmic-settings commit 5793cbb).
  • cosmic-osk gained a CI workflow for format, lint, and test (cosmic-osk commit 3dfc0b0).
  • The Nix flake builds with Rust 1.95 (cosmic-comp commit e716e74); the epoch version-update.sh script was updated (epoch commit 16883d0, cosmic-app-library commit c19e73e).
  • cosmic-session only imports SSH_AUTH_SOCK when it is actually set (cosmic-session commit 1de865b).

Content and smaller apps

cosmic-player, cosmic-randr, cosmic-screenshot, cosmic-viewer, cosmic-monitor, and cosmic-workspaces-epoch are version bumps plus translation updates in this epoch. cosmic-viewer has no functional commits beyond the version update and one Weblate batch (cosmic-viewer commit 57b134c, cosmic-viewer commit df2d02b, cosmic-viewer commit 067c4fd). pop-launcher moved to zbus 6 and updated dependencies (pop-launcher commit df5151e, pop-launcher commit 4111617).

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, input

  • Pointer motion uses the new position in PointerMotion, and is_legal uses the correct position (cosmic-comp commit 14513fa, cosmic-comp commit b9bd128).
  • Mismatched output groups are filtered (cosmic-comp commit de9a66d), submenus are not placed inside a tile when their parent is outside (cosmic-comp commit cfd6a50), and tiling no longer panics when focusing with an empty focus stack (cosmic-comp commit 6e29ee6).
  • Toplevel info updates when window geometry changes (cosmic-comp commit bb74e8a); saved sizes that no longer fit a group are not restored (cosmic-comp commit 66524a0).
  • Focus is repaired when there is no target but a session lock is active (cosmic-comp commit ec674cd); seats send wl_surface.enter and leave to client cursor surfaces (cosmic-comp commit 9cde272).
  • Output manager done events are scoped per output (cosmic-comp commit 2c30140), surface threads are joined on device_changed (cosmic-comp commit eeca8b0), and the compositor no longer sleeps its Wayland thread with an event queued (xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic commit 2d70101).
  • Screen sharing rejects a request with no selected source (xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic commit 67624f8) and avoids a double-response panic (xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic commit 3dbe884).

Login and sessions

  • Greeter hides the password field while a username is typed; locker rate-limits bad PAM attempts as described above.
  • cosmic-settings-daemon restores audio controls after PipeWire restarts (cosmic-settings-daemon commit a8d9d84) and fixes Bluetooth headset control on Ubuntu 26.04 (cosmic-settings-daemon commit 212f39a). It no longer divides by zero when no keyboard layout is set (cosmic-settings-daemon commit 108e095).
  • cosmic-initial-setup no longer panics when changing scale with no display loaded (cosmic-initial-setup commit 27b79e7).
  • Cosmic Settings re-registers the Bluetooth agent when bluetoothd restarts (cosmic-settings commit e82cbc4) and keeps the active audio device when the one before it is removed (cosmic-settings commit aaaf4e0).

Apps

  • App-list actions no longer do nothing when an item is selected (cosmic-applets commit ef6c9e6), and the applets no longer abort or wait forever on Wayland errors (cosmic-applets commit ecb6b61) or when the workspace manager disappears (cosmic-applets commit cb3ea91).
  • VPN state stays in the scrollable area (cosmic-applets commit 779f920); the panel redraws when an applet’s window goes away (cosmic-panel commit cc0bdb3).
  • cosmic-store remembers scroll position when opening app details (cosmic-store commit 18ba81b) and resets it on page switches (cosmic-store commit 5b9bbed).
  • File operations write every chunk in full (cosmic-files commit 76823cb), propagate sync errors (cosmic-files commit 3d3e70b), skip cleanup only when appropriate (cosmic-files commit 84ffd15), and do not follow a symlink given as the copy root (cosmic-files commit 8166f67).
  • cosmic-term no longer pastes while the search or context drawer is open (cosmic-term commit b0ab376, cosmic-term commit a5e1bb5).
  • cosmic-settings preserves interface and base state across bundle changes (cosmic-settings commit f8816b0), caps theme names (cosmic-settings commit b8a3b6c), truncates bundle titles at 40 characters (cosmic-settings commit b2db1bf), shows the current wallpaper on inactive theme cards (cosmic-settings commit 6aaf30d), and fixes a search navbar panic (cosmic-settings commit ee6ea8a).

Security

  • cosmic-files bumps zip-rs to 9.x (cosmic-files commit 4efe802).
  • The lock screen enforces the 500 ms PAM attempt floor, which limits rapid-fire guessing.
  • Screen sharing requires an explicit source selection and handles a duplicate dialog response safely.

Libraries and build

  • jxl-rs replaces the previous JPEG XL path in several apps; the pipeline uses PipeWire from crates.io in the portal (xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic commit 7b0864c) and jiff 1.0 (xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic commit ce75265).
  • cosmic-settings applies theme reset settings to packaged defaults (cosmic-settings commit b7920db) and no longer pins a cosmic-protocols revision (cosmic-settings commit b68d89d).
  • Debian packaging for cosmic-settings and initial setup builds with the pop-os feature (cosmic-settings commit 4d515f2, cosmic-initial-setup commit 282c01a).

Known regressions and deferred work

The release body is empty, so this post is reconstructed from commits and may miss packaging-only changes. The update notification toggle was removed on purpose, not deferred. Theme bundles are new in this epoch and are the most likely place for migration rough edges. There is no published list of known regressions for the tag yet.

Sources

The annotated epoch tag is epoch-1.12.0, created November 24 2026, and the full change set is the comparison epoch-1.11.0…epoch-1.12.0. Feature details come from the merged commits in the submodules, including the theme bundle work in cosmic-settings, per-mode wallpapers in cosmic-bg, the configurable cursor size in cosmic-comp, and the urgent notification option in cosmic-notifications. System76 announced Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS on the same day, which covers the broader COSMIC work this epoch packages. Phoronix’s most recent COSMIC release article is still Epoch 1.11 at the time of writing.

item.title: Debian 13.8: what actually changed
item.description: The eighth trixie point release landed on November 21, 2026. It folds in a large batch of security fixes, a GRUB Secure Boot fix, fresh Intel microcode, glibc corrections, and an installer kernel bump. Here is the concrete list.
item.content:encoded:
Debian 13.8 is a stable point release, the eighth update of trixie, published on November 21, 2026. It is not a new version of Debian 13 and there is no feature freeze involved. The release adds corrections for security issues plus fixes for a set of serious problems. Security advisories went out separately and are referenced in the announcement. Old 13.x media still installs, then upgrades to current packages through any up-to-date mirror. There is a lot here: 122 source packages in the miscellaneous bugfix table and well over a hundred DSAs rolled into the stable set. Most of the DSA packages will already be current on machines that follow security.debian.org.

Things worth your attention

Boot, firmware and the C library

Change Where Who it affects
GRUB: Secure Boot bypass (CVE-2026-97876), use-after-free denials of service (CVE-2025-54770, CVE-2025-54771, CVE-2025-61661 to CVE-2025-61664), SBAT revision bump, riscv64 crash fix grub2 and the amd64, arm64, ia32 signed EFI builds Anyone booting with UEFI Secure Boot. The signed packages and grub2 all get the same fix, and the SBAT bump matters for dual-boot setups with shim.
glibc: buffer over-reads (CVE-2026-6238, CVE-2026-97399), out-of-bounds writes (CVE-2026-5435, CVE-2026-19542), stack overflows (CVE-2026-6791, CVE-2026-89092, CVE-2026-95818), buffer overflows (CVE-2026-19499, CVE-2026-18374), UTF-32 decode hangs (CVE-2026-77117, CVE-2026-80489), a wordexp WRDE_APPEND state fix (CVE-2026-6368) and a race condition (CVE-2026-86805) glibc Everyone. On Intel CPUs, ld.so now caches cpuid results, which is a small startup-path change worth watching if you run unusual CPUID-overriding tools.
New upstream microcode with twelve CVEs, among them CVE-2024-24853 and CVE-2026-20917 intel-microcode Intel CPU owners. This is a firmware-level fix delivered as a package, so a reboot is needed before it takes effect.
New upstream stable release openssl Anything doing TLS. No CVE is named for this one in the announcement; it arrives folded in with the earlier DSA-6531.

The glibc entry also changes zic so TZif files keep a needed last transition to a new type. That is a data-format detail, but it is the kind of change that quietly breaks hand-rolled timezone tooling.

Time zones and the calendar

tzdata gets a substantial data update. Cuba moves to permanent daylight saving time, which means no more twice-yearly clock changes there. Manitoba and the Northwest Territories get updated rules, Ireland, Iran, Colombia, Brazil and Ukraine get historical corrections, and the upstream signing key is rotated. Anyone with recurring meetings across those zones will want the update. The Perl side follows with libdatetime-timezone-perl moving to Olson DB 2026f and the same Manitoba data.

Databases and server software

mariadb moves to a new upstream stable release with a long security list: code execution fixes (CVE-2026-44168, CVE-2026-48163, CVE-2026-48165), an authorization bypass (CVE-2026-44169), path traversal (CVE-2026-44171), SQL injection (CVE-2026-44172), an incomplete privilege check (CVE-2026-44173), and six further CVEs. It also clears two concrete errors users hit: “Illegal mix of collations”, and Mroonga hanging on an invalid index flag, plus a crash in information_schema.table_constraints and a regression with temporal result columns. Database admins should treat this as more than a routine bump.

The OpenStack stack gets a broad set of authorization and injection fixes. glance stops unrestricted image downloads and blocks access to internal services through image imports and HTTP image locations (CVE-2026-71196, CVE-2026-71197, CVE-2026-71198), prevents DNS rebinding during downloads and enforces URI filtering for legacy import tasks (CVE-2026-77648). nova strips internal scheduler hints on server creation (CVE-2026-46448) and stops WebSocket Origin allow-list poisoning. octavia fixes cross-tenant QoS authorization (CVE-2026-74248) and HAProxy configuration injection through redirect URLs and TLS cipher settings (CVE-2026-94571, CVE-2026-94572). aodh, manila, gnocchi, watcher, zaqar and ironic-python-agent carry related fixes. postgresql-17 arrives through DSA-6625.

sssd fixes a use-after-free (CVE-2026-12610), a privilege escalation (CVE-2025-11561), path traversal (CVE-2026-14476), information disclosure (CVE-2026-68744) and two denial-of-service issues. It also warns when ldap_sudo_search_base falls back to the root DN (CVE-2026-14474). This one matters most on machines bound to LDAP or FreeIPA.

Browser and desktop stack

kwin fixes Wayland colour management handling and a null output dereference when unplugging monitors. If you run KDE on Wayland and regularly hot-plug displays, that second fix is the one that stops a crash. chromium accumulates a long run of DSAs from DSA-6408 through DSA-6605, and firefox-esr gets DSA-6501, DSA-6560 and DSA-6573.

Thunderbird 153 compatibility gets a small cluster of fixes: allow-html-temp, mailmindr and xnote are all updated to keep working with that version. Lomiri gets a reworked scaling path instead of Qt-native HiDPI handling: lomiri-session now applies a scaling factor from GSettings, and lomiri-schemas provides the new upstream way of defining it. Lomiri terminal and telephony components get use-after-free and systemd service fixes alongside it.

Smaller changes

Rebuilds and toolchain

A sizeable slice of the 122 packages are rebuilds with no functional change of their own. Rust rebuilds cover atuin, bankstown-lv2, bpftop, btm, cyme and dwarf2sources. docker.io rebuilds cover cosign, crowdsec and distrobuilder, while dar is rebuilt against openssl, zsh against pcre2, and user-mode-linux against the updated kernel. cosign and crowdsec follow the docker.io rebuild; distrobuilder follows both docker.io and incus. llvm-toolchain-22 fixes its armel build.

Networking and system utilities

bird2 and bird3 both fix FlowSpec decoder bounds and validation, authentication key handling and BGP timer calculations. bird3 additionally fixes route display, hostentry stripping, log rotation, RCU journal synchronisation and allocator prefill. proftpd-dfsg fixes a remote denial of service in TLS handling, a denial of service (CVE-2026-119146), an authorization bypass (CVE-2026-119147) and a link-following issue (CVE-2026-119364). sudo blocks TZ variable poisoning (CVE-2026-96512). parted fixes two heap buffer overflows (CVE-2026-89088, CVE-2026-89095), and patch prevents creation of out-of-tree files (CVE-2026-115207). rsync blocks unauthenticated resource exhaustion (CVE-2026-119741), neovim fixes filename command injection (CVE-2026-11487), and nghttp2 fixes HTTP request and response smuggling (CVE-2026-58055). composer gets path traversal and command injection fixes plus sanitising of URL-embedded usernames and tokens in verbose output.

brltty now times out quickly on localhost connections and fixes IPv6 localhost connections. efivar adds SetVariable runtime support. dhcpcd fixes occasional corruption of its NTP server list. wireless-regdb updates regulatory data, and mdadm fixes a memory leak.

Installer and media

debian-installer bumps the Linux ABI to 6.12.117+deb13 and is rebuilt for the point release. debian-installer-netboot-images is rebuilt against proposed-updates. Debian says new installation images will be available soon at the regular locations, so the ISO you download today may still be the older build even though the packages it installs are current.

Bug fixes

Compositor, display and input

kwin: Wayland colour management handling and the monitor-unplug null dereference described above. btrfs-assistant no longer clobbers the user xdg-runtime-dir when running under Wayland. xorg-server and gst-plugins-base1.0 arrive with fixes through DSA-6497 and DSA-6489. brltty’s localhost timeouts and IPv6 fix are also in this area.

Login and sessions

sssd and sudo carry the fixes listed above. lomiri-session, lomiri-telephony-service and lomiri-terminal-app fix systemd user services, a use-after-free and a settings-dialog refocus bug. network-manager-l2tp and network-manager-iodine arrive through DSA-6498 and DSA-6629.

Apps

mariadb, chromium, firefox-esr, thunderbird extension helpers, neovim, vim (DSA-6600), libreoffice (DSA-6512, DSA-6543, DSA-6615), roundcube, wordpress and tor all receive fixes. xiphos fixes a code execution issue (CVE-2026-79079). tone-generator fixes generation of call progress and DTMF tones. spice-vdagent fixes a heap buffer overflow (CVE-2026-57965) and path traversal (CVE-2026-57966).

Security

The DSA tables run from DSA-6408 (chromium) to DSA-6629 (network-manager-iodine), with multiple advisories for chromium, firefox-esr, linux, tor, apache2, nginx, bind9, php8.4, libreoffice, openssl, vim, curl, xz-utils and apt. apt itself is DSA-6607. The complete DSA-to-package mapping is in the announcement, linked below. Many of these were already available individually before 13.8; the point release pulls them into the installable stable set.

Libraries and build

glibc, openssl, freetype (CVE-2026-95512), pygments (CVE-2026-4539), zlib (DSA-6613), expat (DSA-6566), libpng1.6 (DSA-6537), libheif (DSA-6524, DSA-6583) and nss (DSA-6599) get fixes. The Perl stack is busy: libdbi-perl, libnet-dns-perl, libtemplate-perl, libtie-hash-regex-perl, libwww-perl, libxml-bare-perl and libyaml-perl all fix security issues, with libwww-perl stripping the Authorization header on cross-origin redirects (CVE-2026-8368) and refusing insecure downgrades by default. mongo-c-driver, libmongocrypt and qpid-proton carry large CVE batches of their own.

Known regressions and deferred work

There are no 13.8-specific errata entries. The trixie errata page still lists one historical known problem from 13.0: netboot installer packages such as debian-installer-13-netboot-amd64 were initially missing and were meant to be corrected through trixie-updates. The release planning page still shows 13.8 with a January 2027 date, which disagrees with the announcement, the release page and the errata page; all three of those put the release on November 21, 2026. Treat the planning entry as stale.

Sources

Official announcement on the debian-announce list and the matching debian.org News page. The full package-to-change mapping is in the trixie ChangeLog, and the point-release history plus known problems are on the trixie errata page. Individual advisories are indexed on the Debian security tracker.

item.title: Flatpak 1.19.4: what actually changed
item.description: A beta development prerelease with two security fixes, COSMIC applet desktop keys, and new search filters. It also absorbs the withdrawn 1.19.3 tag, so this is the first usable release of that batch.
item.content:encoded:
Flatpak 1.19.4 shipped on November 24 as a beta development prerelease from the 1.19.x branch. No feature freeze date has been announced. Flatpak publishes odd-numbered series as a rolling set of point releases, and the maintainers state that the first stable release from this branch will be 1.20.0, with stable OS releases staying on 1.18.x until then. This tag also absorbs the work from 1.19.3, whose release process failed, so the notes cover everything accumulated since 1.19.2.

The headline is security. Two advisories went out with this tag: a critical local privilege escalation in the system helper and a full sandbox escape through the portal. Alongside those are command line and sandbox fixes plus desktop integration work for COSMIC. What is still open is the 1.20.0 stable tag and the stable-series backports that distributions will pick up on their own schedule.

Things worth your attention

Two security fixes in the system helper and portal

CVE-2026-133842 is rated critical. If an app, runtime or extension installed system-wide uses the extra-data mechanism and its apply_extra program creates a deeply nested directory hierarchy, Flatpak can leave a setuid-root executable under /var/lib/flatpak with its setuid bit intact. A malicious local user working with such an app can turn that into root privilege escalation. The fix makes permission canonicalization fail closed when it cannot open a directory (Flatpak commit d087606) or when readdir() fails (Flatpak commit a21a102). Reported by RoyalOughtness, fixed by Simon McVittie. By default only root-equivalent users can install apps system-wide, which limits exposure, but any setup that relaxes the polkit rules for Flatpak is at risk.

CVE-2026-133845 is rated high and affects anyone running a malicious or compromised Flatpak app. If the third argument to the portal’s Spawn() call maps two file descriptors to the same handle, dup2() fails. That failure was not handled, so a descriptor open inside flatpak-portal ended up in the subsandbox. Predicting the number of the unfiltered D-Bus session bus descriptor is enough to escape the sandbox completely. The immediate mitigation exits the child process when fd mapping fails (Flatpak commit f107d8a). The thorough fix adds a FlatpakUniqueFDList so one descriptor cannot be used twice (Flatpak commit b1b596e, Flatpak commit a7b55f8, with Flatpak commit 07b007e renaming the old variables). Reported by refi64 and independently rediscovered by oz9un, with fixes from refi64 and Simon McVittie.

Both are fixed in the stable 1.18.6 release as well. The advisories note that the 1.19.3 and 1.18.5 tags contained the fixes but their release process failed, so 1.19.4 and 1.18.6 are the tags to use. Backports exist on the flatpak-1.16.x branch for distributions such as Debian 13, though upstream will not publish a formal release from it.

The command line loses a flag and gains search filters

flatpak update --force-remove is gone (Flatpak issue 6915). It had no effect, so the only visible change is that scripts still passing it now get an error. That is the incompatible command line change in this release.

flatpak search gains --app and --runtime (Flatpak issue 6718, implemented in Flatpak issue 6902), matching filters flatpak list already had. So flatpak search --app game looks only at applications, and flatpak search --runtime org.gnome limits results to runtimes. Searches with many matches are faster too (Flatpak issue 6892).

COSMIC applets can export their desktop keys

PR Flatpak PR 6865 adds five COSMIC keys to the allowlist Flatpak applies to exported .desktop files. Without this, those fields were stripped from sandboxed apps. The keys and what they do:

  • X-CosmicApplet marks an applet for the settings app and the panel.
  • X-CosmicHoverPopup asks for a popup on hover when another applet already has one open.
  • X-CosmicOverflowPriority sets the priority of an applet in panel overflow behavior.
  • X-CosmicOverflowMinSize sets the minimum size of a shrinkable applet in applet size units.
  • X-CosmicShrinkable marks a window whose panel padding can shrink so it takes less space.

Who it affects: COSMIC users and anyone packaging a COSMIC applet as a Flatpak. The pull request carried a needs-backport label, and the stable-series backport was still open as Flatpak issue 6936 at release time.

Fonts and sandbox restrictions

Both ~/.local/share/fonts and the legacy ~/.fonts are available inside the sandbox when both exist (Flatpak issue 5675, Flatpak issue 6869). Previously an app could not see font files placed in the older path. Apps started with --no-session-bus or --no-a11y-bus now pass the same restriction to the subsandboxes they create (Flatpak issue 6968), closing a gap where a child sandbox regained bus access its parent had given up.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • Time-remaining estimates during install are more accurate (Flatpak issue 6732).
  • Truncated and dropped HTTP downloads are retried (Flatpak issue 6881), so a flaky connection is less likely to fail an install.
  • flatpak enter picks the smallest process ID when matching by name (Flatpak issue 6878), which is more likely to be the main instance.
  • flatpak uninstall --unused avoids removing pinned runtimes and extensions (Flatpak issue 6859).
  • GPU-rendered terminal emulators no longer flicker (Flatpak issue 6959).

Visual polish and output

  • App IDs are no longer ellipsized by default (Flatpak issue 4719), and AppStream summaries fold onto one line (Flatpak issue 6132), which makes long output easier to read.
  • Agreement titles are no longer shown as though they were the app’s name (Flatpak issue 6965).

Developer tools and documentation

  • Command line completion is improved (Flatpak issue 6759) and faster (Flatpak issue 6325).
  • API documentation received a round of fixes (Flatpak issue 6890, Flatpak issue 6914, Flatpak issue 6912, Flatpak issue 6963).
  • flatpak override precedence is documented (Flatpak issue 6478), as is flatpak build --readonly (Flatpak issue 6966) and how to clear a remote subset filter (Flatpak issue 5637).

Translations

Translation updates shipped for pl, pt_BR, sl and zh_CN.

Bug fixes

Sandbox and portal

  • OCI repositories no longer report up-to-date refs as having updates available (Flatpak issue 6874).
  • The missing SpawnStarted signal from the portal when SPAWN_NOTIFY is used is restored (Flatpak issue 6864).
  • GIO warnings while accessing the system repository are gone (Flatpak issue 6413, Flatpak issue 6766).
  • Unusual WAYLAND_DISPLAY values are handled (Flatpak issue 6970).
  • flatpak install --or-update and --reinstall are no longer ignored when used with .flatpakref files (Flatpak issue 5460).
  • Propagation of the gpg-verify option is fixed so a .flatpakrepo file can disable GPG verification (Flatpak issue 6934).
  • Trailing slashes in --persist paths are ignored, so the persistent directory mounts where intended (Flatpak issue 1469).
  • flatpak-coredumpctl returns early if the selected process is not a Flatpak app (Flatpak issue 6975).

Command line and remotes

  • flatpak remote-ls works with a non-default --arch (Flatpak issue 3805).
  • An assertion failure in flatpak remote-info when optional metadata is missing is fixed (Flatpak issue 6945).
  • flatpak search no longer crashes on AppStream components with no name (Flatpak issue 6958).
  • flatpak run no longer crashes when the GPG agent socket cannot be found (Flatpak issue 6969).
  • Apps missing from native sideload repository listings are back (Flatpak issue 6939).
  • flatpak update --no-pull no longer pulls updated AppStream metadata (Flatpak issue 5163).
  • The default branch for an app in a specific installation is no longer affected by the default branch in another installation, and a runtime shell uses the copy from the selected installation (Flatpak issue 6917).

Libraries and build

  • Memory leak fixes (Flatpak issue 6863, Flatpak issue 6930).
  • Some tests now pass when bubblewrap is unavailable, and a test race condition is removed (Flatpak issue 6963).
  • Test coverage and internal test infrastructure improved (Flatpak issue 6931, Flatpak issue 6932, Flatpak issue 6938, Flatpak issue 6919, Flatpak issue 6980).

Still in flight

Flatpak publishes the 1.19 series as rolling development prereleases and has not announced a feature freeze date, so there is no formal list of proposed features waiting for a later 1.19.x tag. Everything in the 1.19.4 notes is merged and published; there is no hidden batch of finished work behind this tag. Two things are genuinely still open. The first stable release from this branch, 1.20.0, has not been tagged. The COSMIC desktop key change carries a needs-backport label, and its stable-series backport was still open in Flatpak issue 6936, so 1.18.x users will not get it in 1.18.6. Anything else that lands before 1.20.0 will arrive in a later point release, and I would not assume any particular feature will make it.

Known regressions and deferred work

None listed yet. The 1.19.3 tag carried the same fixes but its release process failed, so anyone who picked up that tag directly should move to 1.19.4. The advisory for CVE-2026-133842 notes that exploit attempts can leave behind a directory under /var/lib/flatpak/app/ containing a setuid executable. After the fix the files/extra subdirectory is locked down so non-root users cannot reach it, but that leftover directory is not cleaned up. Debian 13 users on the 1.16.x branch get backports of both fixes but no formal upstream release.

Sources

Official release notes on GitHub: Flatpak 1.19.4, with the withdrawn 1.19.3 carrying the same text. The security advisories are CVE-2026-133842 / GHSA-p4mw-6jfq-r82r and CVE-2026-133845 / GHSA-5jrj-948r-2wx6. The COSMIC keys came in #6865 and its open stable backport is #6936. Search filters were requested in #6718 and implemented in #6902. The co-released stable point release 1.18.6 carries the same two security fixes for the stable series.

item.title: Cinnamon 6.8.4: what actually changed
item.description: A small stable point release from November 20 that fixes modal dialogs closing too early, workspace switches that never finished, and a lock screen that showed the default avatar. It also brings a round of translation regeneration.
item.content:encoded:
Cinnamon 6.8.4 is a stable point release, tagged and published on November 20, 2026. There is no feature freeze to talk about here: the 6.8.0 feature work landed on November 4, and 6.8.1 through 6.8.4 are a run of small fix releases inside two weeks. The GitHub release entry carries no notes text, so the authoritative record is the Debian changelog and the tagged diff. This covers all five code changes in 6.8.4.

Things worth your attention

Modal dialogs no longer close on a held modifier

If you opened the run dialog, Expo or the overview with a Super based shortcut, releasing Super closed the modal straight away. The dialog only stayed open while you held the key, which made combos like Super+space useless inside it. The fix came from Cinnamon issue 14150 and landed as Cinnamon commit ccfea90.

The stage event handler now records a modifier as “tapped” only when it was pressed while the modal was up and no other key was pressed before its release. A click, touch or scroll cancels the tap. A modifier you were already holding when the modal opened, such as the one from the shortcut that launched it, is never recorded, so letting go of it does nothing. The same tap test is used by the run dialog, Expo and the workspace view when they decide whether to close. This also feeds modifier only keybindings, so a bare Super press can be bound without it firing on the release of a shortcut. Keyboard users and anyone relying on Super based launchers are the ones who notice.

Workspace switches finish when a window closes mid slide

Dániel Ruszki fixed a stuck workspace animation in Cinnamon issue 14153, closing Cinnamon issue 14134. If you closed a window while the switch slide was running, Cinnamon never called completed_switch_workspace(). Muffin kept switch_workspace_in_progress at 1, and while it was non zero it skipped plugin effects and deferred hiding windows. From that point every minimized window stayed painted on screen until the next workspace switch or a Cinnamon restart.

The two slide animations now use onStopped instead of onComplete, so an interrupted transition still removes its actor from the pending sets. Actors are removed before cleanup, which makes re entry through remove_all_transitions() harmless, and a complete() helper disconnects the kill handler and calls completed_switch_workspace() exactly once. The author reproduced it on X11 with animations on, and reported the minimize behaviour back to normal at 0, 50 and 100 ms delays. This matters most on X11 sessions with animations enabled.

Smaller changes

Visual polish

The lock screen no longer draws your picture when it is the default avatar. If you never set an account photo, the generic silhouette is now hidden instead of shown on the unlock dialog, while a real photo still appears as before. The user widget is re centered each time the screensaver runs, because the widget is kept around rather than rebuilt and has to react to an avatar change. The same hiding rule was applied to the menu applet and the user applet popup menu, but not the panel icon.

Under the hood the unlock dialog gets a hideDefaultImage flag, and the avatar widget uses it to decide whether the image is visible. The screen shield wraps the dialog in a bin layout container and centers that container within the monitor space, taking the on screen keyboard height into account.

Developer tools and localization

The translation generation script had a path bug. generate_cs_module_desktop_files.py imported config.py straight from the source tree even though that file is now a configured one, so it read the wrong copy. It now uses the installed file. Running the generation scripts refreshed roughly 36 .desktop files, which is why a five commit release touches 48 files with close to a thousand added lines.

The visible result is new translated names, comments and search keywords. The virtual keyboard gains names such as “Teclado virtual” in Galician, “Виртуалды пернетақта” in Kazakh and “Виртуал гар” in Mongolian, plus matching translated keywords. The screenshot app’s desktop file picked up the largest batch, around 175 new lines of translated names and comments, so “Take a Screenshot of an Area” now has translations in many more languages. Accessibility settings gained keywords like “лупа;сөйлеу;қол жеткізу” in Kazakh. This is translation content only, with no change to how the apps behave.

Bug fixes

Compositor, display and input

The modifier tap work also fixes Expo and the overview closing when you release Super after using a Super based shortcut. Both now call isModifierTap() before hiding themselves. Clicks, touch events and scrolls clear a pending tap, so the release of a modifier after a scroll no longer counts.

Login and sessions

The unlock dialog is centered through a bin layout sized to the monitor and the available height, which handles the on screen keyboard case more cleanly than the old preferred size calculation. The user image is hidden when it is the default, and the widget is re centered on each use of the screensaver.

Libraries and build

The i18n script now reads the installed config.py instead of the source copy, and the generated .desktop files were refreshed. The meson project version moves from 6.8.3 to 6.8.4. No library APIs changed in this release.

Known regressions and deferred work

None listed yet. The default avatar hiding applies to the screensaver, the menu applet and the user applet popup, but the panel icon was deliberately left alone. The translation refresh changes strings and keywords across the desktop files only.

Sources

The authoritative change list is the 6.8.4 Debian changelog, with the full 6.8.3 to 6.8.4 diff and the tagged source tree. The modal dialog fix is discussed in #14150 and landed in commit ccfea90. The workspace switch fix is #14153, which closes #14134. The screensaver, avatar and i18n details come from the tagged diff of userWidget.js and screenShield.js.

item.title: KDE Plasma 6.8.3: what actually changed since 6.8.2
item.description: The third stable 6.8 update repairs multi-GPU workarounds, screencast frame pacing, and a suspend delay. Desktop focus, panel cloning, screenshots, and everyday widgets also get fixes.
item.content:encoded:
Plasma 6.8.3 is a stable bugfix release, published on November 10, 2026. It follows 6.8.2 with two weeks of fixes and translations, not another feature-development milestone. The broader changes from our 6.8 beta report are already part of the released series. KDE has published the announcement and source archives; distribution packages may follow later.

Things worth your attention

Graphics and the compositor

KWin repairs both NVIDIA and AMD workarounds in MultiGpuSwapchain. The NVIDIA condition was inverted, so the intended exclusion of a problematic Vulkan copy path was wrong (KDE bug 527163, 9c944a4). On AMD, the selected linear buffer modifier was overwritten immediately afterward; that assignment is now kept (KDE bug 521716, 7d296e8). These matter when rendering and display output involve different GPUs. They are repairs to existing workarounds, not a new rendering backend or a general performance claim.

Frame pacing gets a separate correction. KWin now advances Wayland FIFO and commit timing through one relevant scene view rather than every view for an output (b145d8b, KDE bug 498628, KDE bug 525619). Mirroring and screencasting can create multiple views of the same output; advancing through all of them could double the FIFO frame rate or cause commit-timing stutter. The render loop also fixes scheduling with triple buffering and commit timing (c7a6bdc). These are specific scheduling fixes, not measured frame-rate gains.

KWin corrects the linear segment of its inverse sRGB transfer function (KDE bug 528375, 232eff1). The low-luminance branch now multiplies the normalized value by 12.92 instead of dividing it. This concerns color conversion near black, not newly added HDR support. The DRM backend also clears damage tracking for non-shadow-buffer swapchains and overrides a buffer modifier with INVALID where required, both linked to KDE bug 527421.

Suspend, brightness, and display defaults

KWin ignores requests to wake displays once the system is committed to sleeping (KDE bug 528221, 5b0a41d). Previously, input arriving while the screens were turning off could cancel that transition but leave the sleep-delay inhibitor active. The result was a visible lock screen and a wait for logind’s timeout before suspend. Input can wake the displays again after resume. This is particularly relevant if a last mouse movement made closing down for sleep feel unreliable.

Powerdevil fixes screens remaining dimmed after brightness control is lost (KDE bug 523988). The Battery Monitor limits its charge-limit hint to the system battery (KDE bug 448020, KDE bug 497345), rather than applying the hint indiscriminately to other batteries.

Default scaling now distinguishes tablets and handhelds from phones (91857c5, KWin MR 10345). KWin’s added test expects a 1.5 scale for the Legion Go S at 1920 × 1080. This changes automatic scale selection, not a promise to replace everyone’s saved settings. Automatic mode selection also avoids interlaced modes when the preferred mode is progressive (KDE bug 527502).

Recording and remote desktop

KWin smooths the cursor image written into PipeWire screencast metadata (KDE bug 528423, e553ba0). People sharing or recording their screen should no longer get the jagged cursor caused by that scaling path. The KDE desktop portal fixes duplicate virtual-output names (9516674).

Spectacle initializes final image data when the captured images have the same scale and calculates the combined image size more accurately (ad648f3, fa4b068). These are screenshot assembly fixes, especially relevant to combined captures. It also skips QR-code scanning in background mode.

KRDP explicitly disables RDSTLS, which it does not implement, instead of relying on FreeRDP’s default (8fe3696, KRDP MR 287). That is one RDP negotiation mode. The patch retains the existing TLS and NLA selection according to the authentication path; it does not turn off encrypted remote desktop generally.

Shell, panels, and desktop files

Plasma Desktop fixes a panel hang when layout spacing is zero (KDE bug 528228). Plasma Workspace assigns a cloned panel to the screen it was cloned to (KDE bug 527445). Those are useful corrections for people arranging panels across several displays.

Desktop clicks now give the desktop focus (KDE bug 434090), and Show Desktop manually restores focus for minimized windows (KDE bug 450137). Scrolling the Pager no longer triggers Show Desktop (KDE bug 471241). Adding a launcher to the desktop targets the current Activity (KDE bug 520511), while launching through shortcuts no longer hits the reported segmentation fault (KDE bug 527810).

Folder View removes invalid or nonexistent files from its positioner (KDE bug 469445), fixes press-position resets when its model resets (KDE bug 526073), and handles drag images better during very fast drags (KDE bug 527529). Widgets no longer offer unsupported manual sorting (KDE bug 513880) and can shrink to a single cell (KDE bug 515561). The desktop’s “Create New” menu now shows Ctrl+Shift+N beside “Folder…” (KDE bug 473045, e8ddeed). The shortcut already worked; the menu finally tells you about it.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • The image wallpaper loader stops launching overlapping loads during rapid screen-size changes. It lets the current request finish, then checks whether the latest options need another load (64fd6b7). This fixes a race that could replace the chosen wallpaper with the default during repeated rotations or resizes.
  • libksysguard cancels its ReadPids runnable if the corresponding cgroup is destroyed (KDE bug 502879), relevant to process monitoring while groups disappear.
  • KWin deletes the forwarding input devices belonging to OffscreenQuickView (c2e5658).
  • Union raises its cache allowance and skips cache updates for pixel metrics, linked to KDE bug 527409. This is internal widget-style work, not a published benchmark.

Visual polish

Oxygen restores a missing outline for borderless decorations, adjusts neutral and negative text colors (KDE bug 528121), and fixes lines in menus under fractional scaling (KDE bug 527745). Breeze’s Plasma desktop theme stops drawing a faint background on the active tab (881e157). Attached desktop tooltips inherit Plasma styling correctly with Qt 6.12 (KDE bug 527730).

Volume percentages and on-screen progress labels use tabular digits without overriding the font’s other default features. The brightness applet gets the same preservation fix. Kicker keeps its current list index while scrolling, Kickoff scrolls to the correct position, and Window List elides long titles instead of growing without limit (KDE bug 456148).

The Timer’s default notification stops forcing the English text “Timer finished” in every language (KDE bug 413374, a4b2681). Existing translated text is used when no custom message is set. Its preset configuration also shows seconds. The Digital Clock zero-pads hours when 24-hour display is forced in a 12-hour locale (KDE bug 517262), so an hour such as 9 appears as 09.

Developer tools and diagnostics

KWin adds an opt-in hang-detection thread (273d39d, KWin MR 10248, KDE bug 527622). A positive KWIN_HANG_DETECTION_TIMEOUT, in microseconds, enables periodic pings of the main thread. A missed response produces a warning and provides Application::onMainHang as a breakpoint target; recovery logs how long the thread was busy. This helps developers collect evidence about stalls. It is not an automatic recovery mechanism or an always-running watchdog.

KWin logs input devices during libinput setup and exposes left, top, right, and bottom properties on its internal Rect and RectF types. libkworkspace exposes session management to QML. Both libkscreen and plasma-workspace raise their plasma-wayland-protocols dependency to 1.23, which distribution builders need to account for.

Content and smaller apps

Plasma Addons updates the Astronomy Picture of the Day provider’s URL, corrects Picture of the Day context-menu icons, and fixes the tiled wallpaper’s default directory. Media Frame passes cached remote files as URLs (KDE bug 508225), uses a hover handler, and updates its icon immediately when a new image is selected. These repair existing content providers and widgets; there is no new wallpaper collection announced here.

Info Center’s energy graph shows the correct date and value (798f13f). Plasma Welcome fixes its KDE Connect AppStream link and Mac detection on the Meta-key page. Bigscreen reconnects its CEC adapter after libcec reports a lost connection and allows switching settings modules while the settings app is open (KDE bug 527030).

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, input

KWin ends an interactive move or resize without waiting for every mouse button to be released (6e1c799). Picture-in-picture windows preserve their resize anchors at screen edges (KDE bug 527641). Maximize guides work with floating-point geometry, and a typo in window-size adjustment is corrected (KDE bug 465124). The Zoom effect finds adjacent monitors correctly in Push mode.

The Screen Transform effect paints the entire snapshot instead of only a subset. Window-opacity changes emit the damage notification needed for repainting (KDE bug 502748). KWin handles a missing render device (KDE bug 527984), honors KWIN_DISABLE_UDMABUF_IMPORT even without a DRM device, and cancels touch sequences when displays turn off. Its Dim Screen effect recognizes pinentry-qt’s Wayland window class. Display Configuration avoids a zero preferred height for its panel view (KDE bug 527131), and the Touchscreen settings device selector gets its missing text role.

Login and sessions

The SDDM theme restores the Qt Virtual Keyboard fallback on X11 (KDE bug 527138). The lock-screen UI ignores empty authentication messages instead of bringing up its login interface (KDE bug 527262). kscreenlocker uses the view as the context for its frameSwapped connection (KDE bug 528438).

Plasma Workspace restores the Show Desktop state when leaving edit mode (KDE bug 502272). Bigscreen’s on-screen-keyboard toggle now changes KWin’s virtual-keyboard mode correctly. These are separate from the suspend-delay fix above.

Apps and widgets

Discover corrects keyboard-shortcut handling and settings indentation in right-to-left layouts. KRunner and Milou repair pseudo-Vim keyboard navigation (KDE bug 528257). Plasma Addons fixes keyboard use of the Calculator on the desktop, keyboard movement of Quicklaunch items between models, preset-timer keyboard navigation and reordering, the Color Picker’s circle border and middle-click preview, and Disk Quota hover highlighting.

The Audio Volume OSD appears only for the currently preferred output device (KDE bug 517055). The Digital Clock passes its current font only after the dialog exists (KDE bug 503333, KDE bug 511164). The calendar moves its selected date along with today at midnight (KDE bug 523827, KDE bug 518640) and stops interpreting years 0–99 as 1900–1999 (KDE bug 474972).

System Monitor closes its column-configuration dialog when pages change (KDE bug 523194). The Colors settings grid recalculates its sample text and cell height (KDE bug 528106), and the Wallpaper settings module guards against a null screen (KDE bug 528380). The global application menu loses a stray black pixel (KDE bug 524857). Desktop context menus open at the current item for keyboard menu requests (KDE bug 526282).

Security

The announcement and changelog do not identify a CVE fix. KRDP’s explicit RDSTLS disablement is the security-protocol correction described above; it should not be read as a switch to unencrypted RDP.

Libraries and build

libplasma avoids a crash on an invalid tooltip component, uses the parent’s screen for nested-containment geometry (KDE bug 525536), and reports shell-package load failures (12709e5). plasma-integration restores the color picker’s alpha channel (KDE bug 528396).

Union fixes checkbox alignment (KDE bug 528493), spinbox sizing and backgrounds (KDE bug 528280), combo-box text (KDE bug 527410), and mnemonic drawing (KDE bug 528236). It reserves menu-icon columns, corrects font metrics, improves header and element fallbacks, and respects palette text and background overrides (KDE bug 527260). Library-directory checks now require a directory rather than merely an existing path (KDE bug 528147).

Known regressions and deferred work

None listed yet. KDE’s announcement does not publish a new regression or deferred-feature list for 6.8.3. The issues above are fixes included in this release, not a claim that all outstanding 6.8 bugs are resolved.

Sources

KDE’s official Plasma 6.8.3 release announcement confirms the stable bugfix release and November 10 date. The complete module-by-module record is the 6.8.2 to 6.8.3 changelog, with archives and signatures on the 6.8.3 source information page. KDE’s commit explanations give the details behind NVIDIA buffer copying, the AMD modifier workaround, screencast and mirror timing, suspend-time display wakeups, handheld scaling, and RDSTLS negotiation. The hang-detector patch, wallpaper-loading fix, and Timer translation fix document the behavior described here.

item.title: Cinnamon 6.8.0: what actually changed
item.description: Cinnamon 6.8 brings finger-tracking gestures, per-monitor backgrounds and a Wayland session without the experimental label. The release also changes input methods, notifications and the lock screen, with limits worth checking before switching sessions.
item.content:encoded:
Cinnamon 6.8.0 has a stable upstream source tag, created on November 4, 2026. This covers the 6.7 development cycle as well as the final 6.8.0 changes, rather than just the last batch of commits. Distribution integration is a separate step: Linux Mint’s June preview placed the next Mint release at Christmas, so this tag is not an announcement that existing Mint installations have received the new desktop.

Worth your attention

Graphics and the Wayland session

The Wayland session no longer has “experimental” in its name. That change is in the tagged source (d4b411858a02), not just a plan in a monthly news post. Linux Mint says both X11 and Wayland will be supported; X11 has not been removed.

For people testing Wayland, the cycle includes HiDPI icon and image resource scaling, screenshots at physical monitor resolution, and capturing all monitors. The keyboard indicator also reacts to scale changes. These are desktop components and capture fixes, not a promise that every application will scale correctly. The Display panel still hides its fractional-scaling controls in Wayland sessions, which is an important limit behind the new session label.

The background system now has a dedicated daemon and per-monitor configuration (3f134e604a08). Backgrounds offers “Configure monitors individually”, “Use the same background on all monitors” and “Span a single background across all monitors”. People with two differently shaped displays can choose separate pictures rather than crop one image across both. The daemon watches image-file changes, respects embedded orientation and runs as a systemd user service when active. This is wallpaper handling, not a new wallpaper collection.

Gestures that follow your fingers

Workspace switching, Expo, Scale, the window switcher, tiling, maximizing and minimizing can now follow a swipe continuously, then commit or cancel when the fingers lift. The implementation uses a native gesture source on Wayland and Touchegg on X11. X11 users still need the Touchegg package and a running service; switching to the new desktop alone does not remove that dependency.

The Gestures panel includes “Easy Workspace Gestures” and “Easy Window Management Gestures” presets, sensitivity controls, and a marker explaining that selected gestures “can follow your fingers as they move”. Available actions depend on the input device and session type. Laptop users get the most obvious benefit, though the implementation also handles touchscreen gestures.

The work originated in #13992. That pull request is not marked merged by GitHub, but the implementation is present in the release through commit 21280f90440b, followed by fixes for canceled gestures, second swipes and Expo/window-switcher edge cases. This is included code, not a feature still waiting for review.

Shell, notifications and the lock screen

Per-application notification settings landed in #13598. The Notifications panel now has an “Application notifications” button, so people who need different rules for different apps are no longer limited to the desktop-wide switches.

The grouped window list can scroll when its buttons overflow (#13352), and overflowing thumbnail popups can scroll too (Cinnamon issue 14080). That matters on crowded panels, especially when a grouped application has many open windows. The traditional window list gains an “Always on top” context-menu action through #13351.

Cinnamon also includes a native screen locker, introduced in #13432, with a controller shared by locking and session-switching paths. Wayland requires the internal locker and ignores custom screensaver commands. X11 can use the internal locker, enabled by default in upstream settings, or retain an external-locker configuration. The cycle adds busy indicators while authentication is checked, prevents typing during that check, and tells logind about the locked state. Users and distro maintainers should check their session type and locker configuration rather than assume the same behavior everywhere.

Input methods and accessibility

Fcitx5 support reaches the input-method setup, Wayland session and virtual keyboard. The Wayland hookup is in 7274117c2349. Keyboard settings also gains a layout viewer instead of depending on gkbd-capplet (467c8d3e0340). People using IMEs, rather than a single XKB layout, are the audience for these changes.

IBus shows the newly selected layout at the text cursor, but only when an entry has focus. Cinnamon applies the engine’s layout variant and replaces an already running IBus daemon at login. These changes address the relationship between the visible layout indicator and the actual input method, rather than adding more keyboard layouts.

Accessibility work replaces the separate hover-click helper with a native palette, fixes magnifier pointer events on Wayland and disables magnification while the screensaver is active. The accessibility applet also gets a working Wayland keymap.

Storage, networking and desktop services

Pulling a removable drive out while it is still mounted now produces a persistent “Device removed unsafely” notification (#13899). Its text explains that pending writes can remain even when no file appears in use, and names “Safely Remove Drive” and “Eject” as the alternatives. Clean unmounts and ejects do not trigger this warning. It reports a mistake after it happens; it cannot recover the missing writes.

WireGuard and VPN-plugin connections share “VPN Connections” in the network applet (#13913). Rows show the connection kind, such as “WireGuard” or “OpenVPN”, instead of putting WireGuard in its own section. The final batch restores the VPN “More” overflow and removes the heading switch, so the original pull-request description is not a complete description of the finished menu.

For distro maintainers, the Secret portal preference now lists gnome-keyring;oo7-portal;, and pam_oo7 is an optional authentication module (#14062). GNOME Keyring is still first in that preference list. This is support for another provider, not evidence that Cinnamon has removed the existing one.

What left the desktop

The old cinnamon2d session definitions are gone (3ba28f61071c). Downstream references to those definitions need reviewing, but the cinnamon2d launcher itself remains available.

Cinnamon removes its OpenSearch provider (34dbda8778fe) and the grouped window list’s autostart toggle. Settings drops the “Looking for something else?” section. The older edge-flip feature was removed during the cycle (Cinnamon issue 13581); that removal is separate from the new swipe-driven workspace controls.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • Settings-file writes, bookmark loading, media-key proxy creation and power-profile provider lookup are asynchronous in the final batch. These remove synchronous work from desktop paths; upstream does not supply a release-wide startup benchmark.
  • The St toolkit avoids blurring a full widget-sized shadow where a smaller corner-sized silhouette can be stretched instead (#14046). Tall notification menus and HiDPI notification popups were the reported problem cases. The same change reorganizes the CPU blur loops. This is a targeted fix for stalls when shadows are built, not a general compositor frame-rate claim.
  • Spice rows load in batches when opening the Download tab. Xlet loading and versioned-xlet handling were also reworked (Cinnamon issue 13479).
  • Clearing notifications avoids redundant list updates (Cinnamon issue 13704). The notifications applet cancels timers and disconnects signals on removal instead of leaving callbacks behind.
  • The calendar backend moves to Clockenstein (Cinnamon issue 13972). Follow-up work keeps backend lifecycles consistent and avoids reporting out-of-range events as removed.

Visual polish

The sound applet expands output devices by default, keeps the input selector available after recording ends, and shows that selector when multiple inputs are connected (Cinnamon issue 13977). It also supports multiple applet instances (Cinnamon issue 14083), useful for panels on separate monitors.

The grouped window list keeps space between labels and button edges, gives unlabeled buttons equal widths, and shows the title when a pinned app opens a window. Its scrollbar takes space only when needed.

Removable-drive notifications and the drives applet use xsi-media-removable, the USB-stick symbol, rather than the old missing or less appropriate icon names (Cinnamon issue 13899). Other icon fallbacks stop assuming that the current theme is a Mint theme (Cinnamon issue 13995).

Polkit translates PAM messages through the authentication modules’ catalogs (Cinnamon issue 14064), while the password entry keeps the plain “Password” placeholder. Users see translated prompts without an arbitrary PAM message replacing that hint.

Developer tools and configuration

Looking Glass gains Muffin debug controls, scanout controls and an effects slow-down control. Its session type appears in the headerbar, the KMS debug flag goes to Wayland, and file watching uses Gio.FileMonitor instead of pyinotify (Cinnamon issue 13898).

Extension and effect authors get CinnamonGLSLEffect.get_pipeline() (Cinnamon issue 13939). Cinnamon adds GIRepository 2.0 support (Cinnamon issue 13474), while remaining global.screen use is removed from its own JavaScript and deprecated for callers. Several UI objects move to GObject or newer JavaScript class styles.

Power settings adds ambient-light-sensor support (Cinnamon issue 13649). Window settings adds focus-stealing prevention and a “Traditional” button-layout option (Cinnamon issue 13326). Availability still depends on the relevant hardware and session.

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, input

St buttons no longer depend on hover state to accept a click (Cinnamon issue 14048). Viewport and slicer changes fix pick clipping and stale paint volumes. On-screen keyboard positioning is corrected, and the startup pointer stays on the primary monitor.

The cycle fixes panel layout restoration after monitor hotplugging, fullscreen pointer grabs when raising panels on X11, and drag grabs left behind when a drag actor disappears. Alt+Shift+Tab is repaired (Cinnamon issue 13743). Keyboard-shortcut conflict checks now include actions with the same label (Cinnamon issue 14053).

Screenshot fixes cover clipboard output on Wayland, shadows around client- and server-decorated windows, canceled area selections (Cinnamon issue 13948) and a crash when capturing a server-decorated window without its frame. Scrollbars respect disabled animations.

Login and sessions

The desktop locks before switching to the greeter. Screen-lock teardown errors no longer block state updates, and the external-locker controller watches logind lock requests. Session startup fixes argument and environment handling and closes a leaked X connection.

Applets and settings

Network fixes cover removing one of several saved Wi-Fi profiles (Cinnamon issue 14073), updating access points with multiple profiles (Cinnamon issue 14075), duplicate rows after a network gains a profile (Cinnamon issue 14076), and WPA3/SAE and OWE classification (Cinnamon issue 14074). An unmanaged device providing connectivity no longer leaves the applet showing the offline icon (Cinnamon issue 13924).

Window-list fixes preserve ungrouped window order (Cinnamon issue 14089), refresh labels after workspace changes and avoid duplicate signal connections (Cinnamon issue 14055). Notification icons can resolve desktop-entry hints without a PID match (Cinnamon issue 14090), and a notification removed while appearing no longer gets a fresh timeout (Cinnamon issue 14079). Menu search discards results belonging to an older query (Cinnamon issue 14071).

Calendar events ending exactly at midnight no longer occupy another day. Settings avoids crashing on an unreadable user avatar (Cinnamon issue 14077), repairs HiDPI chooser thumbnails, and rebuilds an unparseable icon-theme cache. The sound applet no longer duplicates player open/quit buttons (Cinnamon issue 14060).

Security

cin-debug-run stops building a shell pipeline from the target program and generated GDB script. It invokes GDB with an argument list and passes the script through standard input instead (#14084). This removes that shell-interpolation path. The report describes a CWE-78 finding from static analysis and does not demonstrate a deployment exploit or establish that arbitrary debugger input is safe.

Libraries and build

Python code replaces pytz with datetime.timezone and zoneinfo. Packaging and imports receive cleanup, including a Cinnamon Settings module-name collision (Cinnamon issue 13492). Tray and XApp-status changes address icon lifecycle problems, redisplay races and misbehaving clients (Cinnamon issue 13965, Cinnamon issue 13966).

Known regressions and deferred work

The tagged Display settings module still exposes fractional-scaling controls only outside Wayland. Custom screensavers are disabled on Wayland, and some unsupported commands and menu options are hidden for that session. Removing “experimental” from the session name does not erase these differences.

The unsafe-removal warning relies on GVfs knowing about the mounts; unmount operations outside that knowledge are a documented limitation of Cinnamon issue 13899. Its author also notes that the per-device rate limit was not tested with a physically faulty connector and that a real multi-partition device was not tested. Those are coverage limits, not confirmed regressions.

Sources

Official Cinnamon source and release history: the 6.8.0 tag, its annotated tag metadata, and the tagged Debian changelog covering 6.7.x and 6.8.0. Linux Mint’s June 2026 monthly news explains the Wayland support policy and distinguishes desktop development from the upcoming Mint release. Implementation details are in the included gesture commit, per-monitor background change, notification settings pull request, shadow-rendering fix, unsafe-removal warning, and debug-helper security patch. Current session limits and portal ordering can be read directly in the tagged Display settings module and portal configuration. Locker selection is defined by the screensaver controller and the upstream settings defaults, while the remaining cinnamon2d launcher distinguishes the executable from the removed session definitions.

item.title: Fedora Linux 45: what actually changed
item.description: Fedora 45 went GA on November 3, 2026 after two postponements. It ships GNOME 51, KDE Plasma 6.8, Linux 7.2, and a long list of system-wide changes: kmscon as the VT console, enforced RPM signature checking, oo7 secret storage, Stratis in Anaconda, Podman 6, and more.
item.content:encoded:
Fedora Linux 45 reached general availability on November 3, 2026, after two NO-GO decisions pushed the original October 20 target back. It is a stable release: GNOME 51 on Workstation, KDE Plasma 6.8 on the KDE edition, Linux 7.2 underneath, and 46 approved changes in the ChangeSet. This post covers what actually shipped, not the beta promises.

Things worth your attention

Desktop: GNOME 51 and KDE Plasma 6.8

Fedora Workstation 45 ships GNOME 51, which brings reworked frame scheduling in Mutter for steadier frame rates under load, faster screen capture, better display management, and the oo7 secret service provider. Settings gained automatic screen rotation, remembered monitor brightness, and a touchpad-disable-when-mouse-connected option. Nautilus picked up a drag-and-drop counter badge, non-blocking directory reloads, and grouped notifications. Calendar’s view rendering was rebuilt for speed, and the file previewer (Sushi) was redesigned on GTK 4 and libadwaita. GNOME Maps can download maps for offline use.

The KDE Plasma Desktop edition ships Plasma 6.8.2, with per-screen virtual desktops, a system tray light/dark toggle, microphone testing, improved remote desktop with bidirectional clipboard and virtual display support, and the completed retirement of native X11 desktop sessions (X11 apps still run through XWayland).

Security: signature checking and ptrace restrictions

Two security defaults changed. RPM 6.1 now enforces signature verification by default: an unsigned package cannot be installed, dnf refuses it from a repository, and the local-file path warns. Separately, ptrace permissions for unprivileged users are restricted by default, so malware cannot inspect other processes belonging to the same user; full debugging returns when development tools are installed.

Secret storage: oo7 replaces GNOME Keyring

oo7, a modern Secrets Service implementation written in Rust, replaces GNOME Keyring (and KWallet) as the secret service provider on supported configurations. This is the same oo7 stack GNOME 51 adopted, now the Fedora default.

Console: kmscon replaces fbcon

The VT console moved from the in-kernel fbcon to the userspace kmscon. The new console gives improved Unicode and font rendering, better keyboard layout handling, and less console code running inside the kernel. The Cloud image does not enable the service, so the visible difference is on Server and Workstation.

Installer and storage: Stratis and Anaconda WebUI

Anaconda now supports installing Fedora on Stratis-managed storage, including manual configuration through the WebUI (with Cockpit Storage launched directly from the installer) and automated installs via Kickstart (--type=stratis, stratispool, stratisfs). Atomic Desktop variants (Silverblue, Kinoite, Sericea) moved from the legacy GTK-based Anaconda to the WebUI, and gained secure remote installation over HTTPS with PIN-based authentication. Atomic Desktop installation images are now built with image-builder, with extra qcow2 and raw image artifacts.

Toolchain and runtimes

GCC 16.2, binutils 2.47, glibc 2.44, gdb 17.2, LLVM 23, Go 1.27, Perl 5.44, Python 3.15, RPM 6.1, OpenSSL 4.0, Fontconfig 2.18. Also Pandas 3, Podman 6, Lua 5.5, and NodeJS metapackages (no single default stream anymore).

Repository configuration moved to /usr

The distribution’s own .repo files moved from /etc/yum.repos.d to /usr/share/dnf5/repos.d. Custom repositories still live in /etc/yum.repos.d and dnf still reads both.

Smaller changes

  • Removed legacy VPN plugins: NetworkManager-vpnc and NetworkManager-fortisslvpn are removed automatically during upgrades to Fedora 45. Affected users should migrate to supported alternatives such as OpenConnect or Libreswan.
  • CoreOS: enables systemd-oomd and zram swap by default for better memory management.
  • IBus 1.5.35 and the usual self-contained change set (MySQL 9.7, MariaDB 12.3, Ruby on Rails 8.1, Erlang 27, and others from the approved ChangeSet).
  • Kernel: Linux 7.2 with broad hardware support, improved laptop power management, and enhanced container performance.

Bug fixes

None published as a discrete batch for this release. Fedora tracks fixes through updates after GA; see the common issues thread on Ask Fedora for workarounds.

Known regressions and deferred work

  • No kmscon console on the Cloud image: the service is disabled on the Cloud variant by design; use Server or Workstation to see the console difference.
  • Local RPMs can still install unsigned packages: dnf install ./x.rpm only warns; rpm -i refuses. Use a repository with gpgcheck=1 when a hard block is needed.
  • Installer hangs with network --device=link: observed on Beta; using --device=<actual NIC name> works around it.

Sources

Official announcement: Announcing Fedora Linux 45. What’s New article on Fedora Magazine. Release notes at Fedora Docs for F45. Approved changes in the Fedora 45 ChangeSet. Third-party coverage from Linuxiac and the fedolinux community docs.

item.title: Arch Linux 2026.11.01: the November ISO in plain language
item.description: Monthly snapshot built around Linux 7.2.11, still carrying Archinstall 4.5, plus the PHP RCE and compromised-CA security fixes that landed in October. Existing systems need only pacman -Syu.
item.content:encoded:
Arch Linux’s monthly snapshot for November is out as 2026.11.01. As usual, the ISO itself only matters for fresh installs; existing systems get the same packages through pacman -Syu. The headline this month is a kernel bump to Linux 7.2.11, with the security work that landed in October riding along.

Things worth your attention

Kernel jump to 7.2.11

The kernel package was built for Arch on October 31, with matching headers and documentation. Last month’s ISO shipped 7.2.7, so this is a steady point release bump rather than a major promotion. Linux 7.2 itself was released around mid-August, and the 7.2.11 point release carries the accumulated stable fixes since then. The ISO is x86-64 only and weighs in at 1.2 GB, the leanest Arch disc in a while.

Archinstall 4.5 carries over

Archinstall 4.5, which arrived in the repositories near the end of September, is still the guided installer on this snapshot. It picked up RT kernel variants, AArch64 support for GRUB and Limine EFI, optdepends handling for the linux-firmware package, and a switch of polkit to systemd-logind for the Hyprland, Sway, Niri, and Labwc profiles. Archiso, the toolset Arch uses to build its installation and live media, is at version 91.

Security work from October

The November ISO inherits two security fixes that landed on October 21. PHP needed to move to 8.5.12 or php-legacy to 8.3.36 to close two remote-code-execution holes, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The advisory singles out systems publicly serving PHP apps, so anyone running a public PHP service should confirm the version. On the same date, Arch pulled compromised certificates out of the eMudhra intermediate CA through ca-certificates-mozilla 3.131.1-1 or newer. Skipping that one leaves you open to man-in-the-middle attacks.

TPM2-unlocked LUKS caveat

Since mkinitcpio 42, the systemd hook includes systemd-pcryptsetup.service, which shifts the measured PCR values used to unlock a TPM2-backed LUKS volume. If you rely on TPM2-unlocked disk encryption, re-enroll your TPM2 key after upgrading, as documented in systemd-cryptenroll(1). This is a one-time manual step, not something the upgrade does for you.

AUR hygiene reminder

The June 2026 AUR incident, where a high volume of malicious package adoptions and updates forced the project to lock down new accounts, updates, and adoptions for a stretch, is still the defining security moment of the year.
