Tampered PKGBUILDs had installed malicious npm packages. Arch’s advice has not changed: read your PKGBUILDs, especially when you rely on an automated AUR helper. Do not trust the latest version of an AUR package by version number alone.

Smaller changes

Repository health

Levente “anthraxx” Polyák won a second two-year term as Project Lead in the June 2026 election, so the leadership side stays put. The role breaks deadlocks, enforces the Code of Conduct, and handles money through the SPI foundation.

Package breadth

The snapshot inherits the October repository state: kernel 7.2.11, Archinstall 4.5, and the accumulated core-stack, graphics, desktop, and application updates that landed across September and October. A fresh ISO is the front door; what you build inside is up to you.

Bug fixes

Per-package Arch bug reports track the rest. The kernel bump to 7.2.11 carries the accumulated stable fixes since 7.2.7. The PHP and ca-certificates updates are the security-relevant fixes this cycle.

Known regressions and deferred work

None listed yet.

Sources

Official release details on the Arch release engineering page for 2026.11.01 with SHA256, BLAKE2b, and the PGP fingerprint for verification. The Arch release list confirms kernel 7.2.11 on this snapshot. Coverage from LinuxCompatible on the November 2026 ISO and Linuxiac on the October 2026 ISO.

item.title: Budgie 10.10.4: what actually changed since 10.10.3
item.description: A stable fourth minor release of the 10.10 series. Panel auto-hide and dock mode finally work on Wayland, Raven gets keyboard view switching, panels get a show shortcut, and a long list of panel, Crystal Dock, and labwc bugs get fixed.
item.content:encoded:
Budgie 10.10.4 shipped on November 1, 2026 as the fourth minor release of the 10.10 series. It is primarily a bug fix release, but it also makes automatic and intelligent panel hiding work on Wayland, reworks dock mode, adds keyboard switching between Raven views, adds a shortcut for showing panels, and speeds up panel startup. This is a normal stable release with no feature freeze.

Things worth your attention

Panel auto-hide and dock mode on Wayland

Under X11, Budgie could read window size and position and hid an Intelligent panel whenever a window intersected it. On Wayland it only gets maximized state and monitor from wlr-foreign-toplevel-management, so that overlap check had nothing to work with. In 10.10.3, an Intelligent panel hid by dropping behind windows, which broke once a window was maximized (Budgie issue 950); Automatic did not hide at all; and a hiding dock still reserved its whole edge.

10.10.4 reworks the panel code. A hidden panel now stays above windows but invisible, with a 3px strip along its edge to catch mouse events. Moving the mouse to that edge brings the panel back, and clicks elsewhere pass through to the window underneath. Panels stay visible while one of their popovers is open, so Budgie Menu, Icon Tasklist popovers, and the Sound applet keep working. Panels set to auto-hide no longer reserve screen space, so maximized windows use the full screen.

Since Budgie cannot check whether a window intersects a panel, both policies now go by maximized windows. Automatic hides the panel whenever any window on its monitor is maximized. Intelligent hides it only while the focused window is maximized.

Fullscreen applications

Moving the mouse to the edge of the screen now shows the panel above a fullscreen video. Games that lock the pointer are unaffected, as long as the compositor implements the pointer constraints protocol. Panels set to “Never” stay behind fullscreen applications, and there are two ways to raise panels over one (Budgie issue 600). Super+T is a new shortcut that shows all panels without opening Budgie Menu; pressing it again hides them, as does moving the mouse over a panel and then away. The Super key now shows every panel when opening Budgie Menu, not just the panel the menu sits on. Panels stay visible while the menu is open and hide once it closes and the mouse is not over any of them.

Raven

You can now switch between Raven’s widgets and notifications views with the keyboard while Raven is open (Budgie issue 1005). Super+A or Super+N switches to that view, and pressing the shortcut for the view you are already on closes Raven.

labwc bridge

Super+Shift+arrow keys move the focused window to the monitor in that direction, as they did on Budgie 10.9 (Budgie issue 1006). Picture-in-Picture windows, such as Firefox’s, now stay on top of other windows (Budgie issue 1018). Left clicking the desktop now only focuses it, while right clicking still opens the root menu. This fixes accidental launches on touchpads and Budgie Menu and Raven not closing when left clicking the desktop with desktop icons turned off (Budgie issue 1004). Existing labwc configs migrate on login, keeping any mouse settings you added.

Screen dimming and locking

You can choose how long Budgie waits before dimming the screen, from 30 seconds to 30 minutes, with 0 turning dimming off (Budgie issue 999). Set it with gsettings set com.solus-project.budgie-wm dimming-delay 90. You can also choose which screen locker Budgie uses, gtklock or swaylock (Budgie issue 1021). By default it uses the first one found, checking gtklock first: gsettings set org.buddiesofbudgie.budgie-locker locker-choice 'swaylock'. If the chosen locker is not installed, Budgie falls back to the one that is.

Faster panel startup

Previously, Budgie Menu, Icon Tasklist, and the Autostart page in Budgie Desktop Settings each loaded the full application list separately, and Icon Tasklist did so again for every window it needed to match. Now the list is loaded once and shared across the panel, and reloaded when applications are installed or removed. Measured with 281 applications installed: desktop-file scans at startup dropped from 9 to 1, main-thread scan time from about 200 ms to 22 ms, panel user-space CPU time from 392/427 ms to 255/270 ms (about 36% less), tasklist first population from 106/118 ms to 14/13 ms, allocation calls from 2,756,211 to 1,763,625 (about 36% fewer), and short-lived allocations from 522,009 to 213,184 (about 59% fewer). Peak heap rose by 0.81 MB, which is the shared application list kept for the panel’s lifetime. Opening the Autostart page and matching windows opened after startup also use the shared list now.

Development

Budgie Desktop now supports meson devenv, so the panel, applets, and Raven can run straight from a build directory without installing: meson devenv -C build budgie-panel --replace.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • The shared application list is reloaded when applications are installed or removed, so Icon Tasklist and the Autostart page stay current.
  • Crystal Dock’s wallpaper border workaround can handle JPEG XL wallpapers on distributions whose ImageMagick lacks JPEG XL support, by building Budgie with GraphicsMagick instead (Budgie issue 988).

Visual polish

  • A hidden panel keeps a 3px capture strip along its edge so the mouse can bring it back, while clicks elsewhere pass through to the window underneath.
  • Panels stay visible while a popover is open, so menus and applets remain usable.

Developer tools

  • meson devenv support for running the panel, applets, and Raven from a build tree.

Content and smaller apps

No new applications or content changes in this release.

Bug fixes

Panel

Applets could disappear from the panel after updating to 10.10.3 in a non-English locale. Applet settings store the plugin name, and the panel matched it against the name libpeas reports, which became translatable in 10.10.3, so translated names failed to match. Applets now store the plugin’s module name in a new module key, which the panel prefers; existing applets are migrated on login, and translated names saved by 10.10.3 are still accepted. Other panel fixes: a panel no longer stays hidden when an applet fails to load and that applet is removed from configuration; Budgie Menu no longer covers a panel that does not reserve screen space; clicking a dropdown inside a popover no longer closes the popover; the panel no longer crashes at startup when it has no stored position (Budgie issue 1001); a newly created panel saves its position right away; and a panel no longer moves off the primary monitor after changing its edge.

Bluetooth applet

Budgie Control Center 2.1.1 removed its Bluetooth panel, which broke the settings button. It now opens the first installed of Bluejay, Blueman, or Budgie Control Center.

Crystal Dock

JPEG XL wallpaper handling works via GraphicsMagick builds where ImageMagick lacks JPEG XL support (Budgie issue 988); changing a setting no longer regenerates the wallpaper twice (Budgie issue 945); and restarting budgie-daemon no longer leaves stray swaybg processes.

VMware

The mouse pointer is visible again in VMware virtual machines. The labwc session sets WLR_NO_HARDWARE_CURSORS when it detects VMware’s virtual GPU, as it already did for virgl (Budgie issue 1037).

Qt applications

Older Qt applications and AppImages without Wayland support can launch again. When QT_QPA_PLATFORM is not already set, the labwc session sets it to wayland;xcb, so Qt falls back to XWayland.

Known regressions and deferred work

None listed yet.

Sources

Official release announcement: Budgie 10.10.4 Released. GitHub release: v10.10.4. Forum thread: discussion.

item.title: KDE Plasma 6.8.2: what actually changed since 6.8.1
item.description: The second stable 6.8 update disables troublesome Wayland commit timing, fixes multi-GPU rendering and Sticky Keys, and repairs desktop widgets. Remote desktop, Discover, and the login manager also get corrections.
item.content:encoded:
Plasma 6.8.2 is a stable bugfix release, published on October 27, 2026. Compared with our 6.8 beta report, the feature-development period is over: this post covers the fixes since 6.8.1, not the whole 6.8 feature set. KDE has published the announcement, full changelog, and source downloads. Distribution packages may arrive later; there is no new feature-freeze milestone here.

Things worth your attention

Graphics and the compositor

KWin disables Wayland commit timing by default (c74b9d2, KDE bug 525514, KDE bug 527500). The commit explains why: a mechanism intended to help frame pacing was causing VRR problems, and an NVIDIA Vulkan driver bug could freeze mpv in some situations. This matters to people using variable-refresh displays or that playback path. The code still has an opt-in through KWIN_WAYLAND_SUPPORT_COMMIT_TIMING_V1=1; the default is now off.

Multi-GPU rendering gets two separate repairs. KWin checks buffer types more correctly in MultiGpuSwapchain and fixes synchronization when copying through EGL (KDE bug 527591, KDE bug 527604). The direct-scanout device check also moves to the compositor (KDE bug 527544). These changes concern systems where rendering and display output involve different GPUs, rather than promising a general frame-rate increase.

The DRM backend stops using post-blend offloading when color pipelines are unsupported (KDE bug 527628), and disallows it on the legacy path (KDE bug 527421). It also retries color-pipeline matching at the next hardware block (1b0a1de). These are corrections to hardware color processing, not a newly enabled HDR feature.

Input and accessibility

Sticky Keys now latches and locks modifiers on key release rather than key press (KDE bug 509714, c4b0a90). The old ordering let XKB clear a modifier that the accessibility filter had just locked. The commit gives a useful example: pressing Shift twice and then typing a b c produced Abc instead of ABC. People who use Sticky Keys to avoid holding down modifiers should get the persistent state they requested.

KWin also preserves an application’s keyboard layout after its last window closes (07db8db). This concerns per-application layout users. The Wayland pointer-constraints implementation fixes overwritten state (KDE bug 527675), and the virtual keyboard’s D-Bus API reports its visibility correctly (KDE bug 527067), which matters to programs integrating with the on-screen keyboard.

Remote desktop and recording

KRDP’s Plasma screencast session switches from the old fake-input path to libei (8703881). The commit identifies mapping pointers to individual screens as a reason for the change. That is relevant to remote-control users with multiple monitors; it is not a claim that this update adds every input-device type libei can support.

KRDP now starts with the client’s requested desktop size (215ef0e) and listens for a portal response before making the request (KDE bug 527555). It also stops tracking progressive frames while acknowledgements are suspended, a change linked to KDE bug 520260.

In kpipewire, the libx264 encoder is explicitly told the stream’s frame rate (KDE bug 526931), and an encoded stream honors a requested size set before startup (6cf1ead). These fixes are in the recording and streaming library used by Plasma tools, rather than new controls in Spectacle.

Shell, launchers, and desktop files

Plasma Desktop fixes disappearing desktop icons (fb2c22a). Folder View’s row and column arrangement settings now match their actual behavior (KDE bug 512993). The Pager keeps desktop labels and window icons bound to its model (KDE bug 522322, KDE bug 501660, KDE bug 506247), so those representations stay connected to the underlying data.

Plasma Workspace puts running tasks in the positions of their launchers (KDE bug 527189) and re-filters launchers when a window changes screen (KDE bug 527507). Kicker migrates the old favorite-ID format to the new one (KDE bug 527651). These are corrections for existing desktop and panel setups, not a redesigned Task Manager.

Login and session handling

Plasma Login Manager avoids autologin when someone explicitly switches to the greeter (5715be5). People choosing the login screen should not be sent back through automatic login. Its settings module also checks configuration size before truncation, checks the child process’s exit status, and clears supplementary groups. Those changes matter to administrators and distributions shipping this login manager.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • libksysguard limits the Line Chart applet to 2,000 data points (KDE bug 527627). This bounds the chart’s displayed history rather than changing system-wide sensor collection.
  • KWin fixes a rendering-performance issue in the Touch Points effect (f42c6a0) and stops flipping screenshots on the CPU side (7c028ff).
  • KWin’s virtual backend takes the target presentation timestamp into account. Its animation timeline no longer limits animation steps on software renderers, linked to KDE bug 522222.
  • Plasma Bigscreen improves homescreen blur performance (c143dd4).

Visual polish

Oxygen window-decoration buttons no longer look lumpy in certain fractional-scaling configurations (KDE bug 527549). KWin corrects startup-feedback icon sizing (KDE bug 527308), including a 16-by-16 base icon size. Activities use cropped wallpaper previews instead of stretching them (KDE bug 478784). Plasma Welcome corrects pixelation of its konqi-30.png image (2f151d2).

The Digital Clock preserves the system font’s OpenType features for the time (KDE bug 524257). PlasmaCore tooltips no longer lower label opacity when there is no heading (caedc25). Kickoff ties sidebar spacing to its compact-list style (KDE bug 524003), and Task Manager labels can wrap anywhere (KDE bug 526972).

Developer tools and diagnostics

KWin adds KWIN environment variables to its support information and prints them before Wayland startup (87a60b0, 47470e8). This gives bug reporters and developers a record of compositor overrides. Powerdevil includes the error code when a backlight-brightness job fails, linked to KDE bug 527520.

Union initializes element queries, indicator values, and tab spacing at construction. Its widget output also scales animation duration with the configured animation speed (KDE bug 527527). These are changes to the theming implementation, not a new public styling language.

Content and smaller apps

Plasma Addons restores animated images in tiled wallpapers (KDE bug 516541), repairs adding files and folders to Media Frame, and makes Picture of the Day previews match the “Scaled”, “Centered”, and “Tiled” modes (KDE bug 505690). Those are the concrete options affected, rather than a new wallpaper collection.

The Web Browser widget reapplies its fixed zoom factor after each page load (KDE bug 485583) and allows pages to read and write the clipboard (KDE bug 523381). Kup fixes the checkbox connection for “Exclude user-level Flatpaks” (8ae47dd).

Plasma Mobile respects disabled animations for Quick Settings labels and lock-screen PIN dots, and makes its shell usable with Qt Quick’s software renderer. Bigscreen reworks homescreen rows and tiles, fixes its display settings, and sets “Show Virtual Keyboard” to “With Touch, Tablet, and Mouse”.

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, input

KWin stops hidden scene items from occluding other content (edf9738). It makes the OpenGL context current when grabbing the cursor, guards against resizes in EGLPlatformContext::swapBuffers() (KDE bug 527269), and fails makeCurrent() when the context has failed. Picture-in-picture surfaces are lowered in the stack (KDE bug 527648).

Output identification uses the output name and EDID identifier instead of the raw EDID. The output configuration store can generate a completely new configuration (KDE bug 527401). KWin also adds a missing DPMS event filter and reloads screen-edge configuration when TouchTarget changes.

Sliding notifications handle instant animation speed correctly (KDE bug 527478). The dwell clicker stays open after a click when pinned (43848d5). Kicker uses its containment’s screen when limiting popup size (KDE bug 527385).

Login and sessions

Besides the greeter fix above, Plasma Workspace resets its entered-edit-mode state at startup (KDE bug 527738). Bigscreen fixes lock-screen state handling, a power-management inhibition failure that could occur at boot, and selection of the wrong desktop file when swapping sessions.

Apps and widgets

Discover’s update model reacts when resources disappear (483cd16). Its fwupd backend no longer passes the backend object to the connection thread, and its hidden desktop entries get X-KDE-AliasFor (KDE bug 511886).

Audio Volume plays feedback when increasing or decreasing volume (KDE bug 527775), using the configured sound theme (KDE bug 525954). KWin’s system bell also updates its sound theme when settings change. The Battery Monitor initializes its switch state on first opening (KDE bug 527560), and Info Center avoids reading properties from a null battery.

Plasma notification markup accepts single-quoted attributes (KDE bug 506733). Image wallpaper packages load correctly (KDE bug 527150), and the plain-color wallpaper derives the accent color from its configured color (KDE bug 513851). The calendar stops navigation before year 1 (KDE bug 525980).

The global play/pause shortcut no longer auto-repeats (KDE bug 521448). Media metadata fallbacks retain non-ASCII characters in titles and albums (KDE bug 503405). The Activity Bar fixes Tab focus and arrow-key navigation (KDE bug 527235), the application menu automatically focuses its search field (KDE bug 525569), and restored applet layouts no longer take preferred size into account (KDE bug 490687).

Security

Spectacle deletes its temporary OCR text file when the job finishes (e853a02). That reduces the lifetime of a file containing recognized screen text. Plasma Login Manager’s supplementary-group cleanup is also worth noting. The release announcement and changelog do not identify either as a CVE fix.

Libraries and build

System Monitor keeps its SplitView maximum width above its minimum width. qqc2-breeze-style restores contextual actions for TextArea (KDE bug 526591) and closes the mobile text-action popup after an action. Union guards against a potential null dereference (KDE bug 527459), fixes TextArea background styling (KDE bug 527455), adjusts list-delegate rounding (KDE bug 527087), and corrects menubar horizontal padding (KDE bug 527213).

Known regressions and deferred work

None listed yet in the release announcement. Two deliberate rollbacks deserve separate mention: commit timing is disabled by default, as described above, and KWin reverts its default server-side drop-shadow rule for Steam (fba4609). The latter commit says the rule exposed visual flaws in Steam, including a more obvious black outline and child-window closing problems. A manually added or customized rule remains in the user’s configuration; the unmodified default goes away. This is narrower than removing shadow-only decorations generally.

Sources

KDE’s official Plasma 6.8.2 release announcement confirms the date and stable bugfix status. The complete per-module changes are in the 6.8.1 to 6.8.2 changelog, with published archives and signatures on the 6.8.2 source information page. Commit explanations in KDE’s official GitHub mirrors cover disabling commit timing, Sticky Keys modifier handling, KRDP’s libei port, and reverting the Steam shadow rule.

item.title: KDE Plasma 6.8.1: what actually changed since 6.8.0
item.description: A bugfix update that landed six days after 6.8.0. Kwin gets the bulk of the fixes: pointer constraints, slowkeys, color pipelines, and suspend handling. Plasma Desktop and Workspace pick up smaller corrections.
item.content:encoded:
Plasma 6.8.1 is a bugfix update that shipped on October 20, six days after 6.8.0. It is the first point release of the 6.8 series. No official announcement page exists yet; the tag is on Invent and the tarballs are on download.kde.org. The changes are drawn from the compare views for plasma-desktop, plasma-workspace, and kwin.

Things worth your attention

Kwin: pointer constraints and pointer focus

Xaver Hugl fixed a cluster of Wayland pointer handling issues. The pointerconstraints_v1 implementation no longer requires a commit for locking or unlocking, which fixes problems with Wine Wayland (BUG: 526010). Implicit pointer grabs on subsurfaces were broken; they now work correctly. The effective pointer focus surface was not always updated, making the pointer position calculate as if it were on the toplevel surface. An autotest for pointer warping with pointer locks was added, and another for implicit pointer grabs. The OSK now hides immediately when the input method deactivates (BUG: 459136).

Kwin: slowkeys accessibility filter

Vlad Zahorodnii fixed the slowkeys accessibility filter, which was dropping key release events in certain cases (BUG: 523419). The filter logic now correctly sends the release event when a client has seen at least one press. Cleanup includes removing an unused KF6::WindowSystem dependency and using Q_UNREACHABLE_RETURN.

Kwin: color pipelines disabled for 6.8

Color pipelines in the DRM backend are disabled for the 6.8 series (BUG: 525839). The OpenGL shader now matches the color pipeline calculations more closely, and the compositor takes floating point buffers into account. This is a conservative move: the color pipeline code is not ready for prime time, and disabling it avoids regressions on hardware that depends on it.

Kwin: suspend and screen handling

Screens now turn off before suspend (again), and suspend is delayed correctly. Sleep inhibition is removed when no outputs are connected. The zoom effect zooms towards the pointer in push mode (BUG: 508098). The tabbox thumbnail grid switcher is now a non-grabbing popup (BUG: 520537).

Plasma Desktop: KCM and applet fixes

The landing page KCM now shows default KCMs when there are no most used KCMs (BUG: 522711). The touchpad and mouse KCMs get indentation fixes for checkboxes and scroll-button behavior options, with proper right-to-left layout support. Action names are corrected (BUGS: 526886). The kicker applet inherits LayoutMirroring, adds an inner right margin when scrollable, and only sets drag mimedata URL when one exists. Desktop containments no longer always forward Shift+key to krunner.

Plasma Workspace: floating panels and notifications

The scripting API now saves and restores floating panel config correctly (BUG: 526843). The freespacenotifier configure action is connected (it never was), and the XDG activation token is set on launch jobs and config. Device notifications ignore virtual screens, so starting a screenshare no longer shows a spurious notification about a screen being connected. Klipper requests activation when showing its popup (Bugs: 527326). The Colors KCM unexports top-level on editor close (Bugs: 527382). The wallpaper image view handles the case where the type cannot be determined, falling back to a static image view.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

Kwin: the renderloop makes VRR scheduling use an item instead of a window. The effect timeline does not assume frames are at least 1ms apart. The workspace scene takes layer repaints into account in collectDamage and does not ignore repaints on BackgroundEffectItems. The compositor accumulates cursor updates with a timer (Bugs: 527145, 527273). The DRM backend resolves symlinks in KWIN_DRM_DEVICES when adding GPUs (Bugs: 527309), preserves preferred modes below minimum resolution, and makes DrmVirtualOutput::m_layer a unique_ptr. The multigpuswapchain re-adds the DCC workaround for AMD Cezanne (Bugs: 521716) and enforces the host memory workaround for Nvidia GPUs (Bugs: 527163).

Visual polish

Kwin: the OpenGL texture uses swizzles to ignore non-existent alpha channels. The compositor does not present the cursor if rendering it failed. The scene avoids repainting for blocked timed commits (Bugs: 527144). The effect timeline does not limit animation steps while repaints are throttled (Bugs: 526290). SSD titlebar is permitted when an SSD drop-shadow is applied (Bugs: 527391).

Accessibility

Kwin: slowkeys cleanup (see above). The OSK hides immediately on input method deactivation. The zoom effect zooms towards the pointer in push mode.

Developer tools

Kwin: a new KWIN_WAYLAND_SUPPORT_COMMIT_TIMING_V1 environment variable helps debug performance issues (CCBUG: 525514). Autotests for pointer warping with pointer locks and implicit pointer grabs were added.

Bug fixes

Compositor and display

Kwin: pointer constraints no longer require a commit for locking (BUG: 526010). Implicit pointer grabs on subsurfaces fixed. Effective pointer focus surface updates correctly. Color pipelines disabled for 6.8 (BUG: 525839). OpenGL shader matches color pipeline calculations. Compositor takes floating point buffers into account. Scene takes layer repaints into account. Repaints on BackgroundEffectItems no longer ignored. Cursor updates accumulated with a timer (Bugs: 527145, 527273). Compositor does not present cursor if rendering failed. Scene avoids repainting for blocked timed commits (Bugs: 527144). Effect timeline does not limit animation steps while repaints throttled (Bugs: 526290). VRR scheduling uses an item instead of a window. Tabbox does not show while fullscreen effect active (BUG: 495720). Tabbox thumbnail grid is a non-grabbing popup (BUG: 520537). SSD titlebar permitted with SSD drop-shadow (BUG: 527391). DRM preserves preferred modes below minimum resolution. OpenGL texture uses swizzles for non-existent alpha channels. OpenGL EGL backend does not filter out external-only linear for YUV formats.

Input

Kwin: slowkeys filter sends released events correctly (BUG: 523419). Key repeat disabling fixed (Bugs: 514747, 526575). Tablet mode manager does not let pointer devices override tablet mode switch. Desktop containments do not always forward Shift+key to krunner.

Login and sessions

No changes in this release.

Apps

Plasma Workspace: freespacenotifier configure action connected. Freespacenotifier sets XDG activation token. Device notifications ignore virtual screens. Klipper requests activation on popup (Bugs: 527326). Colors KCM unexports top-level on close (Bugs: 527382). Wallpaper image view handles undetermined type. Scripting saves and restores floating panel config (BUG: 526843). Shell corona sets default containment.

Security

No security fixes in this release.

Libraries and build

Kwin: slowkeys removes unused KF6::WindowSystem dependency. DRM backend makes DrmVirtualOutput::m_layer a unique_ptr. DRM backend renames DrmVirtualOutput::recreateSurface(). DRM backend destroys virtual egl layers in releaseBuffers(). Kwin QPA fixes crash without render device. Kwin scripting destroyed before workspace goes down. Kwin fixes cases where renderItem return value was ignored. Kwin input method does not try to show without context (Bugs: 524506). Kwin screencast closes screencasts for removed outputs.

Known regressions and deferred work

None listed yet. The release is too fresh for a formal regressions list.

Sources

The tag and tarballs are live on Invent for plasma-desktop and download.kde.org. The commit listing for this point release is the compare view for plasma-desktop, plasma-workspace, and kwin. The 6.8.0 feature release was announced on kde.org.

item.title: Ubuntu 26.10 Stonking Stingray: what actually changed
item.description: The October 2026 interim release ships Linux 7.3, GNOME 51, completes the Rust coreutils migration, and introduces Myna local speech-to-text. Nine months of support, until July 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Ubuntu 26.10, codenamed Stonking Stingray, shipped on October 15. It is the first interim release since 26.04 LTS and carries nine months of support through July 2027. The headline items are Linux 7.3, GNOME 51, the completion of the Rust coreutils migration, and a local speech-to-text preview called Myna. There is also a new window tiling interface, TPM-backed full disk encryption without a hardware root of trust, and RISC-V desktop images for the first time.

Things worth your attention

Rust coreutils migration complete

The transition to Rust uutils finished in this release. The remaining cp, mv, and rm commands are now the Rust implementations, completing a migration that started in earlier releases. For most users this is invisible, but it matters for anyone who scripts around edge cases in coreutils behavior. The Rust implementations have been in testing for several release cycles.

D-Bus switches to dbus-broker

Both the system bus and the per-user session bus now run on dbus-broker instead of dbus-daemon. Canonical points to better accounting, reliability, and scalability from its asynchronous, event-driven architecture. The change is documented in a dedicated Discourse post. If you have custom D-Bus policy or monitoring tooling, this is worth a look.

Myna speech-to-text preview

Myna is an early, opt-in speech-to-text feature for Ubuntu Desktop. Hold a configurable key to dictate into the focused app. Transcription runs locally on the machine, with no audio sent to a network service. It is not preinstalled and its features may change before a stable release. Canonical frames this as the first step toward a more context-aware desktop. Read the Myna technology preview announcement for details.

TPM-backed FDE without a hardware root of trust

Computers without a hardware root of trust can now be installed with TPM-backed full disk encryption, provided a PIN or passphrase is also set on the TPM-backed key. This was backported to 26.04.1, but 26.10 is the first release where it is available out of the box. Upgrade support for systems already running under TPM-backed FDE is not ready on release day; Canonical anticipates enabling it during the 26.10 lifecycle.

New window tiling interface

Dragging a window to the edge of the screen now shows a popup offering tiling layout options. This comes from the Tiling-Assistant project and is tracked in ubuntu/Tiling-Assistant#451. It brings Ubuntu closer to the tiling behavior that GNOME extensions have provided for years.

GNOME 51

The desktop is GNOME 51, which brought its own set of changes: smoother frame scheduling, monitor brightness persistence, improved accessibility (reduced motion extended, keyboard-adjustable screenshot selections, Orca improvements), and a more responsive Calendar. The full GNOME 51 changes are covered in the GNOME 51 release notes. Ubuntu-specific additions on top include a unified app-details view in App Center, a dedicated Drivers page, and on-demand multimedia codec installation.

App Center changes

App Center now presents Snap and Debian package details in a unified view, bringing publisher, ratings, permissions, version, package size, screenshots, and description together with the relevant install, open, or uninstall action. A dedicated Drivers page lets you review available graphics drivers, including NVIDIA branches, with clearer metadata for comparison. When a media file uses a codec that is not installed, App Center can offer to install the needed codec for one-time playback.

Ubuntu Certified hardware status in Settings

Settings can now show whether a computer is certified for Ubuntu. The status is checked using the Ubuntu Hardware API, with caching to avoid repeated checks. The hwctl client is included as a snap. For details on what data is collected, see the System Information Notice.

Microsoft Entra ID authentication

The authd service gained support for signing in with a Microsoft Entra ID password and completing MFA challenges on the desktop, in terminal and SSH sessions, and in Polkit dialogs. Passwordless sign-in with FIDO2 security keys, Microsoft Authenticator, or Temporary Access Passes is also supported. New authctl commands cover user management tasks like changing home directories, login shells, and deleting users and groups. See the Entra ID sign-in announcement and the authd documentation.

New wallpapers

Ubuntu 26.10 includes new Stonking Stingray wallpapers, including designs selected through a community wallpaper competition. See the wallpaper announcement.

RISC-V desktop images and amd64v3 optimization

For the first time, Ubuntu ships desktop images for RISC-V. The amd64 installation images are now optimized for amd64v3 (x86-64-v3), which means CPUs from roughly 2013 onward with AVX2 support. Older hardware will need the generic amd64 images.

Post-quantum-ready package signing

Ubuntu 26.10 includes post-quantum cryptography support in package signing, preparing for the transition to quantum-resistant algorithms. The libp11 package also gained post-quantum support for ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and FALCON key operations.

Smaller changes

Toolchain upgrades

GCC 15.2.0 with C++ modules support, .NET 10.0.112, Go 1.27, LLVM 22.1.8, OpenJDK 25.0.4 (with OpenJDK 27 available), Python 3.14.7, Rust 1.97.1, and Zig 0.16. Ubuntu 26.10 sticks with GCC 15 as the default compiler.

Server and infrastructure

FreeRADIUS 3.2.10, FRRouting 10.7.1, HAProxy 3.4.2 (LTS until 2031-Q2, with a new default load balancing algorithm), iPXE 2.0.0 (UEFI Secure Boot, RISC-V and LoongArch64 support), Postfix 3.11.7 (JSON output in postconf/postalias/postmap/postmulti), Samba 4.24.7, MySQL 9.7 LTS (from 8.4 LTS), Valkey 9.1, strongSwan 6.0.7, and rdma-core 64.0. The ssl-cert package increased the default generated key length from 2048 to 3072 bits.

Virtualization and cloud

QEMU 11.0 drops 32-bit host builds. libvirt 12.6.0 drops group-based socket access in favor of polkit and encrypts libvirt secrets. Subiquity 26.10 adds new /boot storage requirements for signed GRUB, experimental TPM/FDE use-gap support, Btrfs resize support, and multi-layout keyboard configuration documentation. edk2 2026.05 brings confidential computing improvements and LoongArch64 Secure Boot support.

System-level opt-out for Ubuntu Insights

Administrators can now opt out of anonymous Ubuntu Insights system report collection for the entire system. The configuration overrides individual opt-ins, so they are interpreted as opt-outs instead. The setting is available in Settings or through the Ubuntu Insights CLI.

Bug fixes

Desktop and GNOME

GNOME 51 brought its own batch of fixes across Mutter, Shell, GTK, and apps. On the Ubuntu side, the Showtime video player might not display subtitles and playback might stall when changing subtitle tracks; the issue is being addressed in GStreamer base plugins (LP: #2119649).

Server and packages

The OpenSSH package was split into GSSAPI/Kerberos and non-GSSAPI variants that conflict with each other. Purging a package in rc state after switching variants can break the openssh configuration and cause loss of remote access. Do not purge an openssh package in rc state until the fix in LP: #2169738 is released. Only openssh-gssapi was fixed for 26.10; the main openssh package will receive an SRU.

Hardware support

On Raspberry Pi CM5 and potentially other Pi 5 models, there is significantly larger power draw at boot time. If you experience boot issues and are not using an official 5A-capable power supply, try one before debugging further. The gnome-initial-setup time zone dropdown can wobble (LP: #2084611). On server images, cloud-init configurations that rely on networking must ensure at least one network interface is marked optional: false in network-config due to Netplan changes to the wait-online service (LP: #2060311). WiFi wlan0 may not activate on first boot (LP: #2170885).

On SpacemiT K3 platforms, the second PCIe slot, DisplayPort and HDMI audio, GPU/VPU/G2D hardware nodes, and power balance elements are not supported. Initial support landed in 26.10 but these gaps remain.

Security

strongSwan 6.0.7 fixed CVE-2026-47895 (libstrongswan identity cloning leading to double-free, potential RCE). The 6.0.6 release fixed seven additional CVEs across libtls, pkcs7, libsimaka, constraints, libradius, and gmp plugins. Exim4 4.99.4 fixed CVE-2026-48840 (uninitialised-stack disclosure in the PROXYv2 parser). The 4.99.2 and 4.99.3 releases fixed eight more CVEs including a musl DNS crash and a use-after-free in GnuTLS BDAT/CHUNKING.

Known regressions and deferred work

Systems running under TPM-backed FDE will not be able to upgrade from Ubuntu 26.04 LTS to 26.10 on release day. Canonical anticipates enabling these upgrades during the 26.10 lifecycle. The App Center is not installed by default on the RISC-V desktop image; users can install it with sudo snap install snap-store. Showtime subtitle issues are tracked but not resolved at release time.

Sources

Ubuntu 26.10 release notes on documentation.ubuntu.com, covering desktop features, server updates, known issues, and hardware support gaps. Ubuntu 26.10 (Stonking Stingray) released on the ubuntu-announce mailing list. Phoronix coverage of the release, including the Linux 7.3 kernel, GNOME 51, and Rust coreutils completion. Canonical press release with the official announcement. Myna speech-to-text technology preview and dbus-broker switch announcement on Ubuntu Discourse. Stonking Stingray wallpaper announcement and Microsoft Entra ID sign-in.

item.title: COSMIC Epoch 1.9.0: what actually changed since 1.8.0
item.description: System76 tagged a coordinated submodule bump that adds two new modules to the epoch: cosmic-osk, the on-screen keyboard, and cosmic-viewer, the image viewer. git-lfs becomes a required dependency.
item.content:encoded:
As of September 23 2026, COSMIC Epoch 1.9.0 is tagged. GitHub marks it as pre-release with release notes pending, but the tag itself is the pin point. The diff between 1.8.0 and 1.9.0 is seven commits: it adds two new submodules (cosmic-osk and cosmic-viewer), bumps git-lfs as a required dependency, and updates every existing submodule. The real story is the on-screen keyboard and image viewer joining the epoch.

Things worth your attention

New modules: cosmic-osk and cosmic-viewer

Two new submodules joined the epoch for the first time.

cosmic-osk is the COSMIC On-Screen Keyboard. It has been in development for over a year (55 commits) and uses libei sockets instead of the older virtual-keyboard-unstable-v1 protocol. It supports multiple keyboard layouts that change to match the group sent by the compositor, gamepad input via gilrs, drag on touch input, and a cosmic-session-lock-layer-v1 protocol for the lock screen. Settings control when the OSK appears, and checkboxes toggle gamepad and IME activation. The function row is hidden by default. A recent commit allows overriding the layer to be overlay, so the keyboard can appear over fullscreen apps. The OSK also implements dead key display improvements and xkb symbol-based key naming per level. Inline examples of new UI strings and icons: “Hide function row by default”, “Settings for when to show OSK”, “Add guide for controller bindings”, “Use symbols for some keys”, “Add gamepad icons”, and “Improve modifiers support”.

cosmic-viewer is the COSMIC Image Viewer. It has 203 commits and its own 1.9.0 tag. It includes a settings drawer for theme and startup preferences, text annotation with placeholder fixes, and a toolbar that uses the Primary style. A recent commit allows opening just a single file.

Who it affects: anyone who has been waiting for a native on-screen keyboard and image viewer in COSMIC. The OSK is the first to use libei rather than the deprecated virtual-keyboard protocol.

Build and packaging

git-lfs is now a required dependency. cosmic-edit uses it for PNG files, so distros packaging the epoch need to include it. The README build instructions were updated to reflect this. The justfile and version-update.sh script were also updated.

Submodule bumps

Every existing submodule received a version bump: cosmic-applets, cosmic-applibrary, cosmic-bg, cosmic-comp, cosmic-edit, cosmic-files, cosmic-greeter, cosmic-initial-setup, cosmic-launcher, cosmic-monitor, cosmic-notifications, cosmic-osd, cosmic-panel, cosmic-player, cosmic-session, cosmic-settings, cosmic-settings-daemon, cosmic-store, cosmic-term, cosmic-workspaces-epoch, and xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • cosmic-osk uses libei socket instead of virtual-keyboard-unstable-v1 (cosmic-osk commit a1a57a2)
  • cosmic-osk supports multiple layouts with compositor-driven group switching (cosmic-osk commit b7af9c0)
  • cosmic-osk implements gamepad support via gilrs with mouse emulation (cosmic-osk commit 52f2934)
  • cosmic-osk adds drag on touch input (cosmic-osk commit 4a757d6)
  • cosmic-osk blurs just the floating keyboard with rounded rectangle strips (cosmic-osk commit fb7a36d)
  • cosmic-osk hides function row by default (cosmic-osk commit 22885b1)
  • cosmic-osk replaces settings link button with checkboxes for gamepad and IME activation (cosmic-osk commit 5f6c118)
  • cosmic-osk allows overriding the layer to be overlay (cosmic-osk commit 38e9625)
  • cosmic-viewer adds settings drawer for theme and startup
  • cosmic-viewer allows opening just a single file

Developer tools and packaging

  • git-lfs added as required dependency (COSMIC PR 1324)
  • justfile updated
  • version-update.sh updated

Bug fixes

On-screen keyboard

  • cosmic-osk fixes dead_belowring unicode mapping (cosmic-osk commit 0a859e3)
  • cosmic-osk improves display of dead keys, fixes COSMIC OSK issue 24 (cosmic-osk commit 11d0622)
  • cosmic-osk fixes active log spam on input commit (cosmic-osk commit 36c55db)
  • cosmic-osk fixes wrong height on startup (cosmic-osk commit 5feb77f)
  • cosmic-osk fixes right arrow (cosmic-osk commit c344e49)
  • cosmic-osk ensures keys are released when dragging, docking, or hiding (cosmic-osk commit 121cf5c)
  • cosmic-osk fixes caps lock using return icon (cosmic-osk commit 2fccccc)
  • cosmic-osk ignores repeated activates after hiding OSK, waits for next deactivate (cosmic-osk commit 93aed50)
  • cosmic-osk uses xkb syms to determine key names per level, fixes COSMIC OSK issue 15 (cosmic-osk commit 44038c1)

Image viewer

  • cosmic-viewer fixes text annotation placeholder
  • cosmic-viewer fixes toolbar should use Primary style
  • cosmic-viewer fixes text / select and move

Known regressions and deferred work

  • GitHub marks 1.9.0 as pre-release with release notes pending
  • cosmic-osk and cosmic-viewer are new modules and may have rough edges

Sources

Official epoch tag on GitHub: epoch-1.9.0 and the submodule bump commit c7ae713. New submodule repositories: cosmic-osk and cosmic-viewer. The epoch comparison epoch-1.8.0…epoch-1.9.0 shows seven commits and 27 files changed. The git-lfs dependency addition is tracked in #1324.

item.title: KDE Plasma 6.8 RC: what changed since the beta
item.description: The release candidate (Beta 2, versioned 6.7.91) is out, the feature freeze is in effect, and the final release lands October 14. Here is everything that changed since the beta, including the Union QtWidgets preview, a KWin memory leak fix, and dozens of polishing touches.
item.content:encoded:
As of September 24, 2026, Plasma 6.8 Beta 2 (versioned 6.7.91) is out. KDE labels this the release candidate; the feature freeze and soft UI freeze have been in effect since Beta 1 on September 10. The final release is due October 14, coinciding with KDE’s 30th anniversary. Only fixes and translations should land between now and then.

Things worth your attention

Union theming enters its second phase

The Union theming system’s public tech preview enters its second half. Union now themes QtWidgets applications such as Dolphin and Kate (Union MR 270). To test it, install the union package, open System Settings → Colors & Themes → Application Style, and select “Breeze (Union)”. This applies Union styling to both QtQuick and QtWidgets apps. Visual glitches are expected and known; report them at bugs.kde.org with product=Union. The goal is for Union-styled apps to look as close as possible to their Breeze equivalents, with minor visual improvements considered intentional.

KWin memory leak fixed

KWin now depends on plasma-wayland-protocols 1.23.0 to fix a memory leak that could grow severe over time (Wayland Protocols MR 525314). The bug leaked one kde_output_device_mode_v2 resource per advertised mode on every client re-bind. After nearly two weeks of uptime, one reporter found kwin_wayland consuming around 2.2 GB of RAM versus a typical ~0.3 GB. Anyone running the beta for extended periods will notice a significant improvement.

Clipboard settings overhauled

The clipboard’s settings for handling copied image data and “MIME actions” are now more comprehensible (Tomáš Hnyk, KDE bug 348932, KDE bug 502274, KDE bug 473882). The old interface was confusing enough that many users never touched it; the new one actually explains what the options do.

Lock screen polish

Clicking the “Show On-Screen Keyboard” button (renamed from “Virtual Keyboard”) on the lock and login screens now always shows the keyboard as expected, regardless of its typical visibility settings (Kristen McWilliam and Nate Graham, KDE bug 467209, Plasma Workspace MR 7044). The lock screen also notifies you when the “Slow Keys” accessibility feature is enabled.

Input Method widget overhauled

The Input Method widget has been reworked. It now primarily switches between on-screen keyboard visibility modes and lets you manually show the keyboard while an XWayland app is focused, since these apps cannot trigger the keyboard automatically (Kristen McWilliam, Plasma Workspace MR 6876).

Kup backup notifications improved

Kup’s backup progress notifications now show elapsed time, and average speed calculations are more accurate (Méven Car, Kup MR 62). Kup itself is new to Plasma in 6.8 — it is the backup scheduler that moved into the Plasma release cycle.

Portal dialogs polished

KDE’s desktop portal dialogs received another round of visual polish for better information density and consistency (David Edmundson and Oliver Beard, Portal MR 628, Portal MR 630).

Smaller changes

Visual polish

  • Kickoff Application Launcher widget is now always big enough by default to fully accommodate all items in its sidebar rather than sometimes being scrollable by a few pixels (Christoph Wolk, KDE bug 515175).
  • Notifications’ speed graphs have better axis label padding (Méven Car, Plasma Workspace MR 151).
  • Spectacle no longer shows a misleading message about copying the image to the clipboard after you use the “Share…” feature to share it elsewhere (Tobias Fella, Spectacle MR 586).
  • Digital Clock widget’s calendar view keyboard navigation improved (Christoph Wolk, Plasma Workspace MR 6900).
  • System Settings’ Quick Settings page now shows a default set of frequently-used pages until the app has learned your habits (Tobias Fella, KDE bug 522711).
  • Power & Battery widget percentages use fixed-width tabular numerals so other UI elements don’t jump around as numbers change (Christoph Wolk, Powerdevil MR 674).
  • Multi-panel setups: the “Show Notifications” button on the missed-notifications notification now opens the history widget on the first panel only (Ameen Al-Asady, Plasma Workspace MR 7028).
  • Clipboard widget inline buttons for the selected item appear only on hover or keyboard focus, so you can read the full text of the selected entry (Christoph Wolk, KDE bug 520130).
  • Renamed audio devices is less awkward (Tomáš Hnyk, KDE bug 508211).
  • KWin’s Overview effect: adjacent virtual desktop highlights no longer touch (Nate Graham, KDE bug 523656).

Performance and internals

  • Plasma no longer writes to a cache file every time it displays a notification (ValdikSS, KDE bug 523805).
  • System Tray ported away from the Animator system, fixing an old crash (KDE bug 487699).
  • ShellCorona tracks uiReady more robustly (KDE bug 525327).
  • KWin virtual backend honors buffer transform when rendering.
  • KWin DRM backend matches pageflip events to unique commit IDs (KDE bug 524883).
  • KWin GBM buffer allocation destroyed as soon as possible (KDE bug 525748).

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, and input

  • Fixed an issue that left Task Manager tasks’ “I’m playing audio right now” indicators stuck after entering and exiting full-screen mode (Christoph Wolk, KDE bug 522471).
  • Fixed a KWin crash when interacting with titlebar buttons in very specific ways (Vlad Zahorodnii, KWin MR 9926).
  • Fixed lockscreen not properly showing when using the “Never require password” setting (KDE bug 525349).
  • Fixed Wine window focus regression (KDE bug 525590).
  • Fixed a crash returning to a game using Alt+Tab (KDE bug 510116).
  • Fixed black wallpaper previews in the Activity Switcher sidebar (KDE bug 378693).
  • Fixed XWayland not launching when an invalid config file existed in /etc/xdg/Xwayland-session.d/ (Ilya Katsnelson, KWin MR 9894).

Login and sessions

  • Fixed Plasma hanging on login when connected to a monitor with a non-standard VCP range, such as the Samsung Odyssey G60SF (Marco Martin, KDE bug 525216).
  • Fixed Plasma crash on login when no screens were present early in boot (KDE bug 520720).
  • Fixed occasional random Plasma crash on login (David Edmundson, Plasma Workspace MR 7042).
  • Fixed a crash when querying the wallpaper via D-Bus while switching wallpaper plugins (Alperen Yildiz, KDE bug 525207).

Apps

  • Fixed a bug where copying text in LibreOffice apps added it to persistent clipboard history only every other time (Tomáš Hnyk, KDE bug 519510).
  • Fixed middle-click-pasting text selected in a non-Qt app into a Qt app working only every other time (Tomáš Hnyk, KDE bug 506325).
  • Fixed Spectacle’s full-screen annotation UI tool settings appearing off-screen (Mirko Laruina, KDE bug 524499).
  • Fixed Menu Editor crashing when deleting three or more items at once (David Edmundson, KDE bug 525598).
  • Fixed KRunner-powered unit conversions in French (Tobias Fella, KDE bug 510873).
  • Fixed Emoji Selector showing incorrect buttons and placeholder when search returned no results.
  • Fixed sRGB color intensity info button in KScreen (KDE bug 525540).

Libraries and build

  • Qt requirement bumped to 6.11.1 across all Plasma modules.
  • KDE Frameworks requirement bumped to 6.30.
  • Fixed a serious QML issue that could break QML-based UIs with nonsensical property errors (Fabian Kosmale, Qt Qt bug 149607 and Qt bug 146886).
  • Fixed “Frames and Outlines Contrast” theme setting not taking effect in some apps (KDE bug 525364).
  • KScreen made XCB a required dependency; dropped obsolete libxcb-randr.

Known regressions and deferred work

Union theming for QtWidgets apps has known visual glitches (acknowledged in the official announcement). Location-based timezone setting remains deferred. Session restore and window position memory are still being improved. Some accessibility features from third-party apps may behave differently on the Wayland-only session.

Sources

Official KDE announcement for Plasma 6.8 Beta 2: 6.7.91. Complete changelog from Beta 1 to Beta 2: 6.7.90-6.7.91. KDE Community Wiki page for Plasma 6.8 features: Plasma 6.8. Phoronix coverage of Beta 2 and earlier performance work. “This Week in Plasma” blog posts: Beta Release and Let the Polishing Begin. 9to5Linux preview of the October 14 release.

item.title: GNOME 51 "A Coruña": the final release
item.description: GNOME 51.0 is out. The beta we previewed in August has shipped, with cross-GPU scan-out, custom pointer acceleration profiles, and a final batch of bug fixes added since the freeze report.
item.content:encoded:
GNOME 51.0 is out. The beta we previewed in August has now shipped, and a few things have changed since that freeze report: Mutter gained cross-GPU buffer scan-out support, custom pointer acceleration profiles landed, and a last batch of bug fixes cleared the final milestone. This post covers everything that made it into the stable release.

Things worth your attention

Graphics and the compositor

Mutter gained cross-GPU buffer scan-out support in the final week before release. This lets a secondary GPU scan out buffers directly, avoiding a copy step on hybrid graphics laptops.

Custom pointer acceleration profiles are another last-minute addition. Mutter now supports libinput’s user-defined acceleration curves through a new gsettings-desktop-schemas key (MR gsettings-desktop-schemas MR 99 on schemas, matching Mutter MR from February 2025). You can tune pointer speed at different movement rates instead of being stuck with the flat default.

The changes from the freeze report all made it in: Mutter blurs window backgrounds through the ext-background-effect-v1 Wayland protocol with GTK 4.24 on the client side, Michel Dänzer’s frame scheduling patches landed, Benjamin Otte reworked the GTK frame clock, cursors ship as SVG now, and Mutter fills in mastering display metadata for HDR output.

Mutter also dropped legacy NVIDIA drivers (Mutter MR 5079). Old proprietary versions stop working; current NVIDIA and open kernel modules are fine.

APIs, protocols, platform

GTK jumped from 4.21.6 to 4.24.0. The new version supports the ext-background-effect protocol for blurred backgrounds, reworked the frame clock for better precision, supports the CSS font-width property, and lets you change the visible focus timeout with gtk-keyboard-focus-visible-timeout. Session save/restore was deferred to GTK 4.26.

GLib 2.90.0 shipped with UAPI file masking and drop-ins for GKeyFile, g_string_free_deep(), g_set_date_time(), GUnixFDList helpers, and finer g_timeout APIs. A heap overflow in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() was fixed (GLib issue 3992, CVE-2026-16118), among several out-of-bounds read fixes.

libsoup 3.7.3 added compression dictionaries (dcb/dcz) and SoupCompressionDictionaryRequest. libadwaita 1.10.0 shipped.

GJS 1.90.0 carries the breaking change where GObject.Interface no longer installs methods as unbound statics. Extensions calling Interface.method(obj) must switch to Interface.prototype.method.call(this).

The platform-level changes from the freeze report all landed: text_input_v3 version 2, xdg_session_management_v1, global shortcut inhibitors for a11y shortcuts, Input Capture portal session persistence and clipboard access, oo7-portal as the Secret portal implementation, and new D-Bus properties SessionIsLocked and SessionClass on gnome-session.

dconf 51.0 ships the safe GVDB writer for home directories on NFS by default.

Shell and login

Web login and the unified auth mechanism (MR GNOME Shell MR 3212) are in. The login screen can offer several authentication mechanisms side by side, including logging in through the web. This is the biggest GDM and Shell change in years.

Shell started honoring the reduced-motion setting (initial support), holding back motion animations for people who want less of them. The COPY, CUT, and PASTE keys work in Shell text entries now.

Calendar reminders pop up as Shell notifications (GNOME Shell MR 1064), so you no longer need to open the calendar app to see them. Monitor brightness is saved and restored across sessions.

GDM 51.0 has a fallback session setting, an option to turn off the local greeter on headless machines, KMSCON VT compatibility, conflicting sessions enumerated through logind, and Kerberos support for remote login. Fingerprint login is no longer allowed for initial system login; the sensor now works only for re-authentication, both for security reasons and because various parts of the system (like the keyring) break when logging in via fingerprint.

The VA-API H.264 screencast pipeline gained rate control, so screen recording loads the machine less. The extensions app moved to its own repository. Extension authors should note that async disable() is explicitly disallowed now.

Applications

Papers can insert visual signatures into documents. Right-click anywhere on a page, draw a signature with mouse or touchscreen, or import an image; Papers removes the background so the signature blends in. The feature was developed by Malika Asman during her Outreachy internship. Papers also prints free text annotations by default, renders fractional scales better using GTK’s new snapping API, and describes paper sizes with more detail in properties.

Loupe shows the ICC or CICP profile description along with metadata like author, copyright, lens, and software.

Maps can download map areas for offline use. Downloaded regions are managed from a simple list. Public transit directions gained live departures, real-time delay information, track and stop details, and walking times. Tapping a station or stop shows live departure and arrival times where data is available.

Files shows a drag counter badge when moving multiple items, auto-selects copied files, stops clearing the selection on right-click in empty space, groups its notifications, and reloads folder views faster.

Web has a keyboard shortcut for copying the page URL (Ctrl+Shift+C), secure password generation via libpwquality, and a cleaned-up address bar that no longer shows raw URLs in search suggestions.

Software warns before installing end-of-life apps, lists more Flatpak permissions, and starts faster thanks to cached AppStream data and optimized icon loading.

Calendar went through its GListModel rework and is noticeably faster in Month view with large schedules. Event locations can be opened directly in Maps, Week view works with the high-contrast setting, and the event editor was cleaned up with better Microsoft Teams link support.

Sushi is now GTK4 and libadwaita. The file previewer got a full interface revamp, supports dark mode, displays images at real size, and uses the same modern loading and rendering libraries as the rest of GNOME.

Calculator remembers calculation history across restarts, shows the exponent in the current base, and does exact rational arithmetic via GMP.

Settings got a new fingerprint management interface in Users, an About panel with a button to open the release notes, an Accessibility setting to disable the focus timeout, an Auto Rotate row for devices with accelerometers, center-aligned display snapping, an option to disable the touchpad when a mouse is plugged in, DNS domain search, Wi-Fi sharing through the QR widget, “ConfigureShortcuts” in Global Shortcuts, reworked panel navigation, and stricter policies for systemd-homed accounts. WEP support is gone. Remote Login now supports SSH socket servers in addition to the service-based setup.

Orca 51 is nearly a release of its own: user plugins and extensions, MathCAT for MathML, announcing formatting changes while reading, language-specific voice sets activated by command, automatic sleep mode for chosen apps, configurable flat review, double-tapped Orca+F showing all font and formatting info in a window, and configurable speech inflection.

Nautilus opens locations from other apps in new tabs, has AdwTabOverview in narrow mode, moves search focus to the most relevant result, ignores duplicate entries in the app chooser, and gives the Projects bookmark its own symbolic icon.

Remote Desktop supports smartcard redirection and Kerberos multi-user remote login. Connections handles H.264 encoding in Flatpak builds, captions in app screenshots, and IPv6 URIs.

GNOME Circle gained three new apps: Bobby for browsing SQLite databases, Tally for simple counting, and Bazaar, a new app store focused on discovering and installing apps and add-ons from Flatpak remotes.

Initial Setup supports systemd-homed accounts and got error indications plus accessibility states for enterprise accounts.

What left the platform

Removed modules: gcr-3, gnome-keyring, evince (Papers replaces it), and gtksourceview-4. Together with oo7-portal from the API section, the direction for secret storage is clear: the oo7 stack. Distros can still package these themselves, but they are no longer part of the GNOME platform.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • Nautilus: faster view reloading, blocking IO pushed off the main thread, no duplicated loading locations.
  • Software: faster icon loading and PackageKit repository refinement.
  • System Monitor: reworked cgroups performance.
  • tinysparql: faster ICU full-text tokenizer; localsearch refactored code shared between processes.
  • GtkSourceView: faster context engine and search context.
  • Shell screencasts minimize stage paints and buffer copies.
  • GLib: the GNetworkMonitor netlink backend behaves like iproute2 and pulls the route table less often.
  • libdex: reworked work stealing in the thread pool; idle workers sleep instead of scanning peers, and work distributes better.
  • GTK: GPU cache scaling limits, text view caches pixel height, motion history is always collected for input prediction.
  • Sysprof: libsysprof-capture optimizations.
  • glycin: fixed a deadlock when consumers exhausted the GTask thread pool by blocking on the sync API. libglycin now uses sync GIO operations when the sync API is used. Also fixed mmap of write-sealed memfds on Linux < 6.7.

Visual polish

New wallpaper set. The default is “Roundhex” (shape interest in the top right corner, tweaked from feedback), joined by “Glass Stripes” and “Curvaturingster” in the chooser.

Shell uses its own sound effects instead of the sound theme, animates app grid label expansion nicer, supports touch scrolling in ScrollView and start/end text alignment, exposes the slow-down-factor in looking glass, lights the audio-input icon only during actual recording, and the session/a11y menus at the login screen respond to both mouse buttons.

Maps moved settings from menus into the preferences dialog, larger place-name fonts in the sidebar match the new pill buttons, transit itineraries show walking durations, going-to animations are skipped over large distances, and tombs have a fresh icon.

Nautilus widened the sidebar limit, shows an empty “Document” entry when the templates directory is empty, uses AdwComboRow for the open-action preference, hides the redundant “Open Parent Folder” row, puts the symlink emblem before read-only/unreadable ones, and badges the selection count while dragging files.

Control Center merged all panel CSS into one stylesheet, adopted clang-format globally, moved the About copy button to AdwButtonRow, modernized the Wacom button-mapping dialog, and hides the auto DNS/route toggles in Manual mode.

libadwaita 1.10 adds AdwSidebarItem :prefix and AdwSidebarSection :suffix, animates the title on the About dialog main page, and fixes adaptive preview issues.

Developer tools

Foundry 1.2.0 runs GitLab CI locally in Podman (includes, rules, stages, needs, artifacts), adds public CI and Git API abstractions, ships foundry ci list/run/shell/clean, bindable amend support, commit templates, and help generated from the command tree. Debugger fixes include better DAP thread, stop, continue, and stack-frame state tracking, plus regression tests.

Builder 50.0 shipped. blueprint-compiler 0.22.2. Vala 0.56.19 with gdbus and vala fixes plus updated bindings. gtk-doc 1.36.1.

Epiphany, Nautilus, PyGObject, and GTK all adopted the gobject-linter CI job at scale. Sushi’s plugin API was overhauled with a system-wide plugin path and documentation. GJS makes GNOME objects more transparent to the garbage collector for accurate Sysprof memory stats.

Content and smaller apps

adwaita-fonts 51.0, Papers 51.0, Simple Scan 50.0, Music 50.0, and Decibels 49.6.1 (PipeWire stream metadata, MPRIS SetPosition/OpenUri fixes). Rygel 46.0 added Reciva devices to the seek hack and fixed a crash on address family mismatch. gdk-pixbuf 2.44.8 brings glycin x-/y-dpi support for PNG, TIFF, and JPEG.

glycin 2.2.1 fixed mmap of write-sealed memfds on older kernels. gnome-user-docs updated GNOME Help.

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, input

Mutter: blurred rendering on non-pixel-aligned monitors, invalid redraw clips on rotated monitors, shader snippets reapplied correctly after resize and scale, unsupported fallback monitor modes no longer offered, wrong stacking order changes on workspace switches, fullscreening edge-tiled windows, alt-tab under sloppy/mouse focus, DND data offers on touch, tablet DND across surfaces, broken switch-monitor mapping on stylus buttons, unfullscreening maximized windows correctly, OSK triggering for text_input_v3 v1 clients, preferred_scale events delivered to clients, cursor position hints for Xwayland under scaling, tablet cursor hotspot scaling, moving maximized windows between monitors by keyboard, window size increases after fast unmaximize drags, plus a run of crash fixes (Mutter MR 5143, Mutter MR 5153, Mutter MR 5151, Mutter MR 5163, Mutter MR 5169, Mutter MR 5170).

Shell: a glitch when switching to a minimized window on another workspace, mis-scaled magnified cursors on HiDPI, sound glitches from redundant volume changes, wiggle feedback on non-password auth failures, the spinner resetting on every keystroke in overview search, layout reapplication on xkb-options changes, the “Install Updates” checkbox in the power dialog, autorun notifications for USB drives, spacing in lock screen media notifications, workspaces disappearing mid-animation, removing arbitrary providers when unregistering search providers, one memory leak, and a glitch with direct scanout on workspace switches.

GTK: the X11 selection clipboard burned excessive CPU (GTK issue 6493), animated SVGs frequently disappeared (GTK issue 8195), type-to-search broke in Epiphany dialogs (GTK issue 8291), GLArea leaked memory on unrealize, GtkPicture dispose left a dangling paintable, tooltips blocked on X11, a frame clock idle deadlock from counter underflow, munmap() of the wrong pointer in the dmabuf format table, CSS text-decoration needing a resize to apply (a regression), application menu items with multiple shortcuts showing none, Super/Hyper no longer counting as text modifiers, AT-SPI using the cache before it was ready (GTK issue 7879), GtkListView missing items (GTK issue 8137), macOS re-entrant GMainContext stale poll array (GTK issue 8263), a macOS memory leak when unfocusing with an open popup (GTK issue 8343), GtkColumnView sortable headers exposing no AT-SPI action (GTK issue 8354), and media queries not respected (GTK issue 8382).

Login and sessions

GDM: Plymouth never quit on headless or monitor-less systems, so the machine never reached graphical.target; X11 sessions started with XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland; kernel VT cursor flicker when logging out; checks that PAM plugins do not drop fsuid privileges and break GDM; PAM modules notified when the user switches right before exec’ing the session leader; autologin bypass where a compromised greeter could request arbitrary usernames; PAM substack safety net so authentication cannot be bypassed; double-free in session worker; path traversal vulnerability where a compromised greeter could load arbitrary .desktop files via SelectSession; and input sanitation when forwarding unknown usernames to the audit subsystem.

gnome-session had a regression in screen blanking and idle handling, fixed in beta. gnome-settings-daemon: Housekeeping failed to launch Baobab, one use-after-free, and power temporary-unidle now cooperates with inhibitors.

Apps

Calendar: sporadically missing horizontal separators in month view, the event editor not saving duration changes, a week view crash with multiple overlapping events, a tooltip on an invisible overflow button, rare crash on Month view scrolling, inverted Ctrl+Scroll zoom direction in Week view.

Nautilus: correct starred status and properties behavior in Recents, right-clicking the view background no longer clears the selection, manual selections survive file operation results, copied files get selected after the operation finishes, Escape closes the app chooser while the entry is focused, thumbnails update during loading, loading getting stuck while thumbnailing in Flatpak, the “Window is ready” notification firing when other apps call “Open location”, timed dialogs destroyed before their timeout, and a memory leak in create-links-in-place.

Epiphany: colons in app-mode URLs converted to “A”, crashes on invalid view-source: URIs, a memory leak in ephy_string_shorten(), an out-of-bounds assert in the JSON helper, duplicate password entries when editing usernames, crashes deleting password records, crashes after adding OpenSearch engines, a preferences crash after deleting the default search engine, a memory-corruption fix-of-fix in web-view, CVE-2026-18487 (address bar host spoofing via userinfo), CVE-2026-77682 (autofill JS code injection via CSS selector), CVE-2026-77679 (WebExtension XPI path traversal ZIPSLIP), and XSS/HTML injection in the error page.

Connections: authentication dialog focus chain, cursor change propagation, IPv6 URI connections, NULL Common Name handling in RDP, and no longer storing already-stored connections. Initial Setup: a crash when the SSID got freed on the network page.

System Monitor: summary units in the process table, translatable disk read/write rate units, duplicate icon text in preferences. Calculator reports an invalid name entry to the accessibility layer. gexiv2 crashed opening files without preview images.

at-spi2-core: a crash in get_registered_event_listeners, grab id 0 assignments, wrongly deregistered event listeners, NULL dereferences when sending events, and detection of unresponsive applications. libatspi gained a Ready signal on the cache, ATSPI_STATE_DEFAULT alias, and main-loop reentrancy control.

GtkSourceView: the file loader rejects non-regular files, bounds expanded/decompressed input size, fails loads cleanly, plugs gutter and gutter-line leaks, breaks a circular reference with line numbers enabled, and fixes Vim emulation for repeated commands.

Orca: table presentation including Chrome’s history table, aria-busy respected, no percent value on indeterminate widgets, false-positive flat review resets in terminals, color-chooser button names, item counts in list boxes, and set_current_voice() persistence.

yelp fixed an issue that allowed remote access to local files (49.1, security relevant). zenity’s --hide-header actually hides the header now.

Security

GLib’s GDBusServer suffered a pre-authentication DoS through unbounded SASL line buffering (GLib issue 3985, CVE-2026-16118 for the heap overflow). Several out-of-bounds reads were fixed in GRegex, GMarkup, GDateTime, GIOChannel, GDBus, and GKeyFile. GDesktopAppInfo now validates desktop file path snippets (GLib issue 4003).

Evolution Data Server got a hardening series: a shell command injection fix in NTLM SASL, ENVID sanitization against SMTP command injection, POP3 rejecting CRLF-bearing credentials (command injection), CardDAV validating photo/logo URI origins against SSRF, a MIME nesting depth limit against stack exhaustion, HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects rejected, and OAuth2 state parameters against CSRF.

gvfs hardened input validation across afp/dav/ftp/mtp/sftp backends, wipes passwords from memory before freeing them, and fixed crashes in the OneDrive, MTP, and SMB backends. glycin switched its sandbox seccomp policy from an allowlist to a blocklist. Epiphany quotes command-line input before passing it to the shell (Epiphany MR 2094) and carries the CVE fixes above.

glib-networking fixed out-of-bounds reads in the OpenSSL backend (CVE-2025-60018, CVE-2026-2574) and an infinite loop in certification path building (CVE-2026-10028).

GDM: path traversal vulnerability where a compromised greeter could load arbitrary .desktop files; autologin bypass where a compromised greeter could request arbitrary usernames; denial of service where an invalid session name caused the daemon to exit; ASLR leak in D-Bus object path generation; and PAM passphrase handling now wipes cached plaintext passwords.

Libraries and build

GLib: an fd leak in g_file_set_contents_full(), a crash on gio help help, a GDBusActionGroupClass failure, Windows UNC paths in the spawn helper, and a purge of G_GNUC_CONST from _get_type() functions across the stack (GCC 17 risked miscompiling those).

libsoup HTTP/2: the content sniffer running while paused, failed messages requeued when a connection is not reusable, buffered bodies consumed before cancel, and reads limited to received content. Pango: CoreText variations and font features, overline/underline/strikethrough staying in sync, undefined-behavior fixes.

Evolution Data Server: LDAP Simple Paged Results (RFC 2696), IMAP4 Multimailbox SEARCH, junk folder unread counting, recurring task due-date reset, camel-lock-helper symlink handling, a deadlock with m365 GOA accounts, a pile of memory leak fixes, and gb2313 mapped to gb18030. gtk+-3, yelp, and tecla carried maintenance and build fixes.

Known regressions and deferred work

Sushi shows only the first frame of animated GIFs, and LibreOffice documents render as PDFs because the old method is incompatible with the GTK4 port. GTK deferred session save/restore to 4.26. Boxes missed the 51 train (Disks made it). GDM keeps PreSession/PostSession hook scripts removed; the decision from the 50.x series stands.

Sources

Official gnome-build-meta NEWS with complete per-module changelogs: 51.0 and the earlier 51.alpha and 51.beta. Release announcement on GNOME Discourse and the official GNOME 51 release notes. Phoronix coverage of the final release and custom pointer acceleration profiles.

item.title: Flatpak 1.19: what actually changed
item.description: Flatpak 1.19 ships as a beta development release, dominated by nine security fixes and a polkit-authenticated path for system-wide downgrades.
item.content:encoded:
Flatpak 1.19.0 was released August 11 as a development/beta release (the final 1.19 is not yet timed). The headline is security-driven: nine CVEs were resolved, ranging from a full sandbox escape to integer overflows, and the system helper gained polkit-authenticated downgrades so administrators no longer need root to downgrade system apps.

This is a beta. Nine security fixes and the bug-fix batch are already published; the new features are landed and stable API-wise, but the release is not yet declared stable.

Things worth your attention

Security

Flatpak 1.19 resolves nine security advisories. A representative subset:

  • Sandbox escape with full host filesystem read/write via symlink attack on app data directories ([GHSA-8688-9x26-hhxj]).
  • Local root privilege escalation via revokefs symlink path traversal and commit tampering ([GHSA-qrwq-7qwx-q9rp]).
  • Arbitrary root write via symlink and path traversal in extra-data extraction ([GHSA-fqx6-vh4p-42cg]).
  • Arbitrary root write via path traversal in flatpak build-init ([GHSA-8qxj-x646-phcm]).
  • Arbitrary host file read via hardlink path traversal in OCI archive extraction ([GHSA-9rww-v4mm-x4jg]).
  • Path traversal via unvalidated architecture parameter in DeployAppstream ([GHSA-v2gw-v9h5-9q4x]).
  • Buffer overflow in OCI delta stream path names on 32-bit systems ([GHSA-jr92-2v97-wgvc]).
  • Fixed-filename writes to arbitrary locations via symlink attack on .ld.so ([GHSA-99wv-m8rp-g58x]).
  • Extension metadata path traversal allowing host filesystem probing ([GHSA-w69g-9x8j-7p8f]).
  • Anti-downgrade bypass allowing unprivileged users to downgrade system apps ([GHSA-q4gr-vc25-57m5]).

All of these affect distributors and system administrators who package or deploy Flatpak at scale. End users benefit automatically once their distro updates the flatpak package, but the downgrade bypass is particularly worth flagging: it was exploitable by any local unprivileged user on multi-user systems.

Downgrades authenticated via polkit

The system helper can now perform system-wide downgrades authenticated through new polkit actions instead of requiring root (Flatpak issue 6669). This replaces the previous behavior where downgrading a system-installed app needed root privileges. Who it affects: distribution integrators, fleet managers, and developers who need to pin or roll back system apps without granting full root access.

Coredump inspection

Added flatpak-coredumpctl list subcommand alongside Bash completion for flatpak-coredumpctl (Flatpak issue 6705, Flatpak issue 6678, Flatpak issue 6677). Developers debugging application crashes inside sandboxes can now enumerate coredumps without leaving the flatpak tooling.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • Added flatpak_transaction_progress_get_bytes_per_second() to the library API (Flatpak issue 6679), so tooling can display real-time download/progress rates.
  • The session helper’s runtime directory is now locked to prevent systemd-tmpfiles from cleaning the p11-kit socket (Flatpak issue 6754).
  • OCI signatures are now checked from the mirrored repo in the system helper rather than fetched from the lookaside server (Flatpak issue 6682), improving reliability in air-gapped or offline-mirror setups.
  • Translation updates shipped for pt_BR (Flatpak issue 6701, Flatpak issue 6751), sl (Flatpak issue 6726), sv (Flatpak issue 6750), uk (Flatpak issue 6715), and zh_CN (Flatpak issue 6748).

Developer tools

  • Bash completion cleanup (Flatpak issue 6710) makes the shell hints consistent across install/update/override subcommands.

Bug fixes

Sandbox, build, and portal integration

  • Fixed the portal flatpak-spawn environment handling regression (Flatpak issue 6721).
  • --assumeyes no longer sets no_interaction, so credential and polkit prompts still work (Flatpak issue 6744).
  • The inverted behavior of --clear-env is corrected (Flatpak issue 6722).
  • Negated permission strings for allow and share run options now parse correctly (Flatpak issue 6684, Flatpak issue 6687).
  • File forwarding of empty paths now errors out instead of silently misbehaving (Flatpak issue 6693).
  • Build failure when exporting metainfo releases.xml files is resolved (Flatpak issue 6698).
