  • Crashes in the portal update monitor (Flatpak issue 6692) and OCI JSON handling (Flatpak issue 6704) are fixed.
  • The GI annotation for flatpak_instance_get_all is corrected (Flatpak issue 6696).
  • TLS certs are now applied to OCI registry requests, and stream write failures propagate to curl (Flatpak issue 6685).

System helper hardening

  • Remote names are validated, supplementary groups are dropped, and credentials are no longer logged (Flatpak issue 6722, Flatpak issue 6724).
  • Numerous crash, memory leak, integer overflow, and error-handling fixes across the system helper and core (Flatpak issue 6722, Flatpak issue 6724, Flatpak issue 6723, Flatpak issue 6713, Flatpak issue 6725).

Known regressions and deferred work

None published yet.

Still in flight

This is 1.19, the development branch. No stable tag has shipped yet (the Flatpak maintainers release a new odd-numbered series roughly yearly, so 1.19 follows the same cadence as past development cycles). A 1.18.x point release line for the stable 1.18 series runs in parallel; the next stable minor (1.20) has not yet entered development. What is missing: the final 1.19.0 stable tag, and any further point releases for 1.18.x that the maintenance branch will accumulate before 1.20 begins.

Sources

Official release notes on GitHub: Flatpak 1.19.0. Coverage on Phoronix: Flatpak 1.19 Released With Nine Security Fixes. The co-released stable point release 1.18.1 carries the same security fixes for the stable series.

item.title: Pantheon 8.1: what actually changed
item.description: Elementary OS 8.1 ships with the Secure Session as default, a blur-behind Dock, background-app management, new Monitor and Maps apps, and over 1,100 fixed issues.
item.content:encoded:
Pantheon 8.1 is a stable release shipping as elementary OS 8.1, based on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with Linux 6.14 and Mesa 25. This is the release that finally makes the Wayland-based Secure Session the default, adds the blur-behind visual effect to the Dock and notifications, brings system monitoring and mapping to the default app set, and closes over 1,100 issues from the community since the OS 8 launch in November 2025.

Things worth your attention

Desktop and window management

The Secure Session is now the default session type. In OS 8 it was an optional Wayland session; after a year of fixes from third-party app developers and hardware vendors including Nvidia, the team reports that it “provides a much better experience for most people and supports a broader range of modern hardware features.” Users who prefer the old session can still select the X11-based Classic Session at the login screen.

Authentication dialogs in the Secure Session now dim the rest of the screen and block other windows from stealing focus when opened, so you can be sure you are typing your password into a genuine system dialog and not a spoofed prompt.

The Dock gained background-app support through the Background Portal. You can see a list of apps running without a window, read their stated reason for running, and force them to quit. Workspace switching moved into the Dock itself: press the “+” tile to open a new workspace, click an existing one to switch, click one that is already open to jump straight into the Multitasking View, or drag apps into the Multitasking View from the Dock. The Dock also appears when you open the Multitasking View, and a new Pressure Reveal makes it easier to select app controls at the bottom of the screen without accidentally revealing the Dock. A shake animation fires when you middle-click an app that already has a single window open.

The window manager gained a new Gesture Controller that enables multi-touch features, including swiping up in the Multitasking View to close windows and a long-press gesture for context menus in more places like the Dock. Hotcorners now work even when an app is fullscreen, and the Applications Menu hotcorner is shown only in its corresponding panel corner: top-left for left-to-right readers, top-right for right-to-left.

Visual effects and design

OS 8.1 adds a blur-behind effect for translucent desktop elements including the Dock, Notifications, and the Alt+Tab window switcher, giving those panels visual separation from the applications behind them while keeping text legible. Notifications have rounder corners, and their close animation now matches the associated swipe gesture. Picture-in-Picture windows also have rounded corners.

Focus indicators now appear only when navigating with the keyboard and disappear when using a mouse or touch, removing a persistent visual artifact for pointer users while keeping accessibility intact. The new Reduce Motion setting covers a wider range of animations across the desktop and apps, with smooth multi-touch gestures preserved.

Folder icons were redesigned to be rounder and match the Files app icon more closely. Mouse icons gained a scroll wheel detail, and pointer icons were updated to match. The system falls back to Adwaita icons when an app uses a non-standard icon name.

New default apps: Monitor and Maps

Two new default apps shipped with OS 8.1. Monitor is a system-resource and process viewer with live graphs and an optional panel indicator for passive checking. Maps covers the basics — explore, transit maps, location search, and geo:// link support that integrates with Calendar for event locations.

Privacy and security

AppArmor profiles ship with this release that resolve Flatpak sandbox issues, notably for Steam and apps running in a Guest session. In System Settings → Applications you can now directly deny an app access to notification bubbles alongside other permissions. System Settings can configure its own notifications, and stale notifications from apps like Terminal are withdrawn when no longer relevant. Screenshot notifications open Image Viewer when clicked and offer to show the image in Files.

Apps

Music now saves and restores the play queue and last-played track across sessions, lets you remove individual tracks via context menus or clear the whole queue, searches the queue by track name, and shows album artwork in the panel media controls. Performance for large queues improved.

Files supports the admin:// URI protocol for administrator access, the New file submenu respects the Templates folder hierarchy, and Properties windows show more precise date and time with a new format setting in the main menu.

Code can clone repositories from the sidebar projects menu, switch to remote git branches with a warning about uncommitted changes, and the Symbols sidebar shows more detail for Vala and C symbols in tooltips. Edit marks can be placed in the source-view gutter and jumped between with Alt+←/→.

Terminal adopted the modern tab bar widget shared with Web, Files, and Code, with an option to hide the tab bar when there is only one tab. Paste protection expanded to cover authentication commands like doas, commands with skip-confirmation flags (-y, –interactive=never, –force), and multi-line command detection. A new option lets you disable paste protection entirely.

GNOME Web 48.3 ships with improved performance, web compatibility, and a redesigned bookmarks sidebar.

Accessibility

The installer and Onboarding were reworked for keyboard and screen reader use after feedback from Florian, a blind cybersecurity tester who returned for a second round of accessibility testing. The “Before Installing”, “Try or Install”, “Choose a Disk”, and Encryption views have improved accessible labels, password-quality feedback is read aloud, and text-style markup is no longer announced unexpectedly. OS 8.1 can now be installed and set up completely blind in most cases.

Notifications and the Shortcut Overlay both got screen-reader support. Calendar main menu, calendar source addition, and the event dialog have improved labels. Firmware updates navigation was rewritten with better screen reader support. The Lock Screen auto-selects the Classic session when accessibility features that do not yet work in the Secure Session are in use, and media keys work on the Lock Screen. Main menus are properly marked and can be opened with F10.

Smaller changes

Visual polish

Dark Mode schedule snoozing lets you manually toggle Dark Mode on or off while using a timed or sunset-to-sunrise schedule without canceling the schedule — it resumes on the next schedule change. Dark Mode screenshots and brand colors appear in AppCenter when available, and the Lock Screen follows your Dark Mode settings. The Bluetooth settings panel was redesigned to separate nearby and paired devices visually, with improved keyboard navigation and screen reader experience. Duplicate devices in the list were fixed, and pairing requests requiring passcodes now work more reliably.

In Network settings, you can now choose whether a network auto-connects when available and whether to reduce background data usage. Middle-clicking a networking toggle in the panel jumps to System Settings. The Power menu shows the device model when available and avoids an empty battery icon, and Power settings now warn about increased energy usage with certain options.

Settings pages with sidebars remember their adjusted width. “About this device” works as a search term in the System page. Panel transparency, orientation lock, and power settings now sync to the Lock Screen.

Performance and internals

The long-term support Hardware Enablement stack from Ubuntu brings Linux 6.14 and Mesa 25, with improved performance while gaming or moving files, reduced power consumption for some AMD and Intel chipsets and GPUs, and new security features. Support was added for Intel Lunar Lake processors and for more webcams, USB network devices, joysticks, gamepads, Wi-Fi devices, and microphones.

For the first time, ARM64 builds are offered for UEFI-booting devices, including Apple Silicon machines and devices that load UEFI-supporting firmware like the Raspberry Pi. The underlying Linux also supports certain Qualcomm and Rockchip processors.

Fractional display scaling now works in the Secure Session, addressing a common complaint about integer-only scaling in OS 8 that left HiDPI-non-pixel-dense displays awkwardly sized. Multi-monitor issues were resolved, including problems when monitor layouts changed or during drag-and-drop. The Installer is now always re-centered on screen, fixing issues when the layout changes while it loads, including in some virtual machines.

Buttons that previously appeared only on hover (in Calendar’s main menu and the Multitasking View) now show all the time, making them discoverable on touch. Wacom stylus detection was improved to prevent a crash when no stylus is found, and the middle-click paste option was fixed in Secure sessions.

The updates system was rewritten: it no longer runs in Demo Mode, checks once daily instead of on every login, and does not automatically download on metered connections, sending a notification instead. AppCenter updates are sorted by release date, the Releases dialog was redesigned, and the “Last checked” time updates every minute while the updates view is open. System updates show the download size beforehand and a progress bar, skip held-back phased packages, and can be reached directly from the Dock, Applications Menu, or search.

Developer tools and platform

Gala 8.6.0 and 8.6.1 shipped alongside OS 8.1 with improvements to the classic session, a new on-screen keyboard for the secure session, screenshotting that includes open menus, and touchscreen swiping up from the bottom to open the Multitasking View. The flatpak-platform repository bumped the GNOME runtime to 49 and then to 50, updated Granite to 7.8.1, and updated the stylesheet to 8.2.2. The icons repository released 9.0.0 with updated symbolic icons for GTK 4.22 across devices, apps, status, emblems, and categories, plus Inkscape-related icon additions.

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, input

The new Gesture Controller and Gesture Manager in Gala fixed several multi-touch and window-management edge cases. Stylus detection in Wacom settings no longer crashes when no stylus is found. Middle-click paste now works in Secure sessions. The Lock Screen no longer freezes when connecting Bluetooth devices, and Airplane Mode now correctly disables only networking radios rather than Bluetooth or wired networks.

Login and sessions

The session-switching issues between Classic and Secure sessions were resolved, so apps that failed to start correctly when switching sessions now launch properly. The Installer’s custom install mode no longer closes unexpectedly for users with complex partitioning schemes, and the corner cases were tracked down with new regression tests added. The Installer is always re-centered on screen, including when the layout changes during loading.

Apps

AppCenter now shows percentage-based ratings from ODRS for Flathub apps, displays elementary-specific screenshots when developers provide them for multiple platforms, indicates controller support for games, shows in-app purchase labels, and supports application add-ons. The action button for free apps now reads “Install” instead of “Free”, and search results show in two columns when space permits. App icons fall back to a nicer placeholder when loading is slow and cross-fade in once ready, and icons reload on the fly as their data is processed.

Calendar received improved screen reader labels and touch-screen support. Terminal’s paste protection now warns when a single paste contains multiple alarming elements and detects commands with newlines better. System Settings warns if a custom keyboard shortcut conflicts with a common system shortcut like Copy, Paste, or New Tab.

Security

New AppArmor profiles resolve Flatpak sandbox issues that affected Steam and Guest sessions. Screen filters are no longer captured in screenshots. The notification system properly denies app access and withdraws stale notifications.

Libraries and build

Gala 8.6.1 fixed a frequent crash when using the classic session. The flatpak-platform and icons repositories updated their translation templates, build tooling, and dependencies, with the platform moving to Docker build-action version 7 and Ubuntu 24.04 runners.

Known regressions and deferred work

The Secure Session does not yet support the onscreen keyboard, so System Settings shows a message when you try to turn it on and directs you to the Classic session instead. Some apps that have not yet updated to Wayland may still require the Classic session. The multi-monitor and fractional scaling improvements are specific to the Secure Session; behavior in the Classic Session remains unchanged from OS 8.0.

Sources

Official elementary blog post: elementary OS 8.1 Available Now. Release listings on elementary Releases, including gala 8.6.0 and 8.6.1, terminal 8.1.0, flatpak-platform 9.0.0, and icons 9.0.0. Detailed feature coverage from OMG! Ubuntu, Debugpoint, and Position is Everything.

item.title: COSMIC Epoch 1.8.0: what actually changed since 1.7.0
item.description: System76 tagged a coordinated submodule bump centered on a major cosmic-comp compositor overhaul. Tablet emulation, libei pasteboard sharing, rounded window corners, and multi-factor PAM login are the headliners, plus a raft of fixes across applets, files, and the greeter.
item.content:encoded:
As of September 9 2026, COSMIC Epoch 1.8.0 is tagged. Epoch releases are not traditional feature drops — they are coordinated snapshots pinning twenty-plus independently developed submodules to a single, tested commit. Pop!_OS gets these changes through its internal pipeline; the epoch tag gives Arch, Fedora, NixOS, and other distros a reliable pin point. The diff between 1.7.0 and 1.8.0 is one epoch commit e7bc6be) that bumps every submodule; the real story lives in those submodule diffs.

Things worth your attention

Compositor and Wayland protocols

The heavy lifting happened in cosmic-comp, the Wayland compositor. Nearly fifty files were touched, with the tiling layout grab handlers receiving a full rewrite for more accurate resize behavior. Three new protocol handlers landed:

  • tablet emulation (tablet_emu.rs, 256 new lines): drawing tablets now get proper input routing at the compositor level. Pressure, tilt, and rotation are exposed through the ei_stylus interface via libei. Krita and other stylus-aware apps should now register pen input correctly.
  • libei pasteboard sharing: copy text in an X11 app and paste it into a Wayland one without a clipboard daemon throwing a fit. The libei.rs module wires up the pasteboard protocol so copy/paste crosses the XWayland boundary cleanly.
  • cornerRadius protocol (src/wayland/protocols/corner_radius.rs): finally allows rounded window borders. The handler lives in src/wayland/handlers/corner_radius.rs; themes and apps can now request corner radii without hacks.
  • pointer-warp-v1 (src/wayland/handlers/pointer_warp.rs): cross-window cursor syncing for remote-desktop and gaming use cases.
  • keyboard-layout-unstable-v1 (src/wayland/handlers/keyboard_layout.rs): proper layout switching at the compositor level, replacing the previous config-file workaround.

XWayland received fractional-scaling border fixes. KMS/DRM cleanup got more robust error handling. The shadow rendering module was quietly stripped out as dead code. Input handling modules grew from roughly 105 net lines to 332, reflecting a complete overhaul of pointer warping and grab state management.

Who it affects: users with drawing tablets, anyone copying between X11 and Wayland apps, theme authors wanting rounded corners, remote-desktop users, and anyone on fractional-scaling setups.

Bluetooth, audio, and system tray fixes

Outside the compositor, the changes are quieter but immediately noticeable:

  • Bluetooth applet (cosmic-applets/cosmic-applet-bluetooth/src/bluetooth.rs): now displays device alias names instead of raw MAC addresses. The Settings panel lets you rename paired devices directly without digging into the command line.
  • Audio source volume slider (same applet): a long-standing bug finally got fixed — the slider now actually adjusts the input device instead of silently rewriting the output volume.
  • Network manager applet: bumped its Rust client to nmrs 3.5.2, smoothing compatibility with newer NetworkManager releases.
  • System tray icons: stopped rendering downsampled when scaled below 1:1, fixing the persistent fuzzy-icon issue in smaller panels.

Who it affects: Bluetooth headphone/speaker users, anyone adjusting microphone volume, multi-monitor setups with mixed DPI panels.

File manager and settings polish

  • cosmic-files: the rubber-band selection no longer redraws incorrectly when you drag it. Tab focus behavior now correctly stays put when you close a different tab. The search drawer in Settings preserves your scroll position instead of resetting to the top of every section.
  • cosmic-launcher: switched to a standard build.rs, added its first official CI pipeline for clippy and formatting, and stopped leaking environment variables into downstream builds.
  • cosmic-greeter: finally chains sequential PAM prompts, which fixes login failures for users running dual-factor setups (e.g., password + YubiKey, or password + TOTP). It also ships full Nix flake packaging now.

Who it affects: file-manager power users, NixOS users, anyone with multi-factor authentication.

Localization and new modules

  • Initial setup wizard picked up Filipino and Hungarian translation coverage.
  • cosmic-sound-theme and cosmic-screenshot modules were added to the repository structure for the first time (still early, not fully baked).
  • The logind feature gate now compiles cleanly when building without systemd dependencies, removing a long-standing pain point for non-systemd distributions.
  • Weblate pushed a massive localization sweep across fifteen languages (Czech to Traditional Chinese).

Who it affects: non-English users, non-systemd distro packagers, anyone waiting on a native screenshot tool or system sound theme.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

  • Tiling layout grab handlers rewritten for more accurate resize behavior (fewer visual glitches when dragging window edges).
  • Input subsystem overhaul: pointer warping and grab state management consolidated, reducing latency spikes during rapid window operations.
  • KMS/DRM error paths hardened; compositor recovers more gracefully from display hotplug races.
  • Build system hygiene: logind feature gate no longer forces systemd at compile time.

Visual polish

  • System tray icons render crisp at sub-1x scaling (no more fuzzy Bluetooth/battery icons in compact panels).
  • New printer queue icon and refreshed browser icon in cosmic-icons.
  • Rounded window borders now possible via the cornerRadius protocol (theme support required; not yet exposed in Settings).

Developer tools and packaging

  • cosmic-launcher gained a standard build.rs and CI pipeline (clippy + fmt).
  • Full Nix flake packaging for the greeter.
  • Environment variable leakage in launcher builds plugged.
  • cosmic-applibrary and cosmic-store received version bumps and dependency updates only.

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, input

  • Tablet input now registers in stylus-aware apps (Krita, GIMP) — previously only pointer movement worked.
  • X11 ↔ Wayland copy/paste works without a clipboard daemon.
  • Fractional-scaling borders on XWayland clients no longer show gaps or double borders.
  • Pointer warping no longer snaps cursor to (0,0) intermittently (fixes relative mouse input in games).
  • Shadow rendering dead code removed, eliminating a minor memory leak path.
  • Keyboard layout switching at the compositor level now works without editing xkb_config manually.

Login and sessions

  • Greeter PAM chaining: sequential prompts (password → second factor) no longer deadlock or drop the second factor.
  • NixOS users can now install the greeter via flake without patching.

Apps and applets

  • Bluetooth device list shows human-readable aliases; renaming works from Settings.
  • Microphone volume slider adjusts the correct stream (input, not output).
  • System tray icons stay sharp at all panel sizes.
  • File manager rubber-band selection no longer flickers/redraws incorrectly.
  • Tab focus preserved when closing background tabs.
  • Settings search drawer remembers scroll position.

Libraries and build

  • logind feature gate compiles without systemd.
  • nmrs bumped to 3.5.2 for NetworkManager compatibility.
  • Various Cargo.lock and dependency updates across all submodules.

Known regressions and deferred work

  • cosmic-sound-theme and cosmic-screenshot are present in the repo but not yet functional — treat as preview only.
  • Rounded window corners require theme support; no Settings UI to toggle them yet.
  • Tablet emulation covers pressure/tilt/rotation; advanced stylus features (e.g., eraser end, barrel buttons) not yet mapped.
  • The unified changelog for end users is still absent; you have to read submodule diffs to know what actually shipped versus what just compiled.

Sources

Official epoch tag on GitHub: epoch-1.8.0 and the submodule bump commit e7bc6be. Submodule comparisons: cosmic-comp, cosmic-applets, cosmic-files, cosmic-greeter, cosmic-settings, cosmic-launcher, xdg-desktop-portal-cosmic. LinuxCompatible coverage of the epoch tag. System76 blog COSMIC DE tag for historical context.

item.title: KDE Plasma 6.8 Beta: what actually changed since Plasma 6.7
item.description: The first beta is out, feature freeze started September 10, and the final release lands October 14. Here is everything noteworthy, everything minor, and the bug fixes worth knowing about, sorted into sections you can actually read.
item.content:encoded:
As of September 10, 2026, Plasma 6.8 Beta 1 (versioned 6.7.90) is out. The final release is due October 14, coinciding with KDE’s 30th anniversary. The hard feature freeze and soft UI/string freeze took effect at this beta, so this covers practically the whole release: fixes and translations will still land before the final, new features will not. Beta 2 arrives September 24.

Things worth your attention

Window management and compositor

KWin now applies shadows, rounded corners, and outlines to client-side-decorated (CSD) windows that lack their own decoration — think Steam, Discord, and Electron apps. This is handled by a new Breeze decoration option called “shadow-only decorations” (KWin MR 583, KDE bug 504225). The effect is consistent across the desktop and works on Wayland.

Triple buffering is now enabled by default on NVIDIA GPUs. The bugs that blocked this in the past have been fixed, so NVIDIA users should see smoother rendering and lower latency (KWin MR 9472).

KWin internally uses only OpenGL ES now. The proprietary NVIDIA driver and older GPUs required this path anyway, and it turns out to be sufficient for everything KWin needs. Vulkan will replace it in a future release (KWin MR 9488).

Multi-GPU systems with external GPUs get a significant performance boost — up to 80% in some scenarios — because KWin now handles GPU selection more intelligently (zamundaaa.github.io write-up, July 2026).

HDR support expanded: KWin now supports the HLG transfer function in addition to PQ (KDE bug 508817). ICC profile handling for HDR content improved (KDE bug 524038).

KWin’s screenshot and screen-casting paths got faster and smoother on high-refresh-rate displays (KWin MR 9756, KDE bug 524129). Screen-casting latency dropped by one frame across the board, including the built-in RDP server (KPipeWire MR 274).

The Overview effect is slightly easier to trigger with a four-finger swipe gesture (KWin MR 9486).

Audio recording in Spectacle

Spectacle can now record audio during screen recordings. You can choose system audio (what the computer plays), microphone audio, or both (KDE bug 474798). This was the most-requested missing feature for screen recording and finally lands in 6.8.

Remote desktop improvements

KRDP, Plasma’s built-in RDP server, now supports bi-directional clipboard syncing (KRDP MR 213). Previously only the server’s clipboard was shared one-way to the client.

The RDP server can now dynamically adjust its quality level to match available network bandwidth, keeping frame rates consistent (KRDP MR 238).

Remote desktop sessions persist correctly across disconnects, and the System Tray icon for a severed connection now disappears as expected (KRDP MR 234).

A notification now appears when a pre-authorized app starts remote-controlling the system (KDE bug 571).

Lock screen and authentication

The lock screen got a significant overhaul. You can now select which authentication method to use when multiple are available (password, fingerprint, etc.), and the button alignment is improved across languages (Plasma Desktop MR 3689, Plasma Workspace MR 6542, KScreenLocker MR 318, Plasma Desktop MR 3951).

Lock screen notifications now trigger for all GPUs, not just the primary one (KWin MR 9768).

Auto-login works in Plasma Login Manager on distros with older systemd versions like KDE neon (KDE bug 522006).

System Settings search in English

When using the system in a non-English language, you can now search for System Settings pages using English keywords in KRunner and Kickoff, not just the local language (System Settings MR 418). For example, searching “mouse” finds “Souris” on a French system.

Wallpaper and theming

The default wallpaper changed from Waterfall to Hanabi (Breeze commit 0b1e6ce).

SVG-based wallpapers now fully participate in the automatic dark/light wallpaper switching feature (KDE bug 519168).

Wallpaper slideshows can be configured to not change automatically — you switch manually via the desktop context menu or a global shortcut (KDE bug 518669).

If all wallpaper plugins are broken, missing, or misconfigured, Plasma now launches with a plain background instead of failing to start (KDE bug 524875).

Union, KDE’s new CSS-based theming system, gained initial support for styling QtWidgets apps (Union MR 270). This is a tech preview — visual glitches are expected and known. Dolphin and other QtWidgets apps can now be themed through Union, unifying theming across QtQuick and QtWidgets apps.

Breeze styling for GTK4 apps’ menus and window borders improved (Breeze GTK MR 104).

Dark GTK2 theme detection improved, so old GTK2 apps get legible icons more reliably when using a dark color theme (Breeze MR 144).

System Monitor upgrades

System Monitor can now measure VRAM usage as a percentage of total VRAM, not just absolute bytes (KSystemStats MR 135). This mirrors how RAM usage is displayed.

You can set CPU affinity for processes — pin a process to specific cores or core groups (KSystemStats MR 420). This is a power-user feature for fine-tuned workload placement.

The Process Table view shows fractional axis values when needed, and the tree view has better text alignment (KDE bug 521041, KDE bug 442095).

System Monitor graphs request tabular (monospaced) numerals for legends when the font supports them, improving alignment (KQuickCharts MR 109).

Notifications and clipboard

Notifications now slide in from off-screen instead of fading in, with a more natural easing curve (KDE bug 522276). The sliding animation was refined after its initial introduction.

When you copy text marked as a secret (like a password), the clipboard history UI now shows a clear warning instead of hiding the entry and leaving you wondering why nothing appeared (KDE bug 508326).

The screen recording indicator only appears while recording is actually in progress, fixing cases where apps opened sessions early but started recording later (Portal MR 597).

The “Bouncing app icon” launch feedback animation uses a better physics model, easing curve, and higher frame rate (KWin MR 9487).

Input and accessibility

The Emoji Selector updated to Unicode 17, adding new emoji like 🫨 🫪 🐦‍🔥 🏴‍☠️ (KDE bug 3849). The emoji grid now has resize controls (Plasma Addons MR 3878).

Press-and-hold for alternative characters now triggers after 600 ms instead of 200 ms, making accidental activation much harder (KDE bug 157).

Dwell clicker support landed for accessibility on Wayland — you can click by hovering without pressing a physical button (Phoronix coverage).

Stylus interaction works in Overview and Custom Tiling overlays on Wayland (KDE bug 468396, KDE bug 522677).

System tray icons that open widgets now stay visible until the widget popup closes, so you can click a second time to dismiss it (KDE bug 521115).

Network and connectivity

Connecting to an enterprise Wi-Fi network for the first time takes you directly to the credential entry page (Plasma NM MR 635).

Wireless access points can be configured to automatically select a channel in the Networks System Settings page.

Bluetooth widget’s “Configure” button moved to the standard position for consistency (KDE bug 516134).

StrongSwan VPN support added EAP-TTLS authentication (Plasma NM MR 636).

Flatpak version of Microsoft Edge is now supported in Plasma Browser Integration (KDE bug 521109).

Performance and resource usage

Discover’s background notifier process uses much less memory when checking for updates (KDE bug 509180).

Plasma startup is slightly faster by avoiding unnecessary work when loading wallpapers (Plasma Workspace MR 6898).

SVG caching improved in Frameworks 6.30, increasing speed and reducing video memory usage (KDE bug 115).

Spectacle dropped the OpenCV dependency; blur effects are now implemented without it (Spectacle MR 561, KQuickImageEditor MR 53).

Thumbnail rendering in notifications and the Activities sidebar uses fewer resources (Plasma Workspace MR 6966, Plasma Desktop MR 3967). The Trash widget also uses less memory (Plasma Desktop MR 3965).

Disabling a System Tray widget frees its memory immediately, not just after restart (Plasma Workspace MR 6983).

The clipboard’s “Keep selection and clipboard the same” setting no longer breaks multi-cell copying in LibreOffice Calc (KDE bug 505209) and no longer unnecessarily disables other settings (KDE bug 492840).

Calendar and clock

Digital Clock widget text for calendar events is now fully selectable (KDE bug 433668).

Digital Clock requests tabular numerals, preventing width changes as time passes (Plasma Workspace MR 6797).

The Digital Clock tooltip expands to fit long text instead of overflowing (KDE bug 6950).

Drawing tablet and input devices

The Drawing Tablet settings page has a less awkward dialog for configuring pen button mappings (KDE bug 524720).

Amharic virtual keyboard layout added (Plasma Keyboard MR 118).

System Settings and configuration

You can disable autostart entries without deleting them (Plasma Workspace MR 6951).

The Remote Desktop System Settings page works on small/narrow window sizes like phones (KRDP MR 208).

Non-default settings highlighting works on the Remote Desktop page (KRDP MR 232) and the Plasma Search page (Plasma Desktop MR 3973).

The “Report a Bug in the Current Page” feature works for pages that list a bug reporting URL even if they didn’t come from KDE (System Settings MR 412).

KWin prevents setting a resolution so low you’d break your system and be unable to recover (KWin MR 9765).

Removed: X11 session

Plasma 6.8 drops the X11 session entirely — Wayland is now the only session. X11 applications still run via Xwayland. The X11 session will be supported by KDE into early 2027 through Plasma 6.7 bugfix releases. This is the biggest architectural change in Plasma’s 30-year history (announcement blog post, Nov 2025).

Smaller changes

Visual polish

  • Comboboxes in Plasma now use the active theme for their popups instead of hardcoded Breeze styling, and menu highlights no longer animate (Libplasma MR 1547, Libplasma MR 1550).
  • In-window dialogs in Kirigami apps are better highlighted against window content in dark themes (KDE bug 447965).
  • Audio Volume widget popup starts large enough to fit all content without scrolling (KDE bug 522654).
  • Cursor feedback effects dodge screen edges so they’re always fully visible (KDE bug 498068).
  • Menu Editor has fewer visual frames (Menu Editor MR 59).
  • “CD and DVD” category in Discover renamed to “Disc Burning” to match the FreeDesktop spec (Discover MR 1350).
  • Breeze icon theme adds icons for Android app bundle files (KDE bug 508430) and Typst documents (KDE bug 554).
  • System Tray crash icons: only one sad-face icon appears when many crashes occur; clicking it shows the full list (KDE bug 420443).

Developer tools and internals

  • showConfigurationInterface() now works in Plasma scripting (Plasma Workspace MR 6977).
  • System Settings Proxy page rewritten in QML for Plasma Mobile compatibility (kio-extras MR 536).
  • KGlobalAccel internals refactored: dropped X11 bits, normalized shortcut formats, improved lookups (multiple MRs).
  • Kirigami tab bars respond to scroll and standard tab-switching shortcuts (Kirigami MR 2123).
  • Frameworks 6.30 requires Qt 6.11 and KDE Frameworks 6.30 (version bumps across all modules).

Content and smaller apps

  • Ethiopian calendar (13-month) added to alternate calendars (Plasma Addons MR 1079).
  • Nepali (Bikram Sambat) and Ethiopian calendars supported in Plasma Addons (Addons commit 1445c41, Addons commit 076c13a).
  • Vietnamese lunar calendar shows text in Vietnamese regardless of system language (KDE bug 521787).
  • Time zone offset calculations fixed for half-hour offsets earlier than local time (KDE bug 522037).
  • Calendar widget no longer changes displayed date when dragged between screens (KDE bug 472360).
  • Weather widget centers location label, improves badge positioning, uses EnvCan icon codes, and fixes layout issues (multiple MRs).
  • Color Picker widget sizing fixes (KDE bug 522377, KDE bug 517052).
  • KDE Connect SMS app permissions page ported to new Forms (flatpak-kcm commit 1c4d978).
  • KWallet stops spamming logs in non-default configurations (KDE bug 524500).

Performance and technical

  • KWin’s “press and hold for alternative characters” implementation prioritizes app compatibility, fixing many bugs (KDE bug 152).
  • Spectacle no longer includes tooltip with image dimensions in final screenshot when accepting region by double-click (KDE bug 513715).
  • Mic tester records at system sample rate instead of forcing 44.1 kHz (KDE bug 523693).
  • Emulated Input protocol version 1.6 supported (KWin MR 9112).
  • KWin variable refresh rate crash on multi-monitor setups fixed (KDE bug 521909).
  • Full-screen video playback performance improved in Chromium-based apps (KDE bug 521960).
  • KWin no longer leaks CAP_SYS_NICE to child processes, fixing Bubblewrap sandboxing (KDE bug 521013).
  • XWayland apps behave correctly after XWayland crashes and restarts (KWindowSystem MR 220).
  • Task Manager hardened against maliciously-crafted .desktop files (Plasma Workspace MR 6817).
  • ksystemstats_intel_helper hardened against path traversal (KDE bug 141).

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, and input

  • Fixed most common Plasma crash (multi-screen related) (KDE bug 500044).
  • Fixed second-most-common crash on logout (Plasma Workspace MR 6973).
  • KWin crash on lock screen with NVIDIA GPU fixed (KDE bug 520842).
  • KWin crash with DisplayLink monitors fixed (KDE bug 520361).
  • Screens on hybrid NVIDIA/AMD laptops no longer freeze (KDE bug 521727).
  • Shader-based KWin effects (Burn My Windows) restored (KDE bug 521774).
  • Color-related effects (color blindness correction, screen inversion) restored (KDE bug 521737).
  • Corrupted visuals on rotated screens and older AMD GPUs fixed (KDE bug 521878, KDE bug 521764).
  • SDR content desaturation in HDR mode fixed (KDE bug 521759).
  • ICC profile color correctness fixed (KDE bug 522301).
  • KWin lag/hang with poorly-optimized Proton games fixed (KDE bug 522005).
  • Pointer movement in VMs with non-accelerated graphics fixed (KDE bug 524280).
  • Screens incorrectly notifying disconnect/reconnect loop after sleep fixed (KDE bug 521826).
  • Drag-and-drop of desktop files/folders between screens restored (KDE bug 521713).
  • Variable refresh rate crash on multi-monitor setups fixed (KDE bug 521909).
  • Right-to-left languages no longer prevent force-quitting processes in System Monitor (KDE bug 522233).

Login and sessions

  • Screen locker security issue fixed: manual config to turn off screen after “don’t require password” period no longer fails to lock (KDE bug 523504).
  • Auto-login works on older systemd versions (KDE bug 522006).
  • Logout sound no longer delays logout more than necessary (KDE bug 491745).
  • Wallpaper slideshows now remember last-seen wallpaper instead of restarting from first (KDE bug 512559).
  • Activity deletion no longer crashes Plasma; switches to next activity instead (KDE bug 521124).
  • System Monitor no longer crashes when quitting with column config dialog open (KDE bug 491000).
  • DrKonqi crash handler no longer crashes in a loop on severely broken systems (KDE bug 524048).

Apps

  • Discover no longer gets stuck checking for updates when Snap backend present but no upgradeable Snaps (KDE bug 524077).
  • Discover terminates all processes properly on quit (Discover MR 1393).
  • Discover remembers review usefulness ratings and doesn’t let you resubmit (KDE bug 521866).
  • Discover only offers .deb packages on distros that support them (Plasma Desktop MR 3957).
  • Discover fixes: updates stuck when fwupd unavailable (KDE bug 521682), Snap backend signals completion correctly (KDE bug 524077), AppStream preview backend added (Discover commit 4a02b82), package review usefulness persistent (KDE bug 521866).
  • Non-KDE apps no longer crash when closing a dialog (KDE bug 523039).
  • Calendar widget no longer shows info buttons for alerts that do nothing (KDE bug 519676).
  • Weather widget info buttons only appear when functional (KDE bug 519676, Addons commit d13f147).
  • Color Picker widget layout regressions fixed (KDE bug 522377).
  • System Monitor Configure Columns popup is now a traditional window, fixing scroll glitch (KDE bug 517723).
  • Networks widget: connecting to uneditable network no longer makes others look connected (KDE bug 461028).
  • Audio Volume widget shows correct panel icon under unusual conditions (KDE bug 422).
  • Remote desktop connection icon disappears correctly after unexpected disconnect (KDE bug 234).
  • RDP server systemd regression fixed (KDE bug 521776).
  • Chromium apps no longer freeze when another window forced “Keep Above Others” (KDE bug 521687).
  • Plasma no longer crashes after ejecting audio CD from Dolphin/Audex (KDE bug 522051).
  • Kickoff/Kicker: multiple widgets can all return search results for not-yet-installed apps (KDE bug 511220).
  • System Settings sub-category sidebar switching fixed in less-common interaction modes (KDE bug 415).
  • Digital Clock “Today” button highlights correct day in time zones later than UTC (KDE bug 521114).
  • Screencast permission no longer requires identical screen setup to when permission granted (KDE bug 519122).
  • Portal dialog explanatory text shows correctly (KDE bug 584).
  • Icons-Only Task Manager no longer breaks from metadata.desktop in home folder (KDE bug 521247).
  • Weather widget no longer endlessly reloads after wake from sleep (KDE bug 517280).
  • System Monitor graphs show fractional axis values (KDE bug 521041).
  • Un-favoriting apps with weird characters works (KDE bug 520894).
  • Notification icon no longer gets stuck half-rotated (KDE bug 458156).
  • Screen Locking page translated label no longer reverts to English after save (KDE bug 521293).
  • Color Picker widget no longer overflows in Grouping widget (KDE bug 517052).
  • Media Frame widget no longer displays every other image sharpened (KDE bug 521534).
  • Choose Application window no longer percent-encodes filename characters (KDE bug 521748).
  • Mouse page in System Settings no longer has layout glitches in X11 (KDE bug 521992).
  • Networks widget Details tab text no longer overflows (KDE bug 522333).
  • KRunner Bookmarks provider returns results for 2-char queries, uses fewer resources (KDE bug 6764).
  • Clipboard widget Actions Configuration page margins improved (KDE bug 6779).
  • Secret keyboard shortcut (Meta+Ctrl+x) for clipboard actions removed (KDE bug 6773).
  • DrKonqi tells you when safe to close window (KDE bug 397).
  • Kameleon system service disabled by default (KDE bug 521793).
  • Pointer with software rendering no longer disappears when panel dodges windows (KDE bug 521953).
  • Force-quitting processes in System Monitor works with RTL languages (KDE bug 522233).

Security

  • Task Manager hardened against malicious .desktop files (Plasma Workspace MR 6817).
  • ksystemstats_intel_helper hardened against path traversal (KDE bug 141).
  • Screen locker locking logic fixed for edge-case configuration (KDE bug 523504).
  • Flatpak background service crash fixed when allowing app update via KDE portal (KDE bug 6686).
  • KWin no longer leaks CAP_SYS_NICE to child processes (KDE bug 521013).

Libraries and build

  • Qt version requirement bumped to 6.11 across all Plasma modules.
  • KDE Frameworks requirement bumped to 6.30 across all Plasma modules.
  • KGlobalAccel dropped X11 code paths, normalized shortcut handling.
  • KWin split into kwin_wayland and kwin_x11 (from 6.4) — X11 bits now fully removed.
  • Multiple modules ported to KConfigXT, QML modules, and modern CMake patterns.

Known regressions and deferred work

  • Union theming for QtWidgets apps has known visual glitches (acknowledged in announcement).
  • Location-based timezone setting deferred; depends on Date & Time KCM QML conversion (Plasma Desktop MR 3653).
  • Some accessibility features from third-party apps may not work as well on Wayland-only session.
  • Output mirroring issues being actively worked on.
  • Session restore and window position memory still being improved.

Sources

Official KDE announcement for Plasma 6.8 Beta: 6.7.90. Complete changelog from 6.7.5 to 6.7.90: changelog. KDE Community Wiki page for Plasma 6.8 features: Plasma 6.8. Phoronix coverage of Plasma 6.8 performance optimizations: August 21 and triple buffering. 9to5Linux preview of Plasma 6.8: October 14 release. “This Week in Plasma” blog posts covering the 6.8 development cycle: Audio Recording in Spectacle, Better Animations, UI and Performance Improvements, QtWidgets Apps Join the Union, Post-6.7 Bug-fixing, and Going all-in on a Wayland future. New In Linux feature summary: Plasma 6.8 features.

item.title: KDE Plasma 6.7.5: the September bugfix update
item.description: Released September 8, 2026, this is the fifth maintenance update in the Plasma 6.7 series. It brings a month of translation updates and targeted fixes across KWin, Discover, the Task Manager, and system daemons.
item.content:encoded:
KDE Plasma 6.7.5 landed on September 8, 2026, one month after 6.7.4. This is a pure bugfix and translation update — no new features — and it is the last planned point release before Plasma 6.8 arrives on October 14 with its Wayland-only session. The next 6.7.x update would be 6.7.6 in November, but the project has indicated 6.7 will be supported longer to bridge the gap to the 6.8 series.

Things worth your attention

KWin and Wayland

HDR output with ICC profiles now renders more accurately. A series of commits in the OpenGL ICC shader and DRM backend (fixing KDE bug 524038) handle multiplier values, fall back from BToA1 to BToA0 when needed, and validate the color profile source before applying it. Users with HDR displays and custom ICC profiles should see correct colors where they previously did not.

KWin adds support for more than one wl_data_device (MR linked to KDE bug 521494). This improves drag-and-drop between Firefox and other Wayland clients that rely on multiple data devices. The change is in the Wayland backend and does not require application updates.

The Eye On Screen effect had a broken return animation (KDE bug 481100) and horizontal wheel scrolling in the offscreen Quick view — both fixed.

The Tabbox (Alt+Tab switcher) gained horizontal scrolling support and a corrected scroll direction (KDE bug 522229). It also closes when the activation modifier is released, matching the behavior users expect.

A DRM syncobj kernel version check was corrected, and the global removal timer timeout for Wayland clients was increased to one day, which helps with long-lived surfaces.

KWin now avoids using render devices without hardware acceleration (fixing a regression that impaired pointer movement in VMs with non-accelerated graphics drivers). It also checks supported blend modes more carefully before setting them.

EDID parsing now handles hexadecimal strings in output names correctly (KDE bug 523181), so monitor identification in display settings stays reliable on affected hardware.

Input handling iterates over a copy when dispatching to filters and spies, and a use-after-free in the DPMS input event filter’s touch handling was fixed (KDE bug 523770). Warps are no longer counted as user activity for the screen locker (KDE bug 523504).

The internal input method context initializes cursor and anchor positions, and surrounding-text offsets are clamped when clients set them (bugs KDE bug 516195, KDE bug 517620). The wl_fixes v2 protocol is now disabled by default.

A file descriptor leak when starting the input method was plugged, and wl_data_device support for multiple devices improves Firefox drag-and-drop.

Discover package manager

Updates no longer get stuck when fwupd is unavailable or masked via systemd (KDE bug 521682). A regression that mistook an update for needsReboot was reverted. The Snap backend now signals completion of update checks even when zero upgradeable snaps exist (KDE bug 524077). Concurrent KJobs during quit are handled safely (bugs KDE bug 497419, KDE bug 522245, KDE bug 522815, KDE bug 518264). The rpm-ostree notifier crash is fixed, and null-pointer queries in the notifier are guarded (bugs in the rpm-ostree backend). The updates KCM text now reflects the selected update type correctly. Discover also only offers to open and install .deb packages on Debian-based distributions.

Plasma Desktop and widgets

The Task Manager (taskmanager applet) fixes several right-to-left issues: task progress bars now follow RTL layout, and tasks move to the expected location when manually rearranged by dragging (bugs KDE bug 504898, KDE bug 524112). Window thumbnails no longer disappear unexpectedly. The applet also requests a thumbnail when a window is ready for painting, improving the first thumbnail appearance.

Kicker no longer launches favorites twice when pressing Space, and the Emojier returns focus to the search field on Arrow Up. The Emojier window is now large enough for its sidebar (KDE bug 523090). Kicker also disables category dragging and fixes the highlight while dragging. The desktop containment respects the type-ahead setting in widgets (KDE bug 523053). Panel tooltips strip mnemonics (KDE bug 488578). A scripting API reorderApplets() is exposed for panel applet reordering (KDE bug 523675). The wallpaper-provided accent color is no longer overwritten (KDE bug 514656). The landing page KCM fixes color bleed at corners (KDE bug 522042). Spell Checking no longer prompts to apply settings when no backend or dictionary exists (KDE bug 521712).

The Calendar widget no longer changes the displayed date when dragged between screens (KDE bug 472360). The digital clock fixes tooltip overflow, centers time zones, and compares agenda dates across time zones (bugs KDE bug 524390, KDE bug 501555, KDE bug 442100).

The Plasma Login Manager (SDDM KCM) now also syncs ~/.config/plasma-localerc, so the login screen respects your preferred language and time settings (improvement KDE bug 516964).

System Settings and KCMs

Multiple System Settings pages now correctly implement the “highlight changed settings” feature. The Spell Checking KCM no longer erroneously prompts to save unsaved changes when navigating away without making any (KDE bug 521712). The Night Light KCM adds the missing non-default highlight (KDE bug 521974). The System Settings module loader fixes a parent reset issue for modules without a submenu (bugs KDE bug 524340, KDE bug 514006).

Powerdevil clears stale battery warnings after charging, and the battery monitor applet omits the PPD message when there is no PPD. The Powerdevil KCM fixes a non-default highlight issue.

The KScreen KCM fixes the check for showing the calibration button (KDE bug 524507).

System daemons and background services

The KDE daemon (kded) no longer crashes while reading from or writing to the system password storage when network conditions change. A crash affecting non-KDE applications when closing a dialog is fixed. A common kded crash on Wi-Fi connection or hotspot creation is resolved.

DrKonqi stops processing crashes of its own binaries (KDE bug 524048) and ensures its launcher service does not participate in session management (KDE bug 524213), fixing a crash loop on some systems.

The activity manager (kactivitymanagerd) fixes a stats plugin crash with wrong D-Bus calls (KDE bug 524352) and uses contains instead of binary_search on unordered QSet.

KSystemStats fixes the i915 PMU path for discrete Intel GPUs (KDE bug 517334) and provides fallbacks for the OS version property (KDE bug 523727), improving the “OS Version” sensor in System Monitor widgets for KDE Linux and other non-traditional distributions.

Plasma Vault allows networking to be restored when an offline vault was not closed before shutdown (KDE bug 457680).

Plasma NetworkManager fixes duplicate delete/update jobs, missing secrets returned, and a crash with multiple secret requests (bugs KDE bug 521935 and related).

The xdg-desktop-portal-kde fixes a screencast stream leak when creation fails and releases all sessions when the portal frontend disappears (KDE bug 523515). It also guards against deleting an uninitialized DataControlManager.

Visual polish and theming

Breeze now uses font metrics to inset text only where it can spare the space (KDE bug 523118), improving text alignment in buttons and labels. The Breeze GTK theme detects dark GTK 2 themes better and applies a matching icon theme automatically.

The Union (Plasma style) adds styling for modal overlays behind dialogs (KDE bug 523141), makes NavigationTabBar and NavigationTabButton styling look more like upstream, sets default toolbar heights, disables Drawer animations when the animation speed multiplier is zero, uses the animation speed multiplier for StackView animations (KDE bug 522148), exposes the platform’s animationSpeedMultiplier on StyleHint, sets menu margins to zero (KDE bug 520831), and uses fill vertical alignment for delegate layouts.

Spectacle fixes the annotation options submenu overflowing off the top of the screen and a crash when the window under the pointer is destroyed during detection.

Bluedevil fixes the dialog translation for “Forget Device.”

Noteworthy bug fixes

Compositor and display: ICC profile handling for HDR (multiple commits, KDE bug 524038), EDID hex strings in output names (KDE bug 523181), DRM syncobj kernel check, render device hardware acceleration guard, blend mode validation, offscreen Quick view horizontal wheel scrolling, Eye On Screen return animation (KDE bug 481100).

Input and Wayland: Multiple wl_data_device support (KDE bug 521494), input method context initialization, surrounding-text offset clamping (bugs KDE bug 516195, KDE bug 517620), FD leak on input method start, filter/spy dispatch safety, DPMS touch use-after-free (KDE bug 523770), warp not counted as user activity for locker (KDE bug 523504), wl_fixes v2 disabled by default.

Window management: Tabbox horizontal scrolling and scroll direction (KDE bug 522229), Tabbox close on modifier release, window vertical pullback fix using width, custom tile null-pointer dereference, window placement for apps that resize immediately after launch (centered mode).

Task Manager and panels: RTL progress bars and drag reorder (bugs KDE bug 504898, KDE bug 524112), thumbnail disappearance, thumbnail request on window ready, Kicker double-launch on Space, Emojier Arrow Up focus and sidebar size (KDE bug 523090), category drag disabled, highlight while dragging fixed, desktop type-ahead (KDE bug 523053), panel tooltip mnemonics (KDE bug 488578), wallpaper accent color preservation (KDE bug 514656), landing page corner bleed (KDE bug 522042).

Calendar and clock: Calendar date change on cross-screen drag (KDE bug 472360), digital clock tooltip overflow and time zone centering (KDE bug 524390), agenda date comparison across time zones (KDE bug 442100), infinite list current day view, calendar view change on drag (KDE bug 472360).

System Settings: Highlight changed settings across multiple pages, Spell Checking false save prompt (KDE bug 521712), Night Light highlight (KDE bug 521974), module loader parent reset (bugs KDE bug 524340, KDE bug 514006).

Discover: fwupd unavailable/masked (KDE bug 521682), needsReboot regression, Snap zero-upgrade signal (KDE bug 524077), concurrent KJobs quit (bugs KDE bug 497419, KDE bug 522245, KDE bug 522815, KDE bug 518264), rpm-ostree notifier crash and null pointers, update type text, deb-only on deb distros.

Background daemons: kded password storage crash on network change, non-KDE app dialog close crash, kded Wi-Fi/hotspot crash, DrKonqi self-crash filtering (KDE bug 524048) and session management opt-out (KDE bug 524213), kactivitymanagerd stats plugin crash (KDE bug 524352).

Power and battery: Stale warning clear after charge, PPD message omission, KCM highlight.

Network: Plasma NM secret agent duplicate jobs, missing secrets, multi-request crash (KDE bug 521935).

Portals: xdg-desktop-portal-kde screencast stream leak, session release on frontend disappearance (KDE bug 523515), uninitialized DataControlManager guard.

Graphics and stats: i915 PMU for discrete Intel (KDE bug 517334), OS version fallback for KDE Linux (KDE bug 523727).

Vault: Network restore after unclean offline vault shutdown (KDE bug 457680).

Bluedevil: Forget Device dialog translation.

Spectacle: Annotation submenu overflow, window-under-pointer crash.

Known regressions and deferred work

None listed for this bugfix release. Plasma 6.7.6 is scheduled for November 3, 2026, but the project has signaled that the 6.7 series will be extended to cover the transition to the Wayland-only Plasma 6.8 release on October 14.

Sources

Official KDE announcement for Plasma 6.7.5 on kde.org. Complete per-component changelog from 6.7.4 to 6.7.5 on the KDE changelogs page. 9to5Linux coverage of the 6.7.5 release. KDE Plasma 6 schedule and the 6.8 dependency stack (Qt 6.11, Frameworks 6.30) on the Plasma 6 page.

item.title: GNOME 51 “A Coruña”: the release candidate
item.description: The 51.rc tarballs shipped the week of August 29, string freeze is in, and the stable 51.0 release lands September 16. Here is what the rc pulled in over the beta, what is already locked, and what is still being chased for the final.
item.content:encoded:
GNOME 51 has reached its release candidate. The 51.rc tarballs were due on August 29 before 23:59 UTC, and the build-meta tarball covers the same module set as the beta plus a small rc-only batch. String, UI, feature, and API/ABI freezes all started on August 1; the string freeze itself began August 22. GNOME 51.0 stable is scheduled for September 16, with 51.0 tarballs due September 12. Bug fixes and translations can still land before the final. Anything new that wants to ship has to clear a freeze-exception approval, and very little did.

This post covers what changed between the beta and the rc. The full set of changes from alpha through beta is already in the GNOME 51 alpha/beta write-up.

Things worth your attention

Graphics and the compositor

Mutter’s biggest rc addition is cross-GPU buffer scan-out support, which Tyler Schicke wired up (Mutter MR 5219). The compositor can now attempt to hand a buffer directly to the display controller when the buffer lives on a different GPU than the one driving the output, with an automatic test for the path. Hybrid laptops in particular should see less copying between the discrete and integrated GPUs. Michel Dänzer also added the primary GPU rendering path using FBOs (Mutter MR 4921) and throttles timelines that do not produce a frame every cycle (Mutter MR 5252). The background effect protocol that beta added now has a policy with sane defaults (blur radius 24, saturation 1.25, noise 0.015), and shells are free to override that policy (Mutter MR 5160).

Michel also fixed the hardware cursor for SVG themes (Mutter MR 5217), which had been broken since the alpha introduced SVG cursor support. Night Light now works on hardware that lacks a GAMMA_LUT (Mutter MR 5205), stylus eraser button configuration is hooked up (Mutter MR 4819), and direct scan-out works again for captures that do not have a DMA-BUF (Mutter MR 5276). The compositor also stopped requiring EDID to generate a device color profile (Mutter MR 4961), auto-rotates on phones without a tablet-mode switch (Mutter MR 4962), fixes a possible hang on external monitor hot-plug (Mutter MR 5255), stops desaturating SDR content in HDR mode (Mutter MR 5230), and stops reporting multiple monitors as primary (Mutter MR 5228). Crashes and leaks across input capture, the KMS path, and the input event handling also went out, plus a fix for offscreen effect glitches when a resource’s scale changes (Mutter MR 5233).

Shell switched background image loading and caching to Glycin, the Rust image loading library (GNOME Shell MR 4134), which means the same code path that Nautilus and the previewer use now serves Shell. Smoother workspace transitions when direct scan-out is active also went in (GNOME Shell MR 4320).

Login and sessions

GDM gained pre-authenticated remote displays for Kerberos single sign-on with gnome-remote-desktop. Follow-up fixes to the $GDM_AUTH_SESSION_ID environment variable, the redone PAM service loading logic, and the pam_gdm keyring buffer bounds check are also in. The greeter-side autologin bypass that beta fixed has follow-up hardening, and the Fedora PAM rules now prefer oo7 over gnome-keyring for secret storage.

gnome-session switched to D-Bus for looking up the logind graphical session, and downgraded logout inhibitors from strong to weak as a stop-gap for buggy third-party inhibitors. GDM’s enum of conflicting sessions over logind still picks up ThinLinc and TigerVNC sessions, and the headless local greeter toggle and KMSCON VT compatibility from beta are still in.

gnome-initial-setup zeroises the Kerberos password before freeing it, fixes a markup injection in the privacy policy URL, and fixes a potential command injection in the keyboard preview (!later-rc). It now requires accountsservice >= 26.12.8 for act_user_uses_homed, and the realm manager migration from GSimpleAsyncResult to GTask is finally done.

Apps

Epiphany shipped two security fixes that made it into the rc tarball: CVE-2026-77682, an autofill JavaScript injection via a crafted CSS selector (Epiphany issue 2921, Michael Catanzaro), and CVE-2026-77679, a path traversal in the WebExtension XPI installer (Epiphany issue 2922, Fernando Muñoz). Catanzaro also fixed an XSS or HTML injection in the error page (Epiphany issue 2903). On the UX side, the “Not Secure” label in the address bar no longer gets truncated and glued to the domain in translated locales (Epiphany issue 2938), the caret stops jumping to the start when you switch keyboard layout (Epiphany issue 2929), and Epiphany stops offering to save a password that it just autofilled itself after a CSV import (Epiphany issue 2940). The download path stops firing when the MIME type is missing or the HTTP response failed (Epiphany MR 2159), and the canary build no longer points to the wrong WebKitGTK bundle (Epiphany MR 2152).

Calendar went through a small Month-view polish run: events can now be dragged on top of other events, Ctrl+Tab from a focused event jumps focus to the month cell behind it, and Shift+Tab from a month cell jumps back to the first event in front of it. The inverted Ctrl+Scroll zoom direction in the Week view is fixed, the popover no longer shows outside the window when the left mouse button is released outside, and a rare crash in the Month view when scrolling is gone. Calendar also accepts iCalendar files with LF line breaks now, which RFC 5545 does not technically allow but real-world files use.

Sushi in 51.rc picked up F2 to rename, Del to trash, O to open the file in its default app, and P to play or pause audio and video. Videos now render on a dark background, and folders opened from the previewer reuse the currently previewed Nautilus window. The plugin API was reworked: markReady/markInitialized were renamed, markFailed is the explicit error path, and ResizePolicy.CUSTOM is gone in favor of ResizePolicy.SCALED. The text UI is now Blueprint, long filenames no longer make the window absurdly wide, animated images play through Glycin, and the HTML renderer no longer requires WebKit.

Maps switched its public-transit routing to v6 of the MOTIS /plan endpoint, refreshed highway shields from OpenStreetMap-Americana, and updated OpenStreetMap POI types. AppData screenshots were updated.

Loupe stopped asking to save an edited file that the user already cancelled, and “Save as…” no longer leaves unsaved-changes state hanging after the new file is written.

GNOME Characters gained Lao and Norwegian Bokmål, and a long translation batch including Slovak, Indonesian, and Cornish. gnome-clocks, gnome-console, gnome-system-monitor, gnome-software, gnome-calendar, and gnome-calculator each shipped translation updates; Connections shipped an rc.1 the day after rc to fix a Flatpak build. Characters and Clocks dropped a couple of G_GNUC_CONST decorations in _get_type functions as part of the broader GLib cleanup.

APIs, libraries, platform

GLib 2.89.4 is in rc. The big one for framework developers is improved nanosecond source timeouts (GLib issue 4012, GLib issue 4018, GLib issue 4025, work by Benjamin Otte), and gio/outputstream now uses a larger splice buffer that meaningfully improves stream splice throughput (GLib MR 5316, Christian Hergert). The Windows notification backend can finally react to notification icon clicks (GLib MR 5019). Security: CVE-2026-16118, a heap overflow in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() triggered by user-writable XDG data locations, is fixed, and GDesktopAppInfo now validates desktop file path snippets (GLib issue 4003, Philip Withnall).

GJS 1.89.90 has two backwards-incompatible cleanups. Gio.DBus.makeProxyWrapper() now returns a class expression and should be called with new; calling it as a function still works but prints a deprecation warning. The internal GJS_ALWAYS_INLINE macro from gjs/macros.h is now also deprecated for outsiders; do not depend on it. The Maps slow-routing fix is in (GJS MR 1104).

PyGObject 3.58.0 is the rc-stable release. Stable release means no surprises relative to 3.57.x, but a couple of new APIs landed in 3.57.1: GLib.Pid is now a number with a special close method (PyGObject MR 556), bytearray marshals to GBytes quickly (PyGObject MR 558), Gtk.Template accepts PathLike objects (PyGObject MR 555), GValue no longer crashes on NULL (PyGObject MR 559), and the destroy-notifier path got extra safety (PyGObject MR 560). The breaking change from beta, that GFile children are now reachable via the / operator, is in.

Glycin 2.2.beta.1 fixed a deadlock in libglycin’s sync API when consumers exhaust the GTask thread pool by spawning many g_task_run_in_thread() calls, which Nautilus, GNOME Shell, and gdk-pixbuf were doing. The sync API now uses sync GIO under the hood. There is also a workaround for a memory leak in gtk-rs (Glycin issue 314).

Pygobject’s Generic annotations on Async and the / operator on GFile from the beta write-up are still in, and safe GVDB writer for home directories on NFS from dconf is still part of the platform story.

What left the platform

Removed modules from the beta list are unchanged in rc: gcr-3, gnome-keyring, evince (Papers replaces it), and gtksourceview-4. The Fedora PAM rules prefer oo7 over gnome-keyring, and gnome-remote-desktop Kerberos auth is the path forward for smartcard and pre-authenticated sessions.

Smaller changes

Performance and internals

GNOME Shell limited parallel texture loading operations (GNOME Shell MR 4349) and tracks the magnifier mouse position without polling (GNOME Shell MR 4344). The frame clock work from the beta is unchanged in rc but Mutter’s timeline decoupling (Mutter MR 5157) and the new throttling (Mutter MR 5252) line up with it. libdex’s thread pool work-stealing rework is unchanged. Localsearch 3.12.rc avoids needlessly re-extracting files, and tinysparql 3.12.rc plugs memory leaks in the JSON-LD serializer and the SPARQL parser. Sysprof’s libsysprof-capture optimizations are unchanged from alpha.

Visual polish

GTK 4.23.4 added a setting for an accent color (GTK MR 10266, Matthias Clasen), a setting for the inspector frametime overlay (GTK MR 9982, Benjamin Otte), and gtkadjustment honors the reduced-motion setting (GTK MR 10251). The symbolic rendering path in GTK’s SVG code is now opt-in (GTK MR 10214) with tests (GTK MR 10215) and proper state handling (GTK MR 10275, GTK MR 10278). Vertical color scales with alpha work now (GTK MR 10253, GTK MR 10267). The new folder-projects-symbolic icon is in (GTK MR 10250, g.willems). The shortcutswindow can document clicks (GTK MR 10268).

GNOME Calendar Month-view polish was already covered above. Nautilus added Santali and added a shortcut to focus the file chooser filename entry, plus renaming, trashing, and folder-opening to the previewer. The app chooser uses the type-to-search pattern and only shows apps in one section, and the view’s clear-on-navigation delay is gone. adwaita-icon-theme picked up the XDG Projects folder icon (adwaita-icon-theme issue 219). Sushi’s video dark background, GTK’s folder-projects-symbolic, and Nautilus’s single-section app chooser are all small polish items that add up to a cleaner desktop.

Developer tools

GJS 1.89.90’s class-expression makeProxyWrapper() and the deprecated GJS_ALWAYS_INLINE macro are documented above. GTK 4.23.4 dropped a deprecated os.path.commonprefix() use in mkenums (GLib MR 5312). glibmm 2.89.1 exposes connect_ns() and connect_ns_once() on SignalTimeout, get_time_ns() on Source, property_is_remote() on ApplicationCommandLine, property_filename() on DesktopAppInfo, and peek(), lookup(), append_take() on UnixFDList (Kjell Ahlstedt). GLib’s installed service file no longer contains the build path (GLib issue 4011). Gio’s gio/tests/services regression is fixed.

xdg-desktop-portal-gnome cleaned up the Global Shortcuts portal, stopped using G_GNUC_CONST in _get_type functions, and fixed input-only Remote Desktop sessions.

Content and smaller apps

gnome-autoar 0.5.0 added zstd to the supported archive formats and removed the GTK module. adwaita-icon-theme 51.beta added the XDG Projects folder icon. gst-thumbnailers 1.1.0 updated dependencies. msgraph 0.3.5 falls back to /me/drive when /me/drives is denied. gnome-app-list 2026.08 refreshed the app list and fixed data fetching from GNOME GitLab. Rygel 46.rc only bumped gsettings-desktop-schemas for the Flatpak CI pipeline.

Bug fixes

Compositor, display, input

Mutter in rc fixed: the hardware cursor for SVG themes, multiple monitors being reported as primary, desaturated SDR content in HDR mode, hangs on external monitor hotplug, broken direct scan-out for captures without a DMA-BUF, modifier release stopping key repeat (Mutter MR 4974), drag icon coordinates not snapping to the pixel grid (Mutter MR 5212), offscreen effect glitches on resource scale changes, fallback resolution listing, software cursor overlay visibility, and stylus eraser button configuration. Auto-rotate on phones without a tablet-mode switch works. Night Light works on hardware that lacks a GAMMA_LUT. The compositor no longer requires EDID for a device color profile.

GNOME Shell in rc fixed: a glitch when switching workspaces with direct scan-out (GNOME Shell MR 4320), a glitch when cancelling the lock screen prompt with Esc (GNOME Shell MR 4326), a race condition that prevented the password prompt from showing (GNOME Shell MR 4336), the magnifier mouse position polling (GNOME Shell MR 4344), the busy cursor appearing when activating actions (GNOME Shell MR 4325), a race condition when enabling extensions (GNOME Shell MR 3640), wireless toggle blocking (GNOME Shell MR 4323), new-window action workspace handling (GNOME Shell MR 4071), the focus on the calendar app from reminder notifications (GNOME Shell MR 4327), and unlocking the screen after the screen time limit was hit (GNOME Shell MR 4321). The first menu item is now focused when opened via keyboard (GNOME Shell MR 4189).

GTK 4.23.4 fixed AT-SPI attempts to use /org/a11y/atspi/cache before it is ready in GTK 4 (GTK issue 7879), GtkListView missing items (GTK issue 8137), a SIGSEGV in text_input_preedit_hint() when using IBus Chewing in GTK 4 apps on Wayland (GTK issue 8334), and several macOS regressions around DnD and popovers. The cut/copy/delete virtual-cursor regression in GtkTextView is fixed (GTK issue 8351). The menu bar focus with F10 is corrected (GTK issue 8359), and GtkAccessibleTextInterface documentation matches its implementations (GTK issue 8360). Shortcut labels in menus now show regular keys instead of keypad ones (GTK issue 8367). Several SVG state-handling bugs in the renderer are fixed (GTK MR 10249, GTK MR 10275).

Login and sessions

GDM in rc fixed: a follow-up issue in $GDM_AUTH_SESSION_ID, follow-up fixes in the redone PAM service loading logic, and a keyring buffer bounds check in pam_gdm. The Fedora PAM rules now prefer oo7 over gnome-keyring. The autologin bypass from beta still has hardening follow-ups. PAM modules continue to be notified when the user switches right before exec’ing the session leader.

gnome-session in rc downgraded logout inhibitors from strong to weak to work around buggy third-party inhibitors, and switched the logind graphical session lookup to D-Bus.

gnome-initial-setup zeroises the Kerberos password before freeing it and fixes markup injection in the privacy policy URL and a potential command injection in the keyboard preview.

Apps

Epiphany 51.rc fixed: an invalid-bookmark import crash (Epiphany issue 2898), XSS or HTML injection in the error page (Epiphany issue 2903), autofill JavaScript injection via a CSS selector (Epiphany issue 2921, CVE-2026-77682), WebExtension XPI path traversal (Epiphany issue 2922, CVE-2026-77679), a link from another app opening in the fullscreen window during fullscreen video (Epiphany issue 2928), a caret jump when switching keyboard layout (Epiphany issue 2929), a truncated “Not Secure” label (Epiphany issue 2938), Epiphany offering to save a password it just autofilled (Epiphany issue 2940), missing MIME type or failed HTTP responses firing downloads (Epiphany MR 2159), and the canary build pointing at the wrong WebKitGTK bundle (Epiphany MR 2152). highlight.js bumped to 11.2.0 (Epiphany MR 2145).

Calendar 51.rc fixed: a rare Month-view crash on scroll, an inverted Ctrl+Scroll zoom direction in Week view, an event popover showing outside the window, and a tooltip on an invisible overflow button.

Nautilus 51.rc fixed: tab overview behavior with a single tab, an empty list state in the app chooser, only apps being shown in one section in the app chooser, a missing parent folder row when the properties dialog is detached, memory trimming on window closure, non-keypad shortcuts in menus, focus and selection when a file gets removed, the app closing when only property windows are left, and shortcut labels in menus showing keypad keys instead of regular ones.

Loupe 51.rc fixed: an “ask to save the image” flow that fired after the user cancelled the edit, and “Save as…” leaving unsaved-changes state hanging after the new file is written.

Sushi 51.rc fixed: animated image playback through Glycin, dialog re-attachment to Nautilus, errors from stopped or cancelled renderers, the HTML renderer working without WebKit, open-with portal dialogs, window resizing detection, the window resizing on opening, image renderer width/height ratio, scaling up small images, TIFF loading through Glycin rather than Papers, and long filenames making the window too wide.

Orca 51.rc added MathCAT 7.6-rc.3, added an Atspi version API to extensions, and gave assertive live regions higher priority in the event manager’s queue. Orca-controlled text selection is now behind a flag for app and browser developers to fix bugs against before v52 goes live with it. Several caret control bugs in non-web content are fixed, and some Say All line repetition in GTK4 text views is gone.

Connections 51.rc.1 fixed a Flatpak build, and 51.rc added a long translation batch.

Security

Epiphany shipped two CVEs in rc: CVE-2026-77682 (autofill JS injection via CSS selector, Epiphany issue 2921) and CVE-2026-77679 (WebExtension XPI path traversal via ZIPSLIP, Epiphany issue 2922). XSS or HTML injection in the error page (Epiphany issue 2903) is also fixed. GLib’s CVE-2026-16118, the heap overflow in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() from user-writable XDG data, is fixed (GLib issue 3992, Philip Withnall). GDesktopAppInfo validates desktop file path snippets (GLib issue 4003). gnome-initial-setup zeroises the Kerberos password before freeing it.

Libraries and build

GLib 2.89.4 fixed: a fd leak in g_file_set_contents_full() (already mentioned in beta), an installed service file containing the build path (GLib issue 4011), gio/tests/services regressions (GLib MR 5259, GLib MR 5267), the GLib test failures on RISC-V (GLib issue 4012), Hurd (GLib issue 3836, GLib issue 4019), FreeBSD (GLib issue 4023), and msys2-clang64 (GLib issue 4020). ASAN and TSAN data races in gobject and binding tests are fixed (GLib issue 3359, GLib issue 3695). A potentially quadratic-time regex was rewritten to be linear (GLib MR 5296). The G_GNUC_CONST purge from beta continued through GLib, glibmm, gtkmm, gvfs, and the rest of the stack. CVEs aside, GLib also added a CI job for UBSAN (GLib MR 5277).

GTK 4.23.4 enabled UBSAN in the sanitizers CI build (GTK MR 6178), moved its Fedora CI to F45 (GTK MR 10193), and fixed static linking on Windows (GTK MR 10243).

xdg-desktop-portal-gnome stopped using G_GNUC_CONST in _get_type functions.

Still in flight

What 51.0 will land with versus what was tagged in 51.rc is a short list. As of this writing, the 51.0 newstable tarballs are due September 12 and the release date is September 16, so anything still open at the rc has about ten days:

  • The “Boxes missed the 51 train” item from the beta write-up remains. Disks made it, Boxes did not, and there is no sign of a rebase before 51.0.
  • GTK session save and restore was deferred to 4.26 by the GTK team. Apps that depended on the GTK 3 session manager continue to need their own approach.
  • The gnome-control-center 51.rc.1 translation batch and dependency bump on gsettings-desktop-schemas to 51.beta are the last items there; the requests for rebinding global shortcuts on removal and the screen-reader launcher fix are stable.
  • Orca’s Orca-controlled text selection is behind a flag in 51.rc and will go live in v52. There is no expectation that it will flip in 51.0.
  • gst-thumbnailers 1.1.0 was the rc-stable tag, with only a dependency bump. No fixes are queued for 51.0 unless a regression is filed in the next ten days.
  • libshumate 1.7.rc has no changes since 1.7.beta, so the rc is effectively the final API for the 1.7 series.

Known regressions and deferred work

Sushi shows only the first frame of animated GIFs in some cases, and LibreOffice documents render as PDFs because the old rendering method is incompatible with the GTK4 port. The GTK team’s session save/restore is deferred to 4.26. Boxes missed the 51 train. The Sushi HTML renderer needs WebKit at runtime; without it, that renderer is unavailable. GDM keeps the PreSession and PostSession hook scripts removed; the decision from the 50.x series stands. The xdg_session_management_v1 protocol landed, but no major session manager besides GNOME Shell itself implements it yet, so practical use is limited to Mutter-aware compositors. Nautilus’s tab overview behavior with a single tab is fixed in rc, but AdwTabOverview in narrow mode is still narrower than the design intent.

Sources

Official gnome-build-meta NEWS with the rc module changelogs: 51.rc. GNOME Release Team announcement for the rc tarball due date on Discourse. Phoronix coverage of Mutter and Shell 51.rc, with the commit links to Mutter and Shell. The release calendar with the 51.0 newstable schedule is on release.gnome.org.

item.title: Arch Linux 2026.09.01: the September ISO in plain language
item.description: First Arch ISO to ship with Linux 7.2.2. GCC 16.2.1, glibc 2.44, Python 3.14.7, mkinitcpio 41.1, NVIDIA 610.57.04, COSMIC 1.7, and KDE Plasma 6.7.4 land in the same snapshot.
item.content:encoded:
Arch Linux’s monthly snapshot for September is out as 2026.09.01. As usual, the ISO itself only matters for fresh installs; existing systems get the same packages through pacman -Syu. The headline this month is that the installer now boots Linux 7.2.2, the first time a 7.2-series kernel ships in a monthly Arch ISO.
